title: The History of Herodotus, Vol. II (Books V-IX)
creator: Herodotus (George Campbell Macaulay, trans.)
description: Herodotus' Histories, Books V-IX, in G. C. Macaulay's 1890 translation — Vol. II of the complete Histories, covering the Persian Wars to their conclusion.

title: The Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus of Plato, Vol. I (Thomas Taylor, 1820)
creator: Proclus (Thomas Taylor, trans.)
description: Proclus' 5th-century commentary on Plato's Timaeus, Books I-III, in Thomas Taylor's 1820 English translation — the ancient Neoplatonic expansion of the Atlantis narrative. Vol. I of II.

title: The Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus of Plato, Vol. II (Thomas Taylor, 1820)
creator: Proclus (Thomas Taylor, trans.)
description: Proclus' 5th-century commentary on Plato's Timaeus, Books III-V, in Thomas Taylor's 1820 English translation. Vol. II of II.

title: History of the Peloponnesian War
creator: Thucydides (Richard Crawley, trans.)
description: Thucydides' complete History of the Peloponnesian War in Richard Crawley's 1876 translation — the foundational work of scientific historiography.

title: Pyramidographia: or, A Description of the Pyramids in Aegypt
creator: John Greaves
description: John Greaves' Pyramidographia (1646) — the first English book on the pyramids, reporting his 1638-39 measurements at Giza. Transcribed from the EEBO-TCP keyed text.

title: Operations Carried On at the Pyramids of Gizeh in 1837, Vol. I
creator: Howard Vyse
description: Vol. I (1840) of Howard Vyse's three-volume journal of his 1837 excavations at Giza — the great 19th-century pyramid survey, including the discovery of the relieving chambers.

title: Operations Carried On at the Pyramids of Gizeh in 1837, Vol. II
creator: Howard Vyse
description: Vol. II (1840) of Howard Vyse's journal of his 1837 Giza excavations, with appendices.

title: Operations Carried On at the Pyramids of Gizeh in 1837, Vol. III: Appendix
creator: Howard Vyse
description: Vol. III (1842, Appendix) of Vyse's Giza operations, containing J. S. Perring's survey of the pyramids at Abou Roash and southward, including the Faiyoum.

title: The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh
creator: W. M. Flinders Petrie
description: Flinders Petrie's 1883 scientific survey of the Giza pyramids and temples — the baseline of modern pyramid metrology. Transcribed from the Petrie Project transcript of the Cornell scan (raw OCR).

title: Our Inheritance in the Great Pyramid
creator: Charles Piazzi Smyth
description: Piazzi Smyth's Our Inheritance in the Great Pyramid (2nd enlarged ed., 1874; 1st ed. 1864) — the originator text of pyramidology, arguing the Great Pyramid encodes divine metrology. Included as the founding document of the pyramidology tradition.

title: Stonehenge, A Temple Restor'd to the British Druids
creator: William Stukeley
description: William Stukeley's 1740 Stonehenge — the founding text of British megalithic archaeology and the druidic interpretation of Stonehenge. Proofed transcription via sacred-texts.com.

title: Rude Stone Monuments in All Countries: Their Age and Uses
creator: James Fergusson
description: James Fergusson's 1872 worldwide survey of megalithic monuments — the first global comparative study of rude stone monuments.

title: Stonehenge and Other British Stone Monuments Astronomically Considered
creator: Norman Lockyer
description: Sir Norman Lockyer's 1906 work — the founding text of archaeoastronomy, arguing Stonehenge and other monuments were astronomically aligned. Transcription via sacred-texts.com.

title: The Lost Continent of Mu: The Motherland of Man
creator: James Churchward
description: James Churchward's The Lost Continent of Mu (1926, W. E. Rudge first edition) — the originator text of the Mu hypothesis of a sunken Pacific continent. Included as the founding document of the Mu tradition. (The 1931 edition's copyright was renewed; this is the 1926 text.)

title: The Problem of Atlantis
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Lewis Spence's The Problem of Atlantis (revised edition, 1925; 1st ed. 1924) — the major 1920s scholarly-popular synthesis of the Atlantis evidence from classics, geology, and folklore.

title: Queen Moo and the Egyptian Sphinx
creator: Augustus Le Plongeon
description: Augustus Le Plongeon's Queen Moo and the Egyptian Sphinx (1896) — the 19th-century Maya-Atlantis source text arguing a Maya-Egyptian connection and originating the name 'Mu'.

title: The Annals of Tacitus
creator: Tacitus (Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb, trans.)
description: Tacitus' Annals in the 1876 Church and Brodribb translation — the history of Rome from Tiberius to Nero. Books 7-10 are lost; the surviving Books 1-6 and 11-16 are given complete (Books 5, 11, 16 fragmentary as they survive). Transcribed from Wikisource.

title: The Histories of Tacitus
creator: Tacitus (W. Hamilton Fyfe, trans.)
description: Tacitus' Histories in W. Hamilton Fyfe's 1912 translation — the Year of the Four Emperors and the Flavian dynasty.

title: A Dialogue Concerning Oratory
creator: Tacitus (Arthur Murphy, trans.)
description: Tacitus' Dialogue on Oratory in Arthur Murphy's 1793 translation.

title: Germany and Agricola
creator: Tacitus (Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb, trans.)
description: Tacitus' Germania and Agricola in the Church and Brodribb translation — the ethnography of the Germanic tribes and the life of Agricola in Britain.

title: The Geography of Strabo, Vol. I (Books I-VII)
creator: Strabo (Hans Claude Hamilton and William Falconer, trans.)
description: Vol. I (Books I-VII) of Strabo's Geography in the Hamilton and Falconer translation (Bohn, 1854-57) — the complete ancient geography; Book XVII (in Vol. III) is the great ancient description of Egypt.

title: The Geography of Strabo, Vol. II (Books VIII-XIII)
creator: Strabo (Hans Claude Hamilton and William Falconer, trans.)
description: Vol. II (Books VIII-XIII) of Strabo's Geography in the Hamilton and Falconer translation.

title: The Geography of Strabo, Vol. III (Books XIV-XVII)
creator: Strabo (Hans Claude Hamilton and William Falconer, trans.)
description: Vol. III (Books XIV-XVII) of Strabo's Geography in the Hamilton and Falconer translation — including Book XVII on Egypt.

title: Stone-Heng Restored
creator: Inigo Jones
description: Inigo Jones' Stone-Heng Restored (1655) — the earliest English treatise on Stonehenge, arguing it was a Roman temple.

title: The Library of History of Diodorus the Sicilian, Vol. I (Books I-V)
creator: Diodorus Siculus (G. Booth, trans.)
description: Vol. I (Books I-V) of Diodorus Siculus' Library of History in G. Booth's 1814 English translation — including Book I on Egypt and the pyramids. Books VI-X are lost. Transcribed from sarata.com (raw text).

title: The Library of History of Diodorus the Sicilian, Vol. II (Books XI-XX)
creator: Diodorus Siculus (G. Booth, trans.)
description: Vol. II (Books XI-XX) of Diodorus Siculus' Library of History in G. Booth's 1814 English translation — the history of Greece, Sicily, and the successors of Alexander. Transcribed from sarata.com (raw text).

title: Steganographia
creator: Johannes Trithemius (1462-1516)
description: Trithemius's Steganographia (composed c. 1499; first printed Frankfurt, 1606) — the Renaissance root text of both cryptography and spirit-magic, read for centuries as a grimoire of angelic communication. Complete Latin text from the 1608 Frankfurt edition (BSB scan). No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae (text transcription)
creator: Heinrich Khunrath (1560-1605)
description: Khunrath's Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae (Hanau, 1609) — the great theosophical-alchemical emblem book of Christian Kabbalah and divine magic. Text portion transcribed (with German translation) from manuscript; the famous engraved plates are visual and not representable in text. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Utriusque Cosmi Historia, Tomus I, Tractatus I: De Macrocosmi Historia
creator: Robert Fludd (1574-1637)
description: Fludd's Utriusque Cosmi, vol. 1: the metaphysical, physical and technical history of the Macrocosm (Oppenheim, 1617). Complete Latin text; vol. 1 of the staged 4-volume Utriusque Cosmi set. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Utriusque Cosmi Historia, Tomus I, Tractatus II: De Naturae Simia
creator: Robert Fludd (1574-1637)
description: Fludd's Utriusque Cosmi, vol. 2: De Naturae Simia seu Technica Macrocosmi Historia (1624) — the 'ape of nature': technology, arts and machines as mirrors of the macrocosm. Complete Latin text.

title: Utriusque Cosmi Historia, Tomus Secundus: De Supernaturali, Naturali, Praeternaturali et Contranaturali Microcosmi Historia
creator: Robert Fludd (1574-1637)
description: Fludd's Utriusque Cosmi, vol. 3: Tomus Secundus (Oppenheim, 1619) — the history of the Microcosm (man). Complete Latin text. The later continuations (1621/1623/1626) were not found in full text; flagged for a future batch.

title: Utriusque Cosmi, Tomi Secundi Tractatus Primi, Sectio Secunda: De Technica Microcosmi Historia
creator: Robert Fludd (1574-1637)
description: Fludd's Utriusque Cosmi, vol. 4: Tomus Secundus, Tractatus I, Sectio II (1619) — the technical history of the microcosm, including De mentis humanae scientia. Complete Latin text.

title: De vita libri tres (Three Books on Life)
creator: Marsilio Ficino (1433-1499)
description: Ficino's De vita libri tres (composed 1489; this text from the Venice 1498 edition) — the foundational Renaissance work of astrological medicine and talismanic magic: health of scholars, long life, and drawing life from the heavens, with the Apologia. Complete Latin text. The standard English translation (Kaske & Clark, 1989) is in copyright.

title: Oratio de hominis dignitate (Oration on the Dignity of Man)
creator: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463-1494)
description: Pico's Oration on the Dignity of Man (composed 1486; first published 1496) — the 'Manifesto of the Renaissance' and the great defense of syncretic philosophy, Kabbalah and learned magic. Complete Latin text from Wikisource. Modern English translations are in copyright.

title: De arte cabalistica libri tres
creator: Johannes Reuchlin (1455-1522)
description: Reuchlin's De arte cabalistica (Hagenau, 1517) — the founding text of Christian Kabbalah: Simon the Kabbalist, Marranus the Muslim, and Philolaus the Pythagorean debate messianism, Pythagoreanism and practical Kabbalah. Complete Latin text (with Hebrew and Greek). The modern English translation (1993) is in copyright.

title: Monas Hieroglyphica
creator: John Dee (1527-1608)
description: John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica (Antwerp, 1564; this text from the Frankfurt 1591 edition) — the 24 theorems expounding his Hieroglyphic Monad: mathematics, magic, Kabbalah and alchemy in one glyph. Complete Latin text. English translations (1947/1964/2021) are in copyright.

title: The Sword of Moses (Harba de-Moshe)
creator: Anonymous (Moses Gaster, ed. and trans.)
description: The Sword of Moses (London: David Nutt, 1896) — the ancient Jewish book of magic: introduction, full English translation, Hebrew text, and index of 136 sections of mystical names with their ritual uses. Gaster's first edition from his 13th/14th-century manuscript.

title: Rituale Romanum (Roman Ritual)
creator: Catholic Church (Pope Paul V)
description: The Rituale Romanum — the Catholic Church's official ritual book containing the Rite of Exorcism. Complete Latin text of the 1925 typical edition (Ratisbon: Pustet), the direct descendant of Paul V's 1614 editio princeps; the exorcism rite is textually unchanged since 1614.

title: Cautio Criminalis, seu De processibus contra sagas liber
creator: Friedrich Spee von Langenfeld (1591-1635)
description: Spee's Cautio Criminalis (Rinteln, 1631) — the Jesuit confessor's insider demolition of the witch trials: 51 doubts exposing torture, denunciation chains, and the impossibility of proving innocence. Complete Latin text of the first edition. The English translation (2003) is in copyright.

title: Compendium Maleficarum
creator: Francesco Maria Guazzo (E. A. Ashwin, trans.; Montague Summers, ed.)
description: Guazzo's Compendium Maleficarum (orig. Milan, 1608) in the first English translation (London: John Rodker, 1929), by E. A. Ashwin with Montague Summers's notes — the great Italian witch-hunter's manual: pacts, powers, poisons, demon classification, and remedies. Complete, all three books.

title: Disquisitionum Magicarum Libri Sex
creator: Martín Antonio Del Rio (1551-1608)
description: Del Rio's Disquisitiones Magicae (first published Leuven, 1599-1600) — the 'new Catholic Malleus': the Jesuit's six-book encyclopedia of demonology covering sabbaths, pacts, divination, astrology, necromancy and natural magic. Complete Latin text, all six books. The modern English translation (2000) is in copyright.

title: Demoniality; or, Incubi and Succubi
creator: Ludovico Maria Sinistrari (1622-1701)
description: Sinistrari's De Daemonialitate (composed late 17th c.; MS found 1872) in the first English translation (Paris: Liseux, 1879) printed with the Latin text — the Franciscan demonologist's treatise arguing incubi and succubi are rational corporeal creatures. Complete.

title: The History of the Devil, As Well Ancient as Modern (The Political History of the Devil)
creator: Daniel Defoe (1660-1731)
description: Defoe's Political History of the Devil (London, 1726) — the Enlightenment-era history of Satan: scripture, Milton's Paradise Lost, the Crusades, and the devil's migration from witches to 'beaus, beauties, wits, and fools'. Complete, in two parts.

title: Procès des Templiers, Tome I
creator: Jules Michelet (1798-1874), editor
description: Michelet's edition of the Templar trial records (Paris: Imprimerie Royale, 1841), vol. I — interrogations, depositions and papal documents from the suppression of the Knights Templar (1307-1314). Complete French text.

title: Procès des Templiers, Tome II
creator: Jules Michelet (1798-1874), editor
description: Michelet's edition of the Templar trial records, vol. II — continuation of the interrogations and documents of the Templar trials. Complete French text.

title: Illustrations of Masonry
creator: William Preston (1742-1818)
description: Preston's Illustrations of Masonry (London, 1772; first edition) — the founding text of the modern Masonic lecture system: ceremonies, lectures, songs, and the first published history of Masonry, which moved the Craft from taverns toward temples. Complete English text.

title: The Reign of the House of Rothschild
creator: Egon Caesar Corti (1886-1953)
description: Corti's The Reign of the House of Rothschild (New York: Cosmopolitan, 1928) — the documentary history of the Rothschild banking house, 1830-1871, drawn from family archives. Complete English text. Published 1928: US public domain since 1 Jan 2024.

title: Die assyrische Beschwörungsserie Maqlû
creator: Knut L. Tallqvist (1865-1949)
description: Tallqvist's edition of the Assyrian anti-witchcraft series Maqlû ('Burning') — editio princeps with German translation from British Museum originals (Helsingfors, 1895). The standard public-domain source for the Maqlû series; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: The Devils and Evil Spirits of Babylonia, Vol. I: Evil Spirits
creator: R. Campbell Thompson (1876-1941)
description: Thompson's The Devils and Evil Spirits of Babylonia, vol. I (London: Luzac, 1903) — English translations of Babylonian and Assyrian anti-demon incantations (Utukki Limnuti series), with transliterations and notes. The classic public-domain English source for Mesopotamian demonology.

title: The Devils and Evil Spirits of Babylonia, Vol. II: Fever Sickness, Headache, etc.
creator: R. Campbell Thompson (1876-1941)
description: Thompson's The Devils and Evil Spirits of Babylonia, vol. II (London: Luzac, 1904) — Asakki Marsuti, Ti'i, Luh-ka and miscellaneous incantation series in English translation. (The Maqlû series itself is staged separately via Tallqvist 1895.)

title: Anecdota Atheniensia (containing the Hygromanteia transcription, pp. 397-445)
creator: Armand Delatte (1886-1954), editor
description: Delatte's Anecdota Atheniensia (Liège, 1927), containing the only public-domain transcription of the Greek Magical Treatise of Solomon (Hygromanteia), pp. 397-445 — the ancestor of the Key of Solomon: planetary talismans, angel/demon hierarchies, conjurations. Complete volume staged; the modern English translation (2011) is in copyright (see restricted entry).

title: Keely and His Discoveries
creator: Clara Bloomfield-Moore
description: The primary contemporary source on John Worrell Keely and his 'etheric force' machines: Bloomfield-Moore's compilation of letters and investigations of the Keely Motor Co. affair. Public domain; Project Gutenberg edition.

title: The Pneumatics of Hero of Alexandria
creator: Hero of Alexandria
description: Complete English translation (Bennet Woodcroft, 1851) of Hero's treatise on pneumatics, siphons, automata, and aeolipiles — the foundational text of ancient engineering and steam power, from the Taylor Walton and Maberly edition. All 78 sections plus treatise, translators', and editors' prefaces.

title: The Flying Saucers Are Real
creator: Donald E. Keyhoe
description: Book 1 of the Keyhoe UFO set (5 major books: 1950, 1953, 1955, 1960, 1973). The foundational work of civilian UFO research — the expanded 1950 book from the True magazine article that launched the civilian saucer-investigation movement. Public domain (author d. 1988).
source: Global Grey / aprie.uk (1950 Fawcett Gold Medal ed.)

title: Report of Meetings of Scientific Advisory Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects (Robertson Panel)
creator: Central Intelligence Agency
description: The 1953 CIA Robertson Panel report (the Durant Report, incl. Tab A/B/C) — the panel that recommended debunking UFOs via public education and surveillance of civilian saucer groups. Declassified US government work: public domain.

title: The Secret of Life: Cosmic Rays and Radiations of Living Beings
creator: Georges Lakhovsky
description: Mark Clement's 1939 English translation of Lakhovsky's Le Secret de la Vie — the Multiple Wave Oscillator theory of cellular resonance. Likely PD: 1939 translation never renewed; author d. 1942, translator d. before 1963.

title: Lester Hendershot's Fuelless Motor: Primary 1928 Press Accounts
creator: Multiple contemporary reporters
description: Complete set of six primary 1928 newspaper accounts of Lester Hendershot's 'fuelless motor' (New York Times Feb 25/26/27, Mar 10, Mar 25; New York American Feb 27): from the Lindbergh-attended demonstration through the Guggenheim disclaimer and debunk. Public domain.

title: Human Energy
creator: Albert Abrams
description: Abrams' foundational statement of the electronic theory behind radionics ('Electronic Reactions of Abrams'), arguing diseases emit measurable electronic vibrations. Public domain (author d. 1924); HathiTrust PD Google-digitized scan.

title: Hydrogen Gas Injector System for Internal Combustion Engine
creator: Stanley A. Meyer
description: US Patent 4,389,981 by Stanley A. Meyer, granted Jun. 28, 1983 — one of 8 staged patents of the Meyer water-fuel-cell patent family (US 5,149,407 deferred). US patents are public-domain government documents and all are expired. NOTE: a 1996 Ohio court found Meyer's claims fraudulent; patents attest novelty of description, not workability.

description: US Patent 4,421,474 by Stanley A. Meyer, granted Dec. 20, 1983 — one of 8 staged patents of the Meyer water-fuel-cell patent family (US 5,149,407 deferred). US patents are public-domain government documents and all are expired. NOTE: a 1996 Ohio court found Meyer's claims fraudulent; patents attest novelty of description, not workability.

creator: Stanley A. Meyer
description: US Patent 4,465,455 by Stanley A. Meyer, granted Aug. 14, 1984 — one of 8 staged patents of the Meyer water-fuel-cell patent family (US 5,149,407 deferred). creator: Stanley A. Meyer

title: Controlled Process for the Production of Thermal Energy from Gases and Apparatus Useful Therefore
creator: Stanley A. Meyer
description: US Patent 4,826,581 by Stanley A. Meyer, granted May 2, 1989 — one of 8 staged patents of the Meyer water-fuel-cell patent family (US 5,149,407 deferred). US patents are public-domain government documents and all are expired. NOTE: a 1996 Ohio court found Meyer's claims fraudulent; patents attest novelty of description, not workability.

title: Method for the Production of a Fuel Gas
creator: Stanley A. Meyer
description: US Patent 4,936,961 by Stanley A. Meyer, granted Jun. 26, 1990 — one of 8 staged patents of the Meyer water-fuel-cell patent family (US 5,149,407 deferred). US patents are public-domain government documents and all are expired. NOTE: a 1996 Ohio court found Meyer's claims fraudulent; patents attest novelty of description, not workability.

title: Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions
creator: Edwin A. Abbott
description: Edwin Abbott's Flatland (1884) — the founding work of higher-dimensional fiction and popular higher-space geometry; Project Gutenberg ebook #201.

title: Scientific Romances, First Series
creator: Charles Howard Hinton
description: Charles Howard Hinton's Scientific Romances, First Series (1884-86) — coined 'tesseract'; the origin text of fourth-dimension popularization. Project Gutenberg ebook #49289.

title: Researches in the Phenomena of Spiritualism
creator: William Crookes
description: Sir William Crookes' Researches in the Phenomena of Spiritualism (1874) — the landmark scientific investigation of mediumship (D.D. Home, Kate Fox). Text taken from the 1926 Two Worlds reprint (public domain), which adds Crookes' 1898 address and an appendix by Arthur Conan Doyle.

title: The Descent of Man, Vol. I
creator: Charles Darwin
description: Charles Darwin's The Descent of Man, and Selection in Relation to Sex (1871), Volume I — first edition text; applies evolution to human ancestry. Project Gutenberg ebook #34967.

title: The Descent of Man, Vol. II
creator: Charles Darwin
description: Charles Darwin's The Descent of Man, and Selection in Relation to Sex (1871), Volume II — sexual selection across the animal kingdom. Project Gutenberg ebook #36520.

title: Evidence as to Man's Place in Nature
creator: Thomas Henry Huxley
description: T.H. Huxley's Evidence as to Man's Place in Nature (1863) — the first book to apply Darwinism explicitly to human ancestry ('Darwin's bulldog'). Project Gutenberg ebook #2931.

title: The Geological Evidences of the Antiquity of Man
creator: Charles Lyell
description: Sir Charles Lyell's The Antiquity of Man (1863) — the founding text of deep time applied to humanity; established human antiquity alongside extinct fauna. Project Gutenberg ebook #6335.

title: South: The Story of Shackleton's Last Expedition 1914-1917
creator: Ernest Shackleton
description: Ernest Shackleton's South (1919) — the Endurance expedition account: the loss of the ship, the Elephant Island open-boat journey, and the South Georgia crossing. Project Gutenberg ebook #5199.

title: The Worst Journey in the World
creator: Apsley Cherry-Garrard
description: Apsley Cherry-Garrard's The Worst Journey in the World (1922) — the classic Terra Nova expedition memoir: the winter journey, Scott's polar party, survival. Both volumes in one file. Project Gutenberg ebook #14363.

title: The South Pole, Vol. I
creator: Roald Amundsen (A.G. Chater, trans.)
description: Roald Amundsen's The South Pole (1912), Volume I — the first successful South Pole expedition account; A.G. Chater English translation (translator d. 1951). Project Gutenberg ebook #3414.

title: The South Pole, Vol. II
creator: Roald Amundsen (A.G. Chater, trans.)
description: Roald Amundsen's The South Pole (1912), Volume II — the dash to the Pole and return; A.G. Chater English translation (translator d. 1951). Project Gutenberg ebook #3415.

title: Scott's Last Expedition, Vol. I
creator: Robert Falcon Scott
description: Scott's Last Expedition (1913), Volume I — Scott's Terra Nova journals, edited with a preface by Sir Clements Markham. Project Gutenberg ebook #11579.

title: Scott's Last Expedition, Vol. II
creator: Robert Falcon Scott
description: Scott's Last Expedition (1913), Volume II — the scientific reports of the Terra Nova expedition (geology, physics, zoology) and the search-party narratives. Harvested from Wikisource (1913 Smith, Elder edition transclusion).

title: The Fairy Mythology
creator: Thomas Keightley
description: Thomas Keightley's The Fairy Mythology (1828) — the first great comparative survey of fairy lore across Europe, with mermaid and sea-being traditions; Project Gutenberg's 1892 enlarged edition text. Project Gutenberg ebook #41006.

title: The Little Mermaid
creator: Hans Christian Andersen
description: Hans Christian Andersen's 'The Little Mermaid' (1837) — the literary originator of the modern mermaid; complete story extracted from Project Gutenberg's Fairy Tales of Hans Christian Andersen (ebook #27200; translator not credited in the PG edition, classic Mrs. Paull-era rendering).

title: Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697
creator: W.G. Aston (trans.)
description: The Nihongi (Chronicles of Japan), translated by William George Aston (1896) — the first complete English translation of Japan's oldest official history; Books I-XXX with preface, introduction, errata, and index. Harvested from Wikisource (Japan Society / K. Paul, Trench, Trubner edition).

title: The Mishnah
creator: Herbert Danby (trans.)
description: Herbert Danby's English translation of the Mishnah (1933) — the first complete English Mishnah, still the scholarly standard. Under copyright in the US (published 1933; translator d. 1953): no text distributed; metadata only.

title: The Constitution of the United States and the Bill of Rights
creator: United States Constitutional Convention / United States Congress
description: The Constitution of the United States (1787) with the Bill of Rights, the first ten amendments ratified 1791. Text from Wikisource (US House of Representatives edition).

title: Magna Carta (1215)
creator: King John of England
description: Magna Carta Libertatum, the Great Charter of 1215. English translation from the Avalon Project, Yale Law School.

title: English Bill of Rights (1689)
creator: Parliament of England
description: An Act Declaring the Rights and Liberties of the Subject and Settling the Succession of the Crown (1689). From the Avalon Project, Yale Law School.

title: The Federalist Papers
creator: Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, John Jay
description: The Federalist Papers (1787-1788): 85 essays by Hamilton, Madison, and Jay advocating ratification of the US Constitution. Project Gutenberg edition.

title: The Anti-Federalist Papers: The Brutus Essays
creator: Brutus (attributed to Robert Yates)
description: The Brutus essays (1787-1788): sixteen Anti-Federalist essays opposing ratification of the US Constitution, the most important Anti-Federalist work. From constitution.org.

title: The Spirit of Laws
creator: Baron de Montesquieu (Thomas Nugent, trans.)
description: Montesquieu's The Spirit of Laws (1748), Thomas Nugent's 1752 English translation. Complete in 31 books with translator's note and preface. 1914 Bell edition via constitution.org.

title: Rights of Man
creator: Thomas Paine
description: Thomas Paine's Rights of Man (1791-1792), Parts First and Second. Conway edition via Project Gutenberg.

title: Democracy in America, Vol. 1
creator: Alexis de Tocqueville (Henry Reeve, trans.)
description: Tocqueville's Democracy in America, Volume 1 (1835). Henry Reeve translation via Project Gutenberg.

title: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa
creator: Mungo Park
description: Mungo Park's Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (1799 Bulmer first edition) — the landmark account of his 1795-1797 Niger expedition for the African Association, including Rennell's geographical appendix.

title: Journal of a Mission to the Interior of Africa in the Year 1805
creator: Mungo Park
description: Mungo Park's Journal of his fatal second mission to the interior of Africa (1805), published posthumously — the record of the expedition on which he died at Bussa on the Niger.

title: Personal Narrative of a Pilgrimage to El-Medinah and Meccah, Vol. I
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's Personal Narrative of a Pilgrimage to El-Medinah and Meccah (Memorial edition), Vol. I — his disguised 1853 journey to the forbidden holy cities, the founding text of Victorian travel writing.

title: Personal Narrative of a Pilgrimage to El-Medinah and Meccah, Vol. II
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's Personal Narrative of a Pilgrimage to El-Medinah and Meccah (Memorial edition), Vol. II — completing his 1853 pilgrimage account, with the return journey and appendices.

title: Journal of the Discovery of the Source of the Nile
creator: John Hanning Speke
description: Speke's Journal of the Discovery of the Source of the Nile (Blackwood, 1863) — the first-edition account of the 1860-1863 expedition with Grant that identified Lake Victoria as the Nile's source.

title: A Walk Across Africa; or, Domestic Scenes from my Nile Journal
creator: James Augustus Grant
description: Grant's A Walk Across Africa (Blackwood, 1864) — his companion narrative to Speke's Nile expedition, the domestic and logistical record of the first traverse from Zanzibar to Egypt.

title: Missionary Travels and Researches in South Africa
creator: David Livingstone
description: Livingstone's Missionary Travels and Researches in South Africa (1857) — the complete 32-chapter account of his 1841-1856 trans-African journeys, the Victoria Falls, and the Zambezi.

title: Through the Dark Continent, Vol. I
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's Through the Dark Continent (1899 Newnes edition), Vol. I — the account of his 1874-1877 trans-African expedition down the Congo, the second European crossing of the continent.

title: Through the Dark Continent, Vol. II
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's Through the Dark Continent (1899 Newnes edition), Vol. II — completing the 1874-1877 Congo expedition narrative, with appendices.

title: Layamon's Brut, Vol. I
creator: Layamon (Frederic Madden, ed./trans.)
description: Layamon's Brut (c. 1200), Vol. I — Madden's 1847 Society of Antiquaries edition with literal English translation: the first English chronicle in alliterative verse, from Brutus of Troy to the coming of the Saxons.

title: Layamon's Brut, Vol. II
creator: Layamon (Frederic Madden, ed./trans.)
description: Layamon's Brut (c. 1200), Vol. II — Madden's 1847 edition with literal translation, continuing the verse chronicle of Britain's kings through the Arthurian age.

title: Layamon's Brut, Vol. III
creator: Layamon (Frederic Madden, ed./trans.)
description: Layamon's Brut (c. 1200), Vol. III — Madden's 1847 edition with literal translation, completing the chronicle through Cadwalader.

title: The Nibelungenlied
creator: Anonymous (Daniel Bussier Shumway, trans.)
description: The Nibelungenlied (c. 1200) in Shumway's translation — the great German heroic epic of Siegfried, Kriemhild, and the fall of the Burgundians.

title: The Song of Roland
creator: Anonymous (C. K. Scott Moncrieff, trans.)
description: The Song of Roland (c. 1140) in Scott Moncrieff's translation — the foundational French chanson de geste: Roland's last stand at Roncesvalles.

title: Memoirs of Louis IX (Saint Louis)
creator: Jean de Joinville (Thomas Johnes, trans.)
description: Joinville's Memoirs of Louis IX (finished 1309), translated by Thomas Johnes — the intimate first-hand life of Saint Louis and the Seventh Crusade, extracted complete with the 'Appendix to Joinville' (knight lists and Makrisi's Saracen account) from Bohn's Chronicles of the Crusades (1888 reprint of the 1848 edition).

title: The Conquest of Constantinople
creator: Geoffroi de Villehardouin (Frank T. Marzials, trans.)
description: Villehardouin's Conquest of Constantinople (c. 1213) in Marzials's translation — the earliest surviving French prose chronicle, the insider's account of the Fourth Crusade and the sack of Constantinople.

title: Chronicles of England, France, Spain, Vol. I
creator: Jean Froissart (Thomas Johnes, trans.)
description: Froissart's Chronicles (1844 Smith edition), Vol. I — Johnes's English translation of the great 14th-century chronicle of chivalry, the Hundred Years' War to 1385.

title: Chronicles of England, France, Spain, Vol. II
creator: Jean Froissart (Thomas Johnes, trans.)
description: Froissart's Chronicles (1844 Smith edition), Vol. II — Johnes's translation, completing the chronicle through the deposition of Richard II (1399), with index.

title: The History of the Franks, Vol. I
creator: Gregory of Tours (O. M. Dalton, trans.)
description: Gregory of Tours' History of the Franks (completed 594), Vol. I — Dalton's 1927 Clarendon translation, the foundational narrative of Merovingian Gaul.

title: The History of the Franks, Vol. II
creator: Gregory of Tours (O. M. Dalton, trans.)
description: Gregory of Tours' History of the Franks (completed 594), Vol. II — Dalton's 1927 Clarendon translation, completing the ten books of Merovingian history.

title: Ecclesiastical History of the English People
creator: Bede (trans. revised from J. A. Giles)
description: Bede's Ecclesiastical History of the English People (731) — the founding work of English history, from Caesar's invasion to Bede's own day.

title: Life of Charlemagne
creator: Einhard (A. J. Grant, trans.)
description: Einhard's Life of Charlemagne (c. 830) in A. J. Grant's 1905 translation — the classic courtier's biography of Charles the Great, extracted complete (prologue, preface, all 33 chapters, and the will) from Grant's 'Early Lives of Charlemagne' (Gutenberg #48870).

title: Life of King Alfred
creator: Asser (J. A. Giles, trans.)
description: Asser's Life of King Alfred (893) in Giles's translation — the contemporary Welsh monk's biography of Alfred the Great, extracted complete from the Giles 'Six Old English Chronicles' collection (Gutenberg #37848).

title: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle
creator: Anonymous (J. A. Giles, trans.; James Ingram, rev.)
description: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle in Giles's translation (revised by Ingram) — the year-by-year Old English record of England from the Roman invasion to the Norman Conquest.

title: History of the Kings of Britain
creator: Geoffrey of Monmouth (J. A. Giles, trans.)
description: Geoffrey of Monmouth's History of the Kings of Britain (c. 1136) in Giles's translation — the great medieval bestseller that gave the world Arthur, Merlin, and Lear, extracted complete from the Giles 'Six Old English Chronicles' collection (Gutenberg #37848).

title: Six Things You Didn't Know About Watergate
creator: National Security Archive (Luke A. Nichter)
description: National Security Archive briefing book (2021): six new findings on Watergate drawn from declassified Nixon White House tapes, memos, diaries and FBI records — the Colson 'sticking it to Washington' call, the McCord note that broke the cover-up, and more. Primary documents only; public domain U.S. government records.

title: Stopping Korea from Going Nuclear, Part II
creator: National Security Archive (William Burr)
description: National Security Archive Nuclear Vault briefing book, Part II (2017): declassified U.S. documents on South Korea's secret nuclear-weapons program — the French reprocessing-plant deal, the Canadian CANDU bargain, and the U.S. pressure campaign that stopped Seoul from going nuclear. Public domain U.S. government records.

title: The U.S. Nuclear Presence in Western Europe, 1954-1962, Part II
creator: National Security Archive (William Burr)
description: National Security Archive Nuclear Vault briefing book, Part II (2020): declassified documents on U.S. nuclear weapons deployments in Western Europe, 1954-1962 — basing, custody, and allied nuclear sharing at the height of the Cold War. Public domain U.S. government records.

title: Crises, Alerts, and DEFCONS, 1961-1976 – Part II
creator: National Security Archive (William Burr)
description: National Security Archive briefing book, Part II (2021): declassified records of U.S. military alerts, DEFCON changes, and nuclear crisis management, 1961-1976 — from Berlin and Cuba through the 1973 Middle East war. Public domain U.S. government records.

title: Manhattan Project Director's Files Illuminate Early History of Atomic Bomb
creator: National Security Archive
description: National Security Archive Nuclear Vault briefing book (2024): declassified documents from Manhattan Project director Leslie Groves' files illuminating the early history of the atomic bomb — organization, security, and the road to Trinity. Public domain U.S. government records.

title: The CIA Station in Mexico: The Last JFK Assassination Records Secrets
creator: National Security Archive
description: National Security Archive briefing book (2026): newly released JFK assassination records on the CIA's Mexico City station — surveillance of Lee Harvey Oswald's visits to the Soviet and Cuban embassies and what the station knew. Public domain U.S. government records.

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1958–1960, Cuba, Volume VI
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume VI (1958–1960): the complete declassified documentary record of U.S. policy toward Cuba from Batista's fall through Castro's first two years — the revolution, nationalizations, and the break in relations. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume X, Cuba, January 1961–September 1962
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume X (1961–1963): the complete declassified record of U.S.-Cuba relations from the Bay of Pigs through September 1962 — covert operations, the embargo, and the run-up to the missile crisis. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume XI, Cuban Missile Crisis and Aftermath
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume XI (1961–1963): the complete declassified documentary record of the Cuban Missile Crisis and its aftermath — ExComm deliberations, the naval quarantine, and the secret Turkey-for-Cuba missile trade. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume XXI, Chile, 1969–1973
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume XXI (1969–1976): the complete declassified record of U.S. policy toward Chile, 1969–1973 — 'make the economy scream,' Track I and Track II covert action, and the road to the September 1973 coup against Allende. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952–1954, Iran, 1951–1954, Volume X
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume X (1952–1954): the complete declassified documentary record of the 1953 Iran coup — the U.S.-British operation (TPAJAX) that overthrew Premier Mossadeq and restored the Shah. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952–1954, The American Republics, Volume IV
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume IV (1952–1954): the complete declassified record of U.S. policy toward Latin America — including the documentary record of the 1954 CIA operation (PBSUCCESS) that overthrew Guatemala's Arbenz government. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968, Volume XXIII, Congo, 1960–1968
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume XXIII (1964–1968): the complete declassified documentary record of the Congo crisis, 1960–1968 — Lumumba's murder, UN intervention, the Simba rebellion, and Mobutu's rise. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968, Volume XXXI, South and Central America; Mexico
creator: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
description: FRUS Volume XXXI (1964–1968): the complete declassified record of U.S. policy toward South and Central America and Mexico in the 1960s — counterinsurgency, military aid, and the Alliance for Progress after the Cuban revolution. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: U.S. Department of State (Office of the Historian)

title: Final Report of the Independent Counsel for Iran/Contra Matters, Volume I: Investigations and Prosecutions
creator: Lawrence E. Walsh, Independent Counsel
description: The Walsh Report, Volume I (August 4, 1993): the Independent Counsel's complete final account of the Iran-Contra investigation and prosecutions — the arms-for-hostages deals, the Contra diversion, and the cases against North, Poindexter, McFarlane, Secord, and others. Public domain U.S. government work.
source: Federation of American Scientists (U.S. government report)

title: Amerithrax Investigative Summary
creator: U.S. Department of Justice
description: The Justice Department's Amerithrax Investigative Summary (February 19, 2010): the FBI's complete public account of the 2001 anthrax letter attacks investigation — the science, the suspects, and the case against Bruce Ivins. Released under FOIA; public domain U.S. government work.

title: Contributions to the Theory of Natural Selection
creator: Alfred Russel Wallace
description: Wallace's 1870 collection of essays including 'The Limits of Natural Selection as applied to Man' — the co-discoverer of natural selection arguing, controversially, that human intellect required more than selection alone. A founding document of evolutionary anthropology.

title: The Evolution of Man: A Popular Exposition of the Principal Points of Human Ontogeny and Phylogeny, Vol. 1
creator: Ernst Haeckel
description: Vol. 1 of Haeckel's 'Anthropogenie' (1874): human embryology and the biogenetic law, tracing man's descent through the vertebrate series. The most widely read popular evolution text of the 19th century after Darwin.

title: The Evolution of Man: A Popular Exposition of the Principal Points of Human Ontogeny and Phylogeny, Vol. 2
creator: Ernst Haeckel
description: Vol. 2 of Haeckel's 'Anthropogenie': the phylogeny of man, the genealogical tree of the human race, and the hypothetical 'Pithecanthropus alalus' — the speechless ape-man Haeckel predicted decades before Dubois found Java Man.

title: The History of Creation, Vol. 1
creator: Ernst Haeckel
description: Vol. 1 of Haeckel's 'Natürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte' (1868): the general doctrine of evolution, spontaneous generation, and the monophyletic tree of life. The book that made Darwinism a mass movement in Germany.

title: The History of Creation, Vol. 2
creator: Ernst Haeckel
description: Vol. 2 of Haeckel's 'Natürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte': the special morphology and phylogeny of organisms, including man's place among the primates and the famous genealogical trees.

title: The Last Link: Our Present Knowledge of the Descent of Man
creator: Ernst Haeckel
description: Haeckel's 1898 Cambridge lecture on the descent of man, reviewing the fossil evidence — Neanderthal, Pithecanthropus — and defending the ape-man link against Virchow's skepticism.

title: The Riddle of the Universe at the Close of the Nineteenth Century
creator: Ernst Haeckel
description: Haeckel's 'Welträthsel' (1899; this English edition 1901): the monist manifesto applying evolution to cosmology, mind, and morals. Immensely influential — and the prime target of the anti-Darwinian backlash.

title: A Manual of the Antiquity of Man
creator: J. P. MacLean
description: An early American synthesis of human antiquity: fossil man, cave deposits, shell mounds, and the mound-builders, summarizing the state of prehistoric archaeology in the 1870s.

title: Pre-historic Times, as Illustrated by Ancient Remains, and the Manners and Customs of Modern Savages
creator: John Lubbock
description: Lubbock's 1865 classic: coined 'Palaeolithic' and 'Neolithic', systematized the Stone Age, and founded prehistoric archaeology as a discipline. The single most cited synthesis of its generation.

title: The Origin of Civilisation and the Primitive Condition of Man
creator: John Lubbock
description: Lubbock's companion volume (1870) on the mental and social condition of early man: the origin of language, religion, marriage, and law among 'primitive' peoples — the founding text of evolutionary anthropology.

title: Primitive Culture: Researches into the Development of Mythology, Philosophy, Religion, Art, and Custom, Vol. 1
creator: Edward Burnett Tylor
description: Vol. 1 of Tylor's 1871 masterwork: the doctrine of 'survivals' and the animistic theory of religion's origin. Founded cultural anthropology; 'culture' as a technical term starts here.

title: Primitive Culture: Researches into the Development of Mythology, Philosophy, Religion, Art, and Custom, Vol. 2
creator: Edward Burnett Tylor
description: Vol. 2 of 'Primitive Culture': the development of religion from animism through polytheism — the evolutionary scheme of religious belief that dominated anthropology for fifty years.

title: Anthropology: An Introduction to the Study of Man and Civilization
creator: Edward Burnett Tylor
description: Tylor's 1881 textbook: the first general introduction to anthropology, covering physical anthropology, language, and cultural evolution for the general reader. The discipline's standard primer for a generation.

title: Ancient Society; or, Researches in the Lines of Human Progress from Savagery through Barbarism to Civilization
creator: Lewis Henry Morgan
description: Morgan's 1877 evolutionary scheme — savagery, barbarism, civilization — built on kinship systems and Iroquois ethnography. The foundation of both American anthropology and Engels's 'Origin of the Family'.

title: The Ancient Stone Implements, Weapons, and Ornaments of Great Britain
creator: John Evans
description: Evans's 1872 typology of British stone tools: the reference work that made flint typology a science and gave archaeologists the vocabulary — hand-axe, scraper, burin — still used today.

title: Cave Hunting: Researches on the Evidence of Caves Respecting the Early Inhabitants of Europe
creator: W. Boyd Dawkins
description: Dawkins's 1874 synthesis of cave archaeology: the association of extinct fauna with human remains in British and European caves, and the antiquity of man in Britain.

title: Early Man in Britain and His Place in the Tertiary Period
creator: W. Boyd Dawkins
description: Dawkins's 1880 sequel: a systematic survey of British Pleistocene geology, fauna, and human remains — the standard account of early man in Britain for decades.

title: Prehistoric Man: Researches into the Origin of Civilisation in the Old and the New World
creator: Daniel Wilson
description: Wilson's 1862 work: coined the word 'prehistoric' in English and gave the first systematic account of North American archaeology alongside the European evidence.

title: Vestiges of the Natural History of Creation
creator: Robert Chambers
description: The anonymous 1844 bestseller (by Robert Chambers) that popularized evolution — including human evolution — fifteen years before Darwin. The book Darwin had to answer.

title: Zoological Philosophy: An Exposition with Regard to the Natural History of Animals
creator: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
description: Lamarck's 1809 'Philosophie zoologique' (this is Hugh Elliot's 1914 translation): the first comprehensive theory of evolution, including the descent of man — the necessary foil to Darwin.

title: Principles of Geology, Vol. 1
creator: Charles Lyell
description: Vol. 1 of Lyell's 1830 'Principles': uniformitarianism — the present as key to the past — giving Darwin his deep time and his method. First edition text.

title: Principles of Geology, Vol. 2
creator: Charles Lyell
description: Vol. 2 of the 1830 'Principles': the economy of nature, extinction, and the succession of life — the geological framework into which fossil man would later fit.

title: Principles of Geology, Vol. 3
creator: Charles Lyell
description: Vol. 3 of the 1830 'Principles': aqueous and igneous causes, concluding the uniformitarian system that made human antiquity geologically conceivable.

title: Crania Americana; or, A Comparative View of the Skulls of Various Aboriginal Nations of North and South America
creator: Samuel George Morton
description: Morton's 1839 craniometric atlas: the founding — and fatally flawed — work of American physical anthropology, whose racial rankings were demolished by Gould's 'Mismeasure of Man'. Essential for the history of scientific racism.

title: Fossil Men: Elements of Human Palaeontology
creator: Marcellin Boule
description: Boule's 'Les hommes fossiles' (1921; this is the 1923 Ritchie translation): the great French synthesis — La Chapelle-aux-Saints, Neanderthals as a failed side-branch — that defined paleoanthropology for a generation.

title: Skeletal Remains Suggesting or Attributed to Early Man in North America
creator: Aleš Hrdlička
description: Hrdlička's 1907 Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 33: the great debunking — demolishing every claimed 'early man' in North America and setting the peopling of the Americas debate for decades.

title: Pre-historic America
creator: Marquis de Nadaillac
description: Nadaillac's 1884 survey of American prehistory: mound-builders, cliff-dwellers, and the antiquity of man in the New World, from a leading French prehistorian.

title: Ancient Hunters and Their Modern Representatives
creator: W. J. Sollas
description: Sollas's 1915 synthesis (2nd ed.): Palaeolithic races — Neanderthal, Aurignacian, Magdalenian — each matched to living 'primitive' peoples. The classic statement of the unilinear cultural-evolution view of fossil man.

title: Human Origins: A Manual of Prehistory, Vol. 1
creator: George Grant MacCurdy
description: Vol. 1 of MacCurdy's 1924 manual: the geological background, eoliths, and the lower Palaeolithic — the American textbook synthesis of human prehistory between the wars.

title: Human Origins: A Manual of Prehistory, Vol. 2
creator: George Grant MacCurdy
description: Vol. 2 of MacCurdy's 1924 manual: the upper Palaeolithic, Neolithic, and the races of fossil man — Neanderthal through Cro-Magnon.

title: The Antiquity of Man
creator: Arthur Keith
description: Keith's 1925 synthesis: the leading British anatomist's account of fossil man — Piltdown accepted, Neanderthal marginalized — capturing the state of the field at its most confident and most wrong.

title: Pithecanthropus erectus: Eine menschenaehnliche Uebergangsform aus Java
creator: Eugène Dubois
description: Dubois's 1894 monograph (in German): the original description of Pithecanthropus erectus — the Java ape-man, the first fossil hominin found outside Europe, and the vindication of Haeckel's prediction.

title: The Ice Age in North America and Its Bearings upon the Antiquity of Man
creator: G. Frederick Wright
description: Wright's 1889 work: glaciation and the antiquity of man in America — the American counterpart to the European glacial-archaeology debates.

title: Fossil Men and Their Modern Representatives
creator: J. W. Dawson
description: Dawson's 1880 work: a leading anti-Darwinian geologist's account of fossil man, arguing for the recent origin and unity of the human race against evolutionary interpretations.

title: Men of the Old Stone Age: Their Environment, Life and Art
creator: Henry Fairfield Osborn
description: Osborn's lavishly illustrated 1915 synthesis: the standard American account of Palaeolithic man — Cro-Magnon art, Neanderthal life — from the president of the American Museum of Natural History.

title: Man Rises to Parnassus: Critical Epochs in the Prehistory of Man
creator: Henry Fairfield Osborn
description: Osborn's 1928 Princeton lectures: the 'dawn man' theory and the central-Asian origins hypothesis — the last great statement of Osborn's influential, now-abandoned views.

title: Man and His Ancestor: A Study in Evolution
creator: Charles Morris
description: Morris's 1900 popular evolution text: man's descent traced through the primates, with chapters on the antiquity of man and the fossil evidence as then known.

title: Human Origins
creator: Samuel Laing
description: Laing's 1892 popular work: Darwinism applied to man — the antiquity of the human race, the Aryan question, and the coming of civilization, from a Victorian man of letters.

title: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals
creator: Charles Darwin
description: Darwin's 1872 classic: the continuity of human and animal emotion — the third and most human installment of the evolutionary trilogy after Origin and Descent.

title: Inquiries into Human Faculty and Its Development
creator: Francis Galton
description: Galton's 1883 work: the founding text of eugenics and behavioral genetics — twin studies, mental imagery, and the statistical study of human variation.

title: On the Genesis of Species
creator: St. George Jackson Mivart
description: Mivart's 1871 critique: the most formidable scientific attack on Darwinism from within biology — the book that ended Darwin's friendship with his former disciple and forced the 6th edition of the Origin.

title: Der Unterkiefer des Homo Heidelbergensis aus den Sanden von Mauer bei Heidelberg
creator: Otto Schoetensack
description: Schoetensack's 1908 monograph (in German): the original description of the Mauer jaw — Homo heidelbergensis, the oldest human fossil then known, establishing deep human antiquity in Europe.

title: Primitive Man
creator: Louis Figuier
description: Figuier's 1870 popular prehistory (translated from the French): the first lavishly illustrated popular account of primeval man for the general public — a Victorian bestseller.

title: Hereditary Genius: An Inquiry into Its Laws and Consequences
creator: Francis Galton
description: Galton's 1869 founding work of eugenics: the statistical argument that genius — and eminence generally — runs in families, launching the nature-nurture debate and the eugenics movement.

title: Recherches sur les ossemens fossiles découverts dans les cavernes de la province de Liège, Tome 1
creator: Philippe-Charles Schmerling
description: Vol. 1 of Schmerling's 1833 masterpiece (in French): the first scientific demonstration of fossil man — the Engis skull found with extinct fauna — ignored for a generation until the Neanderthal vindicated it.

title: Recherches sur les ossemens fossiles découverts dans les cavernes de la province de Liège, Tome 2
creator: Philippe-Charles Schmerling
description: Vol. 2 of Schmerling's 1833 work: the detailed faunal and geological evidence from the Liège caves establishing the contemporaneity of man with extinct mammals.

title: On the Crania of the Most Ancient Races of Man
creator: Hermann Schaaffhausen (translated by George Busk)
description: The 1861 English translation (with Busk's remarks) of Schaaffhausen's 1858 paper: the first scientific description of the Neanderthal skull, including Fuhlrott's firsthand account of the 1856 discovery. The founding document of paleoanthropology.

title: Australopithecus africanus: The Man-Ape of South Africa
creator: Raymond Dart
description: Dart's 1925 Nature paper announcing the Taung child: Australopithecus africanus — the first African ape-man, rejected for decades, then vindicated as the true root of humanity. One of the century's great scientific papers.

title: A New Cave Man from Rhodesia, South Africa
creator: Arthur Smith Woodward
description: Woodward's 1921 Nature paper naming Homo rhodesiensis from the Broken Hill (Kabwe) skull — the first archaic human fossil found in Africa, announcing the continent's deep human past.

title: On the Pithecanthropus erectus, from the Tertiary of Java
creator: O. C. Marsh
description: Marsh's 1896 notice (American Journal of Science) on Dubois's Java ape-man: the great American paleontologist's verdict on Pithecanthropus, bringing the discovery to Anglophone science.

title: The Reputed Fossil Man of the Neanderthal
creator: William King
description: King's 1864 paper (Quarterly Journal of Science) coining Homo neanderthalensis: the first to declare the Neanderthal a distinct human species — the naming paper for fossil humanity's most famous member.

title: On the Discovery of a Palaeolithic Human Skull and Mandible in a Flint-bearing Gravel overlying the Wealden (Hastings Beds) at Piltdown, Fletching (Sussex)
creator: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward
description: The 1913 announcement (Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society) of 'Piltdown Man' — Eoanthropus dawsoni, the supposed dawn-man of Sussex. Later exposed as a forgery; the most famous scientific fraud in history, and a cautionary classic.

title: Supplementary Note on the Discovery of a Palaeolithic Human Skull and Mandible at Piltdown (Sussex)
creator: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward
description: The 1914 supplementary note: more 'Piltdown' fragments — the canine tooth — tightening the fraud's grip on British paleoanthropology for another forty years.

title: On a Bone Implement from Piltdown (Sussex)
creator: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward
description: The 1915 third Piltdown paper: a worked 'bone implement' from the gravel — part of the growing body of fabricated evidence, read to the Geological Society in December 1914.

title: On Pithecanthropus erectus: A Transitional Form Between Man and the Apes
creator: Eugène Dubois
description: Dubois's 1896 English paper (Journal of the Anthropological Institute): the Java ape-man presented to the Anglophone world — the 'missing link' as a transitional form, with the famous femur, skullcap, and teeth.

title: On Fossil Remains of Man
creator: Thomas Henry Huxley
description: Huxley's 1862 Royal Institution discourse on the Engis and Neanderthal skulls: the first great Darwinian synthesis of the fossil evidence for human antiquity.

title: Further Remarks upon the Human Remains from the Neanderthal
creator: Thomas Henry Huxley
description: Huxley's 1864 reply to King (Natural History Review): demolishing the claim that the Neanderthal skull was generically distinct from man, and the classic statement of the Darwinian view of fossil humanity.

title: Tertiary Man in Asia: The Chou Kou Tien Discovery
creator: Davidson Black
description: Black's 1926 Science announcement: hominid teeth from Choukoutien — the opening shot of the Peking Man saga, arguing for a center of human dispersal in Asia.

title: Sinanthropus pekinensis: The Recovery of Further Fossil Remains of this Early Hominid from the Chou Kou Tien Deposit
creator: Davidson Black
description: Black's 1929 Science paper: the growing Sinanthropus sample — jaws and teeth showing hominid dentition on an anthropoid jaw, the key evidence for Peking Man's humanity.

title: On the Occurrence of Flint-Implements, associated with the Remains of Animals of Extinct Species in Beds of a late Geological Period, in France at Amiens and Abbeville, and in England at Hoxne
creator: Joseph Prestwich
description: Prestwich's 1860 Philosophical Transactions paper: the Royal Society's verdict confirming Boucher de Perthes — flint tools with extinct fauna, establishing the antiquity of man. The paper that ended the debate.

creator: Aeschylus (John Stuart Blackie, trans.)
description: All seven surviving tragedies of Aeschylus (Agamemnon, Choephorae, Eumenides, Persians, Seven Against Thebes, Suppliants, Prometheus Bound) in John Stuart Blackie's translation via Project Gutenberg.

description: Mesmer's own 1781 historical summary of the facts of animal magnetism — the pivotal primary source for early mesmerism.

title: D'Eslon: Observations sur le magnétisme animal
creator: Charles d'Eslon
description: D'Eslon, Mesmer's chief disciple, defends animal magnetism — the key pro-mesmerism medical tract before the 1784 commissions.

title: Puységur: Suite des mémoires sur le magnétisme animal
creator: Marquis de Puységur
description: Puységur's 1786 sequel developing artificial somnambulism — the turning point toward the psychological tradition.

title: Hildegard of Bingen: Physica (1533)
creator: Hildegard of Bingen
description: The 1533 Strasbourg first printed edition of Hildegard's Physica — the nine books on the natures of elements, plants, trees, fish, birds, and beasts.

title: Alexander Neckam: De naturis rerum (Wright, 1863)
creator: Alexander Neckam
description: Neckam's De naturis rerum in Wright's 1863 Rolls Series edition — the great 12th-century English natural history with its marvels.

title: Deleuze: Histoire critique du magnétisme animal
creator: J. P. F. Deleuze
description: Deleuze's 1813 critical history of animal magnetism — the pivotal historiography surveying every tract for and against.

title: Thouret: Recherches et doutes sur le magnétisme animal
creator: Michel Augustin Thouret
description: Thouret's skeptical inquiry into animal magnetism — the medical establishment's critique alongside the royal commissions.

title: Recueil des pièces les plus intéressantes sur le magnétisme animal
creator: Anonymous
description: The essential 1784 anthology of the mesmerism debate — Mesmer's propositions, d'Eslon's letters, and the principal tracts for and against.

title: Rondelet: Libri de piscibus marinis
creator: Guillaume Rondelet
description: Rondelet's 1554-55 Libri de piscibus marinis — the great Renaissance ichthyology with the sea-monk and marine monsters.

title: Lycosthenes: Prodigiorum ac ostentorum chronicon
creator: Conrad Lycosthenes
description: Lycosthenes's 1557 chronicle of prodigies from Creation to 1557 — monstrous births, sea monsters, celestial marvels.

title: Walter Map: De nugis curialium (Tupper/Ogle, 1924)
creator: Walter Map
description: Tupper and Ogle's 1924 Englishing of De nugis curialium — King Herla, the wild man, vampires, and courtier satire.

title: Guillaume le Clerc: Le Bestiaire divin (Hippeau, 1852)
creator: Guillaume le Clerc
description: Guillaume's c. 1210 Norman-French verse Bestiaire divin in Hippeau's edition — the great verse bestiary.

title: The Middle English Bestiary (Morris, 1872)
creator: Anonymous
description: The c. 1250 Middle English verse Bestiary after Morris's 1872 EETS edition — with the famous siren/mermaid chapter.

title: William of Rubruck: The Journey to the Eastern Parts (Rockhill, 1900)
creator: William of Rubruck
description: Rockhill's 1900 Hakluyt edition of Rubruck's 1253-55 journey — Prester John, the dog-headed peoples, and Mongol marvels.

title: Friar Odoric: The Journal, 1318-1330 (Komroff, 1928)
creator: Odoric of Pordenone
description: Odoric's Relatio after Komroff's 1928 Contemporaries of Marco Polo — the Valley of Death, the pepper forests, and Eastern marvels.

title: The Old English Physiologus (Cook, 1921)
creator: Anonymous
description: The surviving Old English Physiologus fragment (Panther, Whale, Partridge) in Cook's 1921 edition with translations.

title: Belon: L'histoire naturelle des estranges poissons marins
creator: Pierre Belon
description: Belon's 1551 book of strange marine fishes — dolphins, whales, and sea-monsters with true portraiture.

title: Gesner: Historiae animalium, Lib. I (de quadrupedibus viviparis)
creator: Conrad Gesner
description: Gesner's 1551 first volume on viviparous quadrupeds — the founding work of modern zoology; multi-volume set, staged as metadata with scan links.

title: Gesner: Historiae animalium, Lib. II (de quadrupedibus oviparis)
creator: Conrad Gesner
description: Gesner's second volume on oviparous quadrupeds (1586 2nd ed. of 1554) — the great Renaissance natural history continued.

title: Gesner: Historiae animalium, Lib. III (de avium natura)
creator: Conrad Gesner
description: Gesner's 1555 third volume on birds — the ornithology of the Historiae animalium.

title: Gesner: Historiae animalium, Lib. IIII (de piscium natura)
creator: Conrad Gesner
description: Gesner's 1558 fourth volume on fishes and aquatics — with the sea-serpent and marine monster accounts.

title: Gesner: Historiae animalium, Lib. V (de serpentium natura)
creator: Conrad Gesner
description: Gesner's posthumous 1587 fifth volume on serpents — completing the Historiae animalium.

title: A Candle in the Dark; or, A Treatise Concerning the Nature of Witches and Witchcraft
creator: Thomas Ady
description: Skeptical English treatise arguing most witchcraft accusations rest on delusion and bad evidence; a key Restoration-era anti-persecution voice.

title: Liber de grandine et tonitruis
creator: Agobard of Lyons
description: Carolingian archbishop's attack on weather-magic and the tempestarii; the earliest systematic ecclesiastical refutation of popular magic, cited for a millennium.

title: De natura daemonum libri IIII
creator: Gian Lorenzo Anania
description: Italian scholastic demonology in four books on the nature, orders and operations of demons; a Counter-Reformation summa of demon lore.

title: Miscellanies Upon Various Subjects
creator: John Aubrey
description: Aubrey's collection of apparitions, omens, dreams, second sight and witchcraft lore; the great English antiquary's folklore of the supernatural.

title: De divinatione daemonum
creator: Augustine of Hippo
description: Augustine's treatise on demonic divination: how demons predict the future and why Christians must reject their oracles; foundational for all medieval demonology.

title: The Certainty of the Worlds of Spirits
creator: Richard Baxter
description: Puritan divine's evidential defense of spirits, apparitions and witchcraft against rising skepticism; the heavyweight anti-Sadducist tract of the 1690s.

title: An Historical, Physiological and Theological Treatise of Spirits, Apparitions, Witchcrafts
creator: John Beaumont
description: Massive early-18th-century compendium defending spirits and witchcraft with hundreds of cases; the last great English demonological summa.

title: De betoverde weereld
creator: Balthasar Bekker
description: Bekker's four-book demolition of belief in demonic action in the physical world; the most radical skeptical work of the early Enlightenment, which got him defrocked.

title: A Guide to Grand-Jury Men
creator: Richard Bernard
description: Puritan minister's two-book manual for grand jurors on identifying and prosecuting witches; the standard English clerical guide to witch-finding.

title: Tractatus de confessionibus maleficorum et sagarum
creator: Peter Binsfeld
description: Trier suffragan bishop's treatise on the confessions of witches and how much faith to place in them; the leading Catholic demonology of the great persecution's peak.

title: De la démonomanie des sorciers
creator: Jean Bodin
description: Bodin's four-book Démonomanie, the most learned French demonology: a direct juridical rebuttal of Weyer that became the persecutors' handbook.

title: De magorum daemonomania (Latin, 1581)
creator: Jean Bodin (trans. Lotarius Philoponus)
description: The 1581 Basel Latin translation of Bodin's Démonomanie, which carried his demonology to learned Europe; staged as the complete Latin text (the library's existing entry is a metadata stub with no text).

title: Discours des sorciers
creator: Henri Boguet
description: The Franche-Comté judge's famous discourse on witches, drawn from his own trials; with the Instruction pour un juge en fait de sorcellerie.

title: Pandaemonium, or the Devil's Cloyster
creator: Richard Bovet
description: A further blow to modern Sadducism: apparition narratives and witchcraft cases proving spirits; Glanvill's popular successor.

title: Pseudodoxia Epidemica; or, Enquiries into Vulgar Errors
creator: Thomas Browne
description: Browne's great anatomy of error, including his famous qualified discussion of witchcraft; the physician-philosopher's skeptical method applied to popular belief.

title: Dialogus miraculorum
creator: Caesarius of Heisterbach
description: Twelve books of dialogue exempla crowded with demons, visions and marvels; the most-cited medieval story-hoard of the supernatural.

title: Canon Episcopi
creator: (canon law; transmitted by Regino of Prüm)
description: The c. 900 canon declaring the witches' night-flight an illusion of demons; the single most-cited pre-scholastic text on witchcraft, quoted for 600 years.

title: A Treatise Proving Spirits, Witches, and Supernatural Operations
creator: Meric Casaubon
description: Casaubon's learned defense of spirits and witches against skepticism, with a critique of naturalistic explanations; a Restoration churchman's demonology.

title: Reprobación de las supersticiones y hechicerías
creator: Pedro Ciruelo
description: Spanish theologian's reprobation of superstitions and sorceries; the classic Salamanca-school condemnation that shaped Spanish demonology.

title: The Mystery of Witch-craft
creator: Thomas Cooper
description: Puritan preacher's systematic uncovering of the truth, nature, occasions and growth of witchcraft; a Jacobean minister's demonology.

title: The Triall of Witch-craft
creator: John Cotta
description: Physician's skeptical method for discovering witchcraft and confuting erroneous tests (swimming, marks); the medical debunking of witch-finding.

title: The Countrey Justice
creator: Michael Dalton
description: The justices' manual whose witchcraft chapter codified English witch-procedure for a century; the legal backbone of the English witch trials.

title: De veneficis, quos olim sortilegos
creator: Lambert Daneau
description: The first French Protestant demonology: a dialogue on witches in Latin that launched the Reformed tradition of witchcraft theory.

title: A Dialogue of Witches
creator: Lambert Daneau (trans. T. T.)
description: The 1575 English translation of Daneau's dialogue, carrying Continental demonology to Elizabethan England.

title: A Detection of that sinnful, shamful, lying and ridiculous discourse of Samuel Harsnett
creator: (anonymous, pro-Darrell)
description: The rebuttal defending the dispossessions against Harsnett's attack; the other half of the great English possession controversy.

title: Errores Gazariorum
creator: (anonymous, Savoy)
description: The c. 1430 Savoyard treatise giving the first full description of the witches' sabbath; the founding document of the sabbath stereotype.
source: J. Hansen, Quellen (1901), via Internet Archive

title: An Advertisement to the Jury-Men of England Touching Witches
creator: Robert Filmer
description: Filmer's legal-skeptical tract warning juries against convicting witches on bad evidence; with his distinction of English and Hebrew witch.

title: Histoire des oracles
creator: Bernard le Bovier de Fontenelle
description: Fontenelle's elegant skeptical history of oracles, built on Van Dale; the Enlightenment's classic demolition of pagan divination.

title: Select Cases of Conscience Touching Witches and Witchcraft
creator: John Gaule
description: The Huntingdonshire minister's cases of conscience against the Hopkins witch-hunt; the first English clerical protest from inside the persecution.

title: A Dialogue Concerning Witches and Witchcrafts
creator: George Gifford
description: Gifford's dialogue exposing how the devil deceives not only witches but their accusers; the subtlest Elizabethan skeptical demonology.

title: Saducismus Triumphatus
creator: Joseph Glanvill
description: Glanvill's full and plain evidence concerning witches and apparitions; the Royal Society fellow's anti-Sadducist manifesto with the Tedworth drummer.

title: Tractatus de sortilegiis
creator: Paolo Grillandi
description: The papal judge's treatise on sorcery from the 1591 Frankfurt Tractatus duo; Italian inquisitorial demonology at its most systematic.

title: Compendium Maleficarum (Latin)
creator: Francesco Maria Guazzo
description: The 1608 Milan Latin original of Guazzo's three-book compendium of witchcraft; the library holds only the 1929 English translation, this is the Latin source text.

title: A Declaration of Egregious Popish Impostures
creator: Samuel Harsnett
description: Harsnett's exposure of Catholic exorcisms as fraud; the great English debunking of possession that Shakespeare mined for King Lear.

title: A Discovery of the Fraudulent Practises of John Darrell
creator: Samuel Harsnett
description: Harsnett's attack on the Puritan exorcist Darrell's dispossessions as counterfeit; the opening shot of the English possession controversy.

title: A Treatise Against Witchcraft
creator: Henry Holland
description: Cambridge dialogue on the greatest doubts concerning witchcraft; an early Elizabethan demonology.

title: An Historical Essay Concerning Witchcraft
creator: Francis Hutchinson
description: The first historical treatment of English witchcraft, with observations on the Salem-adjacent trials; the Enlightenment's scholarly reckoning.

title: Flagellum haereticorum fascinariorum
creator: Nicolas Jacquier
description: Jacquier's 1458 Scourge of Heretical Witches, which demolished the Canon Episcopi's skepticism and made the sabbath real; the pivot of 15th-century demonology.

title: L'incrédulité et mescréance du sortilège
creator: Pierre de Lancre
description: De Lancre's second great treatise, refuting disbelief in sorcery with apparitions, pacts and sabbaths; the Bordeaux judge's demonological summa.

title: Tableau de l'inconstance des mauvais anges et démons
creator: Pierre de Lancre
description: The Labourd witch-judge's sensational 1612 tableau of sabbaths, pacts and demonic marks; the most infamous French demonology.

title: De spectris, lemuribus et magnis atque insolitis fragoribus
creator: Ludwig Lavater
description: Lavater's Latin book on specters, lemures and strange noises; the Swiss Reformed demonology of apparitions.

title: Of Ghostes and Spirites, Walking by Night
creator: Ludwig Lavater (trans. R. H.)
description: The 1572 English translation of Lavater's book of ghosts and strange noises; Elizabethan England's favorite apparition manual.

title: Discours et histoires des spectres
creator: Pierre Le Loyer
description: Le Loyer's eight-book discourse on specters, visions and apparitions of spirits, angels, demons and souls; the French classic of apparition lore.

title: A Treatise of Specters
creator: Pierre Le Loyer (trans. Z. Jones)
description: The 1605 English translation of Le Loyer's discourse on strange sights, visions and apparitions.

title: Malleus Maleficarum (Latin, 1580)
creator: Heinrich Kramer
description: The 1580 Frankfurt Latin edition of the Hammer of Witches in three parts, with the bonus tracts of Basin, Molitor, Gerson and Murner; the library holds only the Summers English translation, this is the Latin original.

title: Christliche Erinnerung an gewaltige Regenten
creator: Johann Matthäus Meyfart
description: Lutheran theologian's Christian reminder to rulers to proceed soberly against witchcraft; the German Protestant protest that helped end the persecutions.

title: De lamiis et pythonicis mulieribus
creator: Ulrich Molitor
description: The 1498 first illustrated edition of Molitor's dialogue on witches and pythonesses; the first printed demonology with woodcuts (a later reprint is also included in the library's 1580 Malleus volume).

title: An Antidote Against Atheism
creator: Henry More
description: The Cambridge Platonist's appeal to apparitions and witchcraft as proofs of spirit against atheism; the philosophical demonology of the 1650s.

title: Formicarius
creator: Johannes Nider
description: Nider's Formicarius (the Ant-hill) in five books, from the 1602 Douai edition; the first great demonological treatise of the witch-hunt era, Kramer's chief source.

title: De la lycanthropie, transformation et extase des sorciers
creator: Jean de Nynauld
description: Nynauld's treatise on lycanthropy and the ecstasies of witches, refuting Bodin; the classic early-modern work on werewolves.

title: A Discourse of the Damned Art of Witchcraft
creator: William Perkins
description: The great Puritan theologian's discourse on witchcraft so far as revealed in Scripture; the most influential English Reformed demonology.

title: Commentarius de praecipuis divinationum generibus
creator: Kaspar Peucer
description: Melanchthon's son-in-law's commentary on the chief kinds of divination, separating diabolical arts from natural prediction; the Lutheran science of divination.

title: Les devins, ou Commentaire des principales sortes de divinations
creator: Kaspar Peucer
description: The 1584 French translation of Peucer's commentary on divination in fifteen books; the vernacular version of the Lutheran demonology of divination.

title: Strix, sive De ludificatione daemonum
creator: Gianfrancesco Pico della Mirandola
description: Pico's three-book dialogue Strix on the delusions of demons; the Italian humanist's demonology, from the 1612 edition.

title: De lamiis
creator: Gianfrancesco Ponzinibio
description: The Piacenza jurist's skeptical De lamiis, arguing flight and sabbath are illusions; the precursor Weyer built on, from the 1591 Frankfurt Tractatus duo.

title: Von Zauberey und Zauberern: Gründlicher Bericht
creator: Anton Praetorius
description: The Reformed preacher's thorough report on sorcery, opposing torture and persecution; the first German clerical voice against the witch trials.

title: De strigimagarum, daemonumque mirandis
creator: Silvestro Mazzolini (Prierias)
description: The papal theologian's three books on the marvels of witches and demons; the first Dominican demonology after the Malleus, hugely influential.

title: De operatione daemonum
creator: Michael Psellos
description: Psellos's Byzantine dialogue on the operation of demons, in Greek with Latin; Ficino's 1497 translation made it the Renaissance's demonology.

title: Libri duo de synodalibus causis et disciplinis ecclesiasticis
creator: Regino of Prüm
description: Regino's c. 906 two books on synodal cases, the transmitter of the Canon Episcopi; the foundational canon-law collection on magic and superstition (Wasserschleben's 1840 edition).

title: Daemonolatreiae libri tres
creator: Nicolas Rémy
description: Rémy's three books on demon-worship, drawn from 900 capital trials in Lorraine; the most prosecution-grounded demonology ever written.

title: A Treatise of Witchcraft
creator: Alexander Roberts
description: Roberts's treatise laying down propositions on witchcraft; a Jacobean minister's demonology.

title: Satan's Invisible World Discovered
creator: George Sinclair
description: Sinclair's choice collection of relations proving spirits, witches and apparitions; the Scottish anti-Sadducist classic.

title: Geschichte der Hexenprozesse, Band 1
creator: W. G. Soldan / H. Heppe (ed. Max Bauer)
description: Volume 1 of the classic German history of the witch trials, from antiquity through the medieval foundations; the founding modern historiography of witchcraft.

title: Geschichte der Hexenprozesse, Band 2
creator: W. G. Soldan / H. Heppe (ed. Max Bauer)
