description: Volume 2 of the classic German history of the witch trials, covering the great persecution and its decline; with trial documents.

title: Cautio Criminalis, seu De processibus contra sagas
creator: Friedrich Spee
description: The Jesuit's searing 1631 attack on witch trials and torture, written from the confessor's cell; the moral turning point of the persecution.

title: Quaestio de strigibus
creator: Bartolomeo Spina
description: The Dominican master of the sacred palace's question on witches, answering Ponzinibio's skepticism; the Counter-Reformation's scholastic defense of the sabbath's reality.

title: Psichologie, ou Traité de l'apparition des esprits
creator: Noël Taillepied
description: Taillepied's treatise on the apparition of spirits: separated souls, phantoms and prodigies; the Norman monk's demonology of ghosts.

title: De crimine magiae
creator: Christian Thomasius
description: Thomasius's inaugural theses on the crime of magic; the Halle Enlightenment's juridical demolition of witchcraft prosecution.

title: Daemonologia, sive De magia naturali, daemoniaca
creator: Francisco Torreblanca Villalpando
description: Torreblanca's four-book Daemonologia on natural, demonic, licit and illicit magic; the Spanish jurist's demonology.

title: De fascino libri tres
creator: Leonardo Vairo
description: Vairo's three books on fascination (the evil eye): its species and causes; the classic early-modern treatise on bewitchment by gaze.

title: De oraculis ethnicorum
creator: Anton van Dale
description: Van Dale's two dissertations on the heathen oracles, their duration and authors; the source Fontenelle popularized, demolishing demonic oracles.

title: The Question of Witchcraft Debated
creator: John Wagstaffe
description: Wagstaffe's discourse against the opinion of witches; the Restoration's boldest skeptical tract, answered by Glanvill's circle.

title: The Displaying of Supposed Witchcraft
creator: John Webster
description: The physician's massive debunking of supposed witchcraft by natural causes; the great Restoration skeptical summa.

title: De lamiis liber
creator: Johann Weyer
description: Weyer's 1582 book on witches, distinct from the De praestigiis (which the library holds); the physician's focused treatise on lamiae.

title: Narratives of Sorcery and Magic, Vol. 1
creator: Thomas Wright
description: Volume 1 of Wright's narratives of sorcery and magic from authentic sources; the Victorian antiquary's history of witchcraft and magic.

title: Narratives of Sorcery and Magic, Vol. 2
creator: Thomas Wright
description: Volume 2 of Wright's narratives of sorcery and magic; completing the Victorian history of witchcraft from authentic sources.

title: A Briefe Discourse of a Disease Called the Suffocation of the Mother
creator: Edward Jorden
description: Physician's 1603 argument that supposed possessions are the natural disease of hysteria; the medical text that undercut possession claims (scan OCR too poor to host; see the Internet Archive scan).

title: Grimorium Verum (French, c. 1817)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 'True Grimoire' in its classic French text — the concise Solomonic grimoire of spirits, seals, and pacts that anchored the 18th-century French grimoire trade.

title: Le Grand Grimoire (French, 19th century)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 'Red Dragon' grimoire in French — the famous pact-with-Lucifuge text that defined the black-book grimoire tradition of 19th-century France.

title: Grimoire du Pape Honorius (1670)
creator: Anonymous
description: The notorious 1670 Grimoire of Pope Honorius — the black-magic manual falsely attributed to a pope, central to the French grimoire canon.

title: Grimoire du Pape Honorius (1670, second printing)
creator: Anonymous
description: A second, textually distinct 1670 printing of the Grimoire of Pope Honorius — kept alongside the other 1670 edition because the two differ substantially in content and order.

title: Le Petit Albert (1782)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 'Little Albert' — the beloved French book of natural and cabalistic magic, secrets, and recipes; the most widely circulated French grimoire chapbook.

title: Ars Almadel (Sloane MS 3825)
creator: Anonymous
description: The Art Almadel from Sloane MS 3825 — Part IV of the Lemegeton, the theurgic art of the four chorae; transcription of the 17th-century manuscript.

title: La Vera Clavicola (Milan, 1868)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1868 Milan Italian edition of the Grimorium Verum redaction — the Italian 'True Key' tradition with its 76 sections of spirits and operations.

title: Le Grand Grimoire (c. 1750 manuscript version)
creator: Anonymous
description: A c. 1750 manuscript version of the Grand Grimoire — an earlier, textually distinct redaction of the pact-grimoire predating the 19th-century printed editions.

title: Heptameron (Turner, 1655)
creator: Peter de Abano; trans. Robert Turner
description: Robert Turner's 1655 English (with Latin) Heptameron — the classic seven-day book of planetary conjurations, the standard English Heptameron for three centuries.

title: Le Grand Albert (Paris, 1800)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1800 Paris edition of the 'Great Albert' — the French book of marvels attributed to Albertus Magnus; the elder companion to the Petit Albert.

title: La Poule Noire (The Black Pullet)
creator: Anonymous
description: The Black Pullet — the French grimoire of talismans narrated by a Napoleonic officer in Egypt; the great talismanic grimoire of the French tradition.

title: Les Véritables Clavicules de Salomon
creator: Anonymous
description: The 'True Keys of Solomon' in French — a distinct Solomonic redaction with its own spirit catalog, separate from the Mathers Key tradition.

title: Enchiridion of Pope Leo (1633)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1633 Enchiridion Leonis Papae — the famous prayer-book of Pope Leo III, the Christian protective-magic manual carried by soldiers for centuries.

title: De occulta philosophia (1533, Latin, first edition)
creator: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
description: Agrippa's Three Books of Occult Philosophy in the 1533 Cologne first edition Latin — the foundational synthesis of Renaissance magic.

title: De incertitudine et vanitate scientiarum (1564, Latin)
creator: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
description: Agrippa's 'On the Uncertainty and Vanity of the Sciences' (1564 Latin) — the great skeptical companion to his Occult Philosophy, demolishing the arts it also taught.

title: Polygraphiae libri sex (1518, Latin, first edition)
creator: Johannes Trithemius
description: Trithemius's Polygraphia (1518 first edition, Latin) — the six books of secret writing that made cryptography a science; the open companion to the Steganographia.

title: De vita libri tres (1529, Latin)
creator: Marsilio Ficino
description: Ficino's Three Books on Life (1529 Latin) — the Renaissance manual of astrological medicine and natural magic; the philosophical root of learned magic.

title: The Sixth and Seventh Books of Moses (1880)
creator: Anonymous; trans. Anonymous
description: The 1880 English Sixth and Seventh Books of Moses — the most famous American grimoire of Solomonic seals; the backbone of Pennsylvania Dutch pow-wow magic.

title: The Long-Lost Friend (Hohman, 1850)
creator: John George Hohman
description: Hohman's 1850 Long-Lost Friend — the classic Pennsylvania Dutch pow-wow grimoire of charms and cures; the living folk-magic tradition of German America.

title: Hocus Pocus Junior: The Anatomy of Legerdemain (1658)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1658 fifth edition of Hocus Pocus Junior (orig. 1634) — the first English book of conjuring; origin of the phrase 'hocus pocus.'

title: The Count of Gabalis (1680)
creator: Nicolas-Pierre-Henri de Montfaucon de Villars
description: The 1680 English Count of Gabalis — Villars's Rosicrucian dialogue on elemental spirits; the founding text of occult elemental lore.

title: A True and Faithful Relation (Casaubon, 1659)
creator: John Dee; ed. Meric Casaubon
description: Casaubon's 1659 True and Faithful Relation — the printed record of Dee and Kelley's angelic conversations; the source text of Enochian magic.

title: Secretum Secretorum (Bologna, 1501, Latin)
creator: Pseudo-Aristotle
description: The 1501 Bologna Latin Secretum Secretorum — the pseudo-Aristotelian 'Secret of Secrets'; the medieval mirror-of-princes with its talismanic lore.

title: Epistola de secretis operibus artis et naturae (1618, Latin)
creator: Roger Bacon; ed. John Dee
description: Bacon's Letter on the Secret Works of Art and Nature (1618, ed. John Dee, Latin) — the famous epistle on marvels, magic, and natural philosophy.

title: The Sacred Magic of Abramelin the Mage: Book Three (Mathers, 1900)
creator: Abraham of Worms; trans. S. L. MacGregor Mathers
description: Book Three of the Mathers Abramelin (1900) — the book of magic squares; completes the three-book Mathers Abramelin in the library.

title: De Magia (Bruno, Latin)
creator: Giordano Bruno
description: Bruno's De Magia (Latin) — the systematic treatise on magical bonds and the magic of attraction; the philosophical peak of Renaissance magic theory.

title: Ars Paulina (Lemegeton, Part III)
creator: Anonymous
description: The Art Pauline from Sloane MS 3825 — Part III of the Lemegeton, the art of the spirits of the hours; transcription of the 17th-century manuscript.

title: The Clavicle of Solomon (Sloane MS 3847, 1572)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1572 Sloane MS 3847 Clavicle of Solomon — one of the earliest English Key manuscripts; a complete two-book Key predating Mathers by three centuries.

title: De naturalium effectuum causis, sive de incantationibus (1556, Latin)
creator: Pietro Pomponazzi
description: Pomponazzi's On Incantations (1556 Latin) — the great naturalistic critique of magic; pivotal for demonology and the philosophy of magic.

title: Propaedeumata Aphoristica (1558, Latin)
creator: John Dee
description: Dee's Propaedeumata Aphoristica (1558 first edition, Latin) — the astrological-physical aphorisms; key to Dee's natural magic.

title: The Regius Manuscript (c. 1390)
creator: Anonymous
description: The oldest known Masonic document — a Middle-English verse rendering of the Old Charges of operative masonry, the root text of the entire speculative tradition.
source: Mastermason.com (VLER transcription); v.167 restored from Internet Archive scan

title: The Matthew Cooke Manuscript (c. 1450)
creator: Anonymous
description: Second-oldest of the Masonic Old Charges (Gothic Constitutions), the bridge text between the Regius poem and the later speculative ritual tradition.

title: Fama Fraternitatis, oder Entdeckung der Brüderschafft des löblichen Ordens deß Rosen Creutzes (Frankfurt, 1615)
creator: Johann Valentin Andreae (attributed)
description: The two founding manifestos of Rosicrucianism in their original German — the Fama and Confessio that ignited the 17th-century Rosicrucian furore across Europe.

title: Chymische Hochzeit Christiani Rosencreutz anno 1459 (Strasbourg, 1616)
creator: Johann Valentin Andreae
description: The third Rosicrucian manifesto in its original German first edition — Andreae's alchemical allegory that completes the founding Rosicrucian trilogy.

title: Schutzschrift für die Aechtheit der Rosenkreutzergesellschaft (Leipzig, 1782)
creator: Robert Fludd
description: German translation of Fludd's 1617 Tractatus Apologeticus — the English Rosicrucian apologist's defense of the Fraternity, the pivotal English reply to the manifestos.

title: Symbola Aureae Mensae Duodecim Nationum (Frankfurt, 1617)
creator: Michael Maier
description: Maier's emblematic survey of twelve alchemical nations — the most lavishly illustrated Rosicrucian work, the visual canon of the movement's alchemical program.

title: Themis Aurea: The Laws of the Fraternity of the Rosie Crosse (London, 1656)
creator: Michael Maier (translated by N. L.)
description: The first English translation of Maier's 1618 laws of the Rosicrucian fraternity — the document that carried Rosicrucian organization theory into England.

title: Lumen de Lumine: or, A New Magicall Light (London, 1651)
creator: Thomas Vaughan (Eugenius Philalethes)
description: Vaughan's English Rosicrucian magic — the foundational text of the English Rosicrucian revival, written as Philalethes at the height of the Interregnum occult ferment.

title: The Holy Guide, Leading the Way to the Wonder of the World (London, 1662)
creator: John Heydon
description: Heydon's massive Rosicrucian compendium — astrology, geomancy, and Rosie-Crucian physic, the most encyclopedic English Rosicrucian work of the 17th century.

title: The Rosie Crucian Infallible Axiomata (London, 1660)
creator: John Heydon
description: Heydon's 1660 Rosicrucian rule-book of general axioms — the Restoration-era statement of Rosie-Crucian doctrine in its most concentrated form.

title: Theomagia, or the Temple of Wisdome (London, 1664)
creator: John Heydon
description: Heydon's three-part temple of wisdom — spiritual, celestial, and elemental magic, the culminating system of his Rosicrucian writings.

title: Le Comte de Gabalis, ou Entretiens sur les sciences secrètes (Paris, 1670)
creator: Abbé N. de Montfaucon de Villars
description: The witty French dialogues on elemental spirits that fixed the Rosicrucian image in French letters — the bridge text between Rosicrucianism and the 18th-century French occult revival.

title: Secret Symbols of the Rosicrucians of the 16th and 17th Centuries (Boston, 1888)
creator: Franz Hartmann
description: Hartmann's 1888 collection of Rosicrucian plates with commentary — the visual source-book through which the 19th-century occult revival received the Rosicrucian emblem tradition.

title: Masonry Dissected (London, 1730)
creator: Samuel Prichard
description: The first and most famous Masonic exposé — Prichard's 1730 catechism of the three degrees, the founding document of Masonic exposure literature and the era's best evidence for early ritual.

title: The Perjur'd Free Mason Detected (London, 1730)
creator: Anonymous ("By a Free Mason")
description: A 1730 anti-exposé answering Prichard — the earliest Masonic counter-pamphlet, pivotal as the fraternity's first printed self-defense.

title: The New Book of Constitutions of the Antient and Honourable Fraternity of Free and Accepted Masons (London, 1738)
creator: James Anderson
description: Anderson's rewritten second edition of Freemasonry's founding constitutional document — substantially recast from 1723 with new history and charges; the live library holds the 1723 first edition only.

title: Ahiman Rezon: or, A Help to a Brother (London, 1756)
creator: Laurence Dermott
description: The complete 1756 first edition of the Antients' rival constitution — Dermott's founding charter of Antient Freemasonry, the other half of the 18th-century Masonic schism; the live library holds only an abridged text.

title: The Free-Masons Accusation and Defence (London, 1726)
creator: Anonymous
description: Six genuine letters for and against the Craft from 1726 — the earliest printed controversy over Freemasonry, predating Prichard's exposé by four years.

title: Mahhabone: or, the Grand Lodge Door Open'd (London, 1766)
creator: Anonymous
description: A 1766 exposé of the three Craft degrees with the Royal Arch — pivotal as early printed evidence for the Royal Arch degree's working in the 1760s.

title: Shibboleth: or, Every Man a Free-Mason (London, 1765)
creator: Anonymous ("Pass'd Master")
description: A 1765 self-initiation manual — the exposé genre's turning point, promising readers they could become Masons without a lodge.

title: Solomon in All His Glory: or, the Master-Mason (London, 1768)
creator: Anonymous ("Thomas Wilson, Master of a Lodge")
description: A 1768 exposé focused on the Master Mason degree — key evidence for the Hiramic legend's ritual form in the 1760s.

title: Hiram; or, the Grand Master-Key (London, 1766)
creator: Anonymous ("A Member of the Royal Arch")
description: The 1766 'Grand Master-Key' exposé covering Antient and Modern masonry — a pivotal witness to the rival rituals of the Masonic schism.

title: Jachin and Boaz; or, An Authentic Key to the Door of Free-Masonry (1812)
creator: Anonymous
description: The most reprinted Masonic exposé of all — this 1812 reprint represents the text that defined public knowledge of Masonic ritual for over a century after its 1762 debut.

title: A Free-Mason's Answer to the Suspected Author of Jachin and Boaz (London, 1762)
creator: Anonymous
description: The immediate 1762 Masonic reply to Jachin and Boaz — the fraternity's contemporary rebuttal to its most damaging exposé.

title: The Three Distinct Knocks; or, the Door of the Most Antient Free-Masonry (Dublin, 1785)
creator: Anonymous
description: The great Irish exposé in its 1785 Dublin reprint — the fullest 18th-century printed ritual of the three degrees, from the original 1760 London edition.

title: The Spirit of Masonry, in Moral and Elucidatory Lectures (London, 1775)
creator: William Hutchinson
description: Hutchinson's 1775 moral lectures — the founding text of Masonic philosophical apologetics, which recast the Craft as a system of morality for a skeptical age.

title: A Candid Disquisition of the Principles and Practices of the Most Ancient and Honourable Society of Free and Accepted Masons (London, 1769)
creator: Wellins Calcott
description: Calcott's 1769 defense of the Craft — the most widely circulated Masonic apology of the 18th century, answering the charge that Masonry was mere conviviality.

title: The Use and Abuse of Free-Masonry (London, 1783)
creator: George Smith (Captain)
description: Captain Smith's 1783 treatise distinguishing true from false Masonry — a pivotal insider's critique that shaped the reform discourse of late-18th-century English lodges.

title: The Freemason's Monitor; or, Illustrations of Masonry (Boston, 1797)
creator: Thomas Smith Webb
description: The 1797 first edition of Webb's Monitor — the founding ritual book of American Freemasonry, which standardized the Preston-Webb lectures across the United States.

title: Discours prononcé à la réception des Francs-maçons (1737)
creator: Andrew Michael Ramsay
description: Ramsay's 1737 oration before the Paris lodge — the founding charter of the Templar myth in Freemasonry, source of the high degrees and the Strict Observance.

title: L'Ordre des Francs-Maçons trahi (1745)
creator: Gabriel-Louis Calabre Pérau
description: Pérau's 1745 French exposé — the first printed revelation of French Masonic ritual, the continental counterpart to Prichard.

title: Des Erreurs et de la Vérité (1775)
creator: Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin
description: Saint-Martin's first book, published as 'the Unknown Philosopher' — the founding text of Martinism, which carried the theosophic current into French high-degree Masonry.

title: Tableau naturel des rapports qui existent entre Dieu, l'homme et l'univers (1782)
creator: Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin
description: Saint-Martin's 1782 natural tableau of God, man, and universe — the mature statement of Martinist theosophy, cornerstone of the French esoteric revival.

title: Memorial, or Brief, for the Comte de Cagliostro (London, 1786)
creator: Alessandro, Count di Cagliostro
description: Cagliostro's 1786 memorial from the Affair of the Diamond Necklace — the primary document of the most notorious occultist of the 18th century at his moment of trial.

title: Einige Originalschriften des Illuminatenordens (München, 1787)
creator: Adam Weishaupt (order papers seized by the Bavarian government)
description: The Bavarian government's 1787 publication of seized Illuminati papers — the foundational documentary source for the real history of the Illuminatenorden.

title: Nachtrag von weitern Originalschriften, welche die Illuminatensekte überhaupt betreffen (München, 1787)
creator: Bavarian government (ed.)
description: The 1787 supplement of further seized Illuminati writings — completes the documentary record of the order's suppression with Zwackh's and other papers.

title: Apologie der Illuminaten (Frankfurt/Leipzig, 1786)
creator: Adam Weishaupt
description: Weishaupt's 1786 apologia for the Illuminati — his own defense of the order's aims, the indispensable counterpart to the hostile seized-papers publications.

title: Das verbesserte System der Illuminaten (Frankfurt/Leipzig, 1787)
creator: Adam Weishaupt
description: Weishaupt's 1787 revised system of the Illuminati — his definitive statement of the order's graded structure after the Bavarian suppression.

title: Kurze Rechtfertigung meiner Absichten (1787)
creator: Adam Weishaupt
description: Weishaupt's short 1787 justification of his intentions — his most personal reply to the charges published from the seized papers.

title: Pythagoras, oder Betrachtungen über die geheime Welt- und Regierungs-Kunst, Bd. 1 (Frankfurt/Leipzig, 1790)
creator: Adam Weishaupt
description: Weishaupt's 1790 Pythagoras — his philosophy of secret government and world-craft, the theoretical summa of Illuminati political thought.

title: Philo's endliche Erklärung und Antwort (Hannover, 1788)
creator: Adolph von Knigge
description: Knigge's 1788 final declaration and break with Weishaupt — the primary document of the Illuminati's internal schism, told by the order's great organizer.

title: Die neuesten Arbeiten des Spartacus und Philo in dem Illuminaten-Orden (1794)
creator: Adam Weishaupt and Adolph von Knigge (published from seized correspondence)
description: The 1794 publication of the latest workings of 'Spartacus' (Weishaupt) and 'Philo' (Knigge) — the documentary climax of the Illuminati papers affair.

title: System und Folgen des Illuminatenordens (München, 1787)
creator: Bavarian government (ed.)
description: The Munich 1787 exposé of the Illuminati's system and consequences — the government's interpretive companion to the seized Originalschriften.

title: Illuminatus Dirigens, oder Schottischer Ritter (1794)
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1794 ritual of the Illuminatus Dirigens (Scottish Knight) degree — rare printed evidence of the Illuminati's higher-degree workings.

title: Mémoires pour servir à l'histoire du Jacobinisme, Tome 1 (Hambourg, 1798)
creator: Augustin Barruel
description: Tome 1 of Barruel's Memoirs — the conspiracy of the 'Sophists of impiety' against altar and throne; the founding text of modern conspiracism and the Illuminati myth.

title: Mémoires pour servir à l'histoire du Jacobinisme, Tome 2 (Hambourg, 1798)
creator: Augustin Barruel
description: Tome 2 of Barruel's Memoirs — the conspiracy against sovereigns and the Sophists of rebellion; completes the anti-philosophe half of the great conspiracy narrative.

title: Mémoires pour servir à l'histoire du Jacobinisme, Tome 3 (Hambourg, 1798)
creator: Augustin Barruel
description: Tome 3 of Barruel's Memoirs — the conspiracy of the Freemasons proper, the volume that fused Illuminati, Masonry, and revolution into a single myth.

title: Mémoires pour servir à l'histoire du Jacobinisme, Tome 4 (Londres, 1798)
creator: Augustin Barruel
description: Tome 4 of Barruel's Memoirs — the Jacobin lodges and the Germanic illuminés; the volume that carried the conspiracy thesis into the 19th century.

title: Narratives of the Witchcraft Cases, 1648-1706
creator: George Lincoln Burr (ed.)
description: The standard documentary anthology of New England witchcraft, gathering 14 primary narratives from 1648 to 1706 in one volume.

title: The Witchcraft Delusion in New England, Vol. 1
creator: Samuel G. Drake (ed.)
description: Reprints Cotton Mather's Wonders of the Invisible World (1693) verbatim with a historical introduction, preserving the key Salem prosecution text.

title: The Witchcraft Delusion in New England, Vol. 2
creator: Samuel G. Drake (ed.)
description: Reprints Robert Calef's More Wonders of the Invisible World (1700), the contemporary rebuttal to Mather's Salem account.

title: The Witchcraft Delusion in New England, Vol. 3
creator: Samuel G. Drake (ed.)
description: Completes Drake's documentary set with further Salem-era tracts and records of the New England witchcraft cases.

title: A Modest Enquiry into the Nature of Witchcraft
creator: John Hale
description: The recanting Salem minister's 1702 examination of the trials, the first insider's critique of the 1692 proceedings.

title: The Wonderfull Discoverie of Witches in the Countie of Lancaster
creator: Thomas Potts
description: The official clerk's full account of the 1612 Pendle witch trials, the most famous English witch-trial record.

title: The Examination and Confession of Certaine Wytches at Chelmsford
creator: Anonymous
description: The first English witch-trial pamphlet, recording the 1566 Chelmsford examinations that set the template for all later ones.

title: A Detection of Damnable Driftes Practized by Three Witches at Chelmsford
creator: Anonymous
description: Records the 1579 Chelmsford witch trials, a key early Elizabethan prosecution pamphlet.

title: The Apprehension and Confession of Three Notorious Witches at Chelmsford
creator: Anonymous
description: Documents the 1589 Chelmsford trials, continuing the landmark Essex prosecution series.

title: A Rehearsall both Straung and True, of Heinous Actes by Elizabeth Stile
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1579 Abingdon/Windsor witch trial pamphlet recording Elizabeth Stile's examination and confession.

title: Newes from Scotland, Declaring the Damnable Life and Death of Doctor Fian
creator: Anonymous
description: The contemporary pamphlet on the 1590-91 North Berwick witch trials, the first major Scottish witch hunt.

title: The Witches of Northamptonshire
creator: Anonymous
description: Records the 1612 Northamptonshire witch trials of Agnes Browne and others, a major Jacobean prosecution.

title: The Lawes against Witches and Coniuration
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1645 statute pamphlet published at the height of the Hopkins witch-hunt, the legal basis for the East Anglian trials.

title: The Wonderfull Discoverie of Elizabeth Sawyer, a Witch Late of Edmonton
creator: Anonymous
description: The trial pamphlet for Elizabeth Sawyer, the Edmonton witch executed in 1621, later dramatized in The Witch of Edmonton.

title: A True and Just Recorde of the Information, Examination and Confession of All the Witches Taken at S. Oses
creator: Anonymous
description: The full record of the 1582 St Osyth witch trials, the largest Elizabethan witch prosecution and a landmark documentary source.

title: The Examination of John Walsh
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1566 examination of John Walsh of Dorchester before the commissary, a rare early sorcery interrogation.

title: Witches Apprehended, Examined and Executed
creator: Anonymous
description: Records the 1613 Bedford witch trial with a contemporary guide to detecting witches, a Jacobean prosecution pamphlet.

title: The Most Wonderfull and True Storie of Alice Gooderige of Stapenhill
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1597 pamphlet on Alice Gooderidge of Stapenhill, an Elizabethan witch trial with full examinations.

title: A True Discourse Declaring the Damnable Life and Death of Stubbe Peeter
creator: Anonymous
description: The English pamphlet on Peter Stumpp, the 'Werewolf of Bedburg' executed in 1589, the most famous lycanthropy trial.

title: An Account of the Tryal and Examination of Joan Buts
creator: Anonymous
description: A 1682 witch-trial broadside recording Joan Buts's examination and acquittal, a rare late acquittal document.

title: The Life and Death of Lewis Gaufredy
creator: Anonymous
description: The English account of Louis Gaufridy, the Aix-en-Provence priest executed for witchcraft in 1611, a landmark French case.

title: The Most Strange and Admirable Discoverie of the Three Witches of Warboys
creator: Anonymous
description: The full 1593 pamphlet on the Warboys witch trial, the best-documented Elizabethan witchcraft prosecution.

title: The Witches of Huntingdon, Their Examinations and Confessions
creator: Anonymous
description: Records the 1646 Huntingdon witch examinations during the Hopkins panic, a key East Anglian trial document.

title: A Tryal of Witches at Bury St. Edmonds
creator: Anonymous
description: The report of the 1664 Bury St Edmunds trial of Amy Duny and Rose Cullender before Hale, the most cited English witch trial.

title: A Full and True Account of the Proceedings at the Old Bailey, June 1682
creator: Anonymous
description: Old Bailey sessions report including the 1682 trial of Jane Kent for witchcraft, a late London prosecution record.

title: The Full Tryals of Four Notorious Witches at Worcester, 1690
creator: Anonymous
description: Records the 1690 Worcester assizes witch trial with confessions and dying speeches, a late Stuart prosecution.

title: The Tryal, Condemnation, and Execution of Three Witches at Bideford, 1682
creator: Anonymous
description: The trial pamphlet for the 1682 Bideford witches, the last witch executions in England.

title: A True and Impartial Relation of the Informations against Three Witches at Bideford
creator: Anonymous
description: A fuller contemporary relation of the 1682 Bideford witch trial, complementing the shorter tryal pamphlet.

title: Witchcraft Discovered and Punished: A Ballad of the Bideford Witches
creator: Anonymous
description: A contemporary street ballad on the 1682 Bideford witch trial, showing popular reception of the last English executions.

title: The Examination, Confession, Triall, and Execution of Joane Williford and Joan Cariden, 1645
creator: Anonymous
description: Records the 1645 Kent witch trial of Williford and Cariden during the Hopkins panic, with examinations and confessions.

title: A Prodigious and Tragicall History of Six Witches at Maidstone, 1652
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1652 Maidstone assizes report on six condemned witches, a major Interregnum trial document.

title: The Witch of Wapping
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1652 pamphlet on the Witch of Wapping case, a London witchcraft prosecution with full relation.

title: A Declaration in Answer to Pamphlets concerning the Witch of Wapping
creator: Anonymous
description: A rebuttal pamphlet defending against false reports of the Wapping witch case, a rare contemporary controversy document.

title: A Relation of the Diabolical Practices of the Witches of Renfrewshire, 1697
creator: Anonymous
description: The official relation of the 1697 Renfrewshire (Paisley) witch trials, the last major Scottish witch prosecution.

title: Relation of the Proceedings at the Northampton Assizes, 1674
creator: Anonymous
description: Reports the 1674 Northampton assizes including the trial of Mary Forster for witchcraft, with confession and execution.

title: A Further Account of the Tryals of the New-England Witches, 1693
creator: Anonymous
description: A 1693 London pamphlet on the Salem trials with Increase Mather's Cases of Conscience, the key contemporary English account.

title: Sadducismus Debellatus: The Bargarran Witchcrafts, 1696-1697
creator: Anonymous
description: The documentary narrative of the Bargarran/Renfrewshire witchcrafts of 1696-97, the evidentiary basis for the Paisley trials.

title: A Collection of Modern Relations concerning Witches and Witchcraft, 1693
creator: Matthew Hale (attrib.)
description: Collects modern witchcraft cases with Hale's meditation on the Bury St Edmunds trial, linking England's two most famous trials.

title: Witchcrafts, Strange and Wonderfull: Seven Witches, 1635
creator: Anonymous
description: A 1635 pamphlet on seven witches practicing against noble personages, a Caroline-era prosecution with a detection guide.

title: The Wonderfull and True Relation of the Bewitching of a Young Girle in Ireland, 1699
creator: Daniel Higgs
description: A 1699 Irish witchcraft relation with a cure receipt, a rare contemporary Irish trial-adjacent document.

title: Le Dossier de l'Affaire des Templiers
creator: Georges Lizerand
description: The standard documentary dossier of the Templar affair, assembling the arrest order, interrogations, and suppression acts.

title: Der Untergang des Templer-Ordens, Vol. 1
creator: Konrad Schottmuller
description: The great 19th-century documentary history of the Templar trial's downfall, volume 1: narrative from the sources.

title: Der Untergang des Templer-Ordens, Vol. 2: Urkunden
creator: Konrad Schottmuller
description: The companion Urkunden volume publishing the Templar trial documents themselves, the documentary core of Schottmuller's work.

title: Proces de Condamnation et de Rehabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, Vol. 1
creator: Jules Quicherat (ed.)
description: Volume 1 of the definitive edition of Joan of Arc's 1431 condemnation trial, publishing the Latin trial text.

title: Proces de Condamnation et de Rehabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, Vol. 2
creator: Jules Quicherat (ed.)
description: Volume 2 of Quicherat's edition, continuing the trial documents and opening the rehabilitation proceedings.

title: Proces de Condamnation et de Rehabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, Vol. 3
creator: Jules Quicherat (ed.)
description: Volume 3 of Quicherat's edition, with the rehabilitation trial testimony of 1455-56.

title: Proces de Condamnation et de Rehabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, Vol. 4
creator: Jules Quicherat (ed.)
description: Volume 4 of Quicherat's edition, with further rehabilitation documents and contemporary chronicles.

title: Proces de Condamnation et de Rehabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, Vol. 5
creator: Jules Quicherat (ed.)
description: Volume 5 of Quicherat's edition, completing the documentary record with opinions, letters, and the index.

title: Gilles de Rais, Marechal de France, dit Barbe-Bleue
creator: Eugene Bossard
description: The documentary biography of Gilles de Rais with the full 1440 trial pieces justificatives, the essential Bluebeard trial record.

title: Ancient Criminal Trials in Scotland, Vol. 1
creator: Robert Pitcairn (ed.)
description: Volume 1 (1488-1596) of the great collection of Scottish criminal trials, including the North Berwick witch trials.

title: Ancient Criminal Trials in Scotland, Vol. 2
creator: Robert Pitcairn (ed.)
description: Volume 2 (1596-1609) of Pitcairn's Scottish criminal trials, continuing the justiciary records.

title: Ancient Criminal Trials in Scotland, Vol. 3
creator: Robert Pitcairn (ed.)
description: Volume 3 (1609-1624) of Pitcairn's Scottish criminal trials, completing the continuous 1488-1624 series.

title: Verzeichnis der Hexen-Leut zu Wuerzburg, 1629
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1629 printed list of 157 witches burned at Wuerzburg, the most chilling single document of the German witch hunts.

title: HexenVerbrennung Bistum Wuertzburg Bamberg, 1627
creator: Anonymous
description: A 1627 pamphlet on the witch burnings in the bishoprics of Wuerzburg and Bamberg, contemporary German trial reportage.

title: The Letters of John Hus
creator: Herbert B. Workman and R. Martin Pope (trans.)
description: The complete English correspondence of Jan Hus including his Constance captivity letters, the key documentary record of his trial.

title: Trioedd Ynys Prydein: The Welsh Triads (Skene 1868; Rhys & Evans 1887)
creator: Anonymous (trans. William F. Skene; John Rhys & J. Gwenogvryn Evans)
description: The Welsh Triads in two public-domain Victorian translations, substituting the unobtainable Bromwich edition.

title: Erec (Haupt 1871)
creator: Hartmann von Aue (ed. Moriz Haupt)
description: Hartmann von Aue's Erec in Haupt's 1871 MHG edition, complete (vv.1-10135).

title: Iwein (Benecke/Lachmann/Wolff)
creator: Hartmann von Aue (ed. Benecke, Lachmann, Wolff)
description: Hartmann's Iwein in the Benecke/Lachmann MHG edition, complete (vv.1-8165).

title: Wigalois (Pfeiffer 1847)
creator: Wirnt von Grafenberg (ed. Franz Pfeiffer)
description: Wirnt von Grafenberg's Wigalois in Pfeiffer's 1847 MHG edition, complete.

title: Lanzelet (Hahn 1845)
creator: Ulrich von Zatzikhoven (ed. K.A. Hahn)
description: Ulrich von Zatzikhoven's Lanzelet in Hahn's 1845 MHG edition, complete (~9,440 vv).

title: Jaufre (Breuer 1925 Occitan edition)
creator: Anonymous (ed. Hermann Breuer)
description: The Occitan romance Jaufre in Breuer's 1925 critical edition, complete (vv.1-10955).

title: Le Bel Inconnu (Williams 1915)
creator: Renaut de Beaujeu (ed. Hugh Williams)
description: Renaut de Beaujeu's Le Bel Inconnu in Williams's 1915 Old French edition, complete (6,266 vv).

title: Sir Libeaus Desconus (Weston 1902)
creator: Anonymous (trans. Jessie L. Weston)
description: Lybeaus Desconus in Weston's 1902 English prose rendering, complete.

title: The Trial of Jeanne d'Arc (Murray 1902)
creator: T. Douglas Murray (trans.)
description: The condemnation trial (1431) and rehabilitation (1450-56) in Murray's 1902 English translation.

title: Peter of Vaux-de-Cernay: Historia Albigensium (1615 Latin edition)
creator: Peter of Vaux-de-Cernay
description: Vaux-de-Cernay's eyewitness history of the Albigensian Crusade in the 1615 Latin edition.

title: William of Puylaurens: Chronicle of the Albigensian War (Du Mege 1864)
creator: William of Puylaurens (trans. Du Mege)
description: Puylaurens's chronicle (1202-1272) in Du Mege's 1864 French translation, complete.

title: The Alliterative Morte Arthure (Halliwell 1847)
creator: Anonymous (ed. James O. Halliwell)
description: The Alliterative Morte Arthure in Halliwell's 1847 Middle English edition, complete.

title: Robert de Boron: Le Roman du Saint-Graal (Michel 1841)
creator: Robert de Boron (ed. Francisque Michel)
description: Robert de Boron's Joseph d'Arimathie and Merlin in Michel's 1841 Old French edition.

title: Varro on Farming (De Re Rustica)
creator: Marcus Terentius Varro (Lloyd Storr-Best, trans.)
description: Storr-Best's 1912 English rendering of Varro's De Re Rustica, the foundational Roman treatise on agriculture — the public-domain substitute for the Loeb edition.

title: Columella of Husbandry (De Re Rustica)
creator: Lucius Junius Moderatus Columella (trans. 1745)
description: The 1745 English rendering of Columella's twelve books on husbandry — the earliest complete English Columella, public-domain substitute for the Loeb.

title: Cato on Farming (De Agri Cultura)
creator: Marcus Porcius Cato (Fairfax Harrison, trans.)
description: Harrison's 1913 English rendering of Cato's De Agri Cultura, the oldest surviving Latin prose work — public-domain substitute for the Loeb.

title: The Five Books of M. Manilius (Astronomica)
creator: Marcus Manilius (Thomas Creech, trans.)
description: Creech's 1697 English rendering of Manilius's Astronomica, the great Roman astrological poem — public-domain substitute for the Goold Loeb.

title: Theon of Smyrna: Mathematics Useful for Understanding Plato
creator: Theon of Smyrna (J. Dupuis, ed./trans.)
description: Dupuis's 1892 Greek-French edition of Theon's mathematical introduction to Plato — public-domain substitute for the Lawlor translation.

title: Eratosthenica: The Fragments of Eratosthenes
creator: Eratosthenes (G. Bernhardy, ed.)
description: Bernhardy's 1822 collection of Eratosthenes's surviving fragments, the foundation for all study of his lost Geography — public-domain substitute for Roller's edition.

title: Pomponius Mela: De Chorographia
creator: Pomponius Mela (C. Frick, ed.)
description: Frick's 1880 Teubner Latin text of Mela's Description of the World, the earliest surviving Latin geography — public-domain substitute for Romer's translation.

title: Ptolemy's Almagest (Manitius German Translation)
creator: Claudius Ptolemy (Karl Manitius, trans.)
description: Manitius's 1912-13 German rendering of the complete Almagest, the great ancient work of mathematical astronomy — public-domain substitute for Toomer's translation.

title: Claudii Ptolemaei Geographia (Nobbe)
creator: Claudius Ptolemy (C. F. A. Nobbe, ed.)
description: Nobbe's 1843-45 Greek edition of Ptolemy's Geography in three volumes — public-domain substitute for Stevenson's translation.

title: The Pyramid Texts (Maspero 1894)
creator: Gaston Maspero (trans.)
description: Maspero's 1894 French rendering, the first complete translation of the ancient Egyptian Pyramid Texts — public-domain substitute for Faulkner's.

title: Le Mahavastu, Tome 1 (Senart)
creator: Émile Senart (ed.)
description: Senart's pioneering edition of the Mahavastu, the great Buddhist Sanskrit 'Great Story', volume one — public-domain substitute for Jones's translation.

title: Le Mahavastu, Tome 2 (Senart)
creator: Émile Senart (ed.)
description: Senart's pioneering edition of the Mahavastu, volume two — public-domain substitute for Jones's translation.

title: Le Mahavastu, Tome 3 (Senart)
creator: Émile Senart (ed.)
description: Senart's pioneering edition of the Mahavastu, volume three — public-domain substitute for Jones's translation.

title: Geminus: Elementa Astronomiae (Manitius 1898)
creator: Geminus (K. Manitius, ed.)
description: Manitius's 1898 Teubner Greek text of Geminus's Introduction to Astronomy — public-domain substitute for Evans and Berggren's translation.

title: Athenaeus Mechanicus: On Machines (Wescher 1867)
creator: Athenaeus Mechanicus (C. Wescher, ed./trans.)
description: Wescher's 1867 Greek-French edition of the Greek writers on siege warfare, containing the complete text of Athenaeus Mechanicus's On Machines — public-domain substitute for Whitehead and Blyth.

title: Firmicus Maternus: Mathesis (1551)
creator: Julius Firmicus Maternus
description: The 1551 Latin edition of Firmicus's Mathesis, the great Roman astrological handbook — public-domain substitute for Bram's translation.

title: Dioscorides: De Materia Medica (Berendes 1902)
creator: Pedanius Dioscorides (Julius Berendes, trans.)
description: Berendes's 1902 German rendering of Dioscorides's De Materia Medica, the foundational ancient pharmacology — public-domain substitute for Osbaldeston's translation.

title: Aelian: On Animals and Historical Miscellany (Hercher 1858)
creator: Claudius Aelianus (R. Hercher, ed.)
description: Hercher's 1858 Didot edition of Aelian's complete surviving works — On Animals (17 books), Historical Miscellany, letters and fragments — public-domain substitute for the Scholfield and Wilson Loebs.

title: On the Track of Unknown Animals (Heuvelmans, 1958)
creator: Bernard Heuvelmans (Richard Garnett, trans.)
description: The founding text of cryptozoology: Heuvelmans' worldwide survey of unknown and out-of-place animals in seven parts and nineteen chapters — from the orang-pendek and the yeti to sea serpents and the mammoth of the taiga — in Richard Garnett's 1958 English translation, public domain.

title: Abominable Snowmen: Legend Come to Life (Sanderson, 1961)
creator: Ivan T. Sanderson
description: The first major English survey of yeti/sasquatch evidence: fourteen chapters of case reports from five continents plus appendices on footprint analysis and Himalayan fauna — Ivan T. Sanderson's 1961 classic, public domain.

title: F. von Bellingshausens Forschungsfahrten im Südlichen Eismeer, 1819–1821 (1902)
creator: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen
description: The German edition (1902, public domain) of Bellingshausen's account of the 1819–1821 Russian Antarctic expedition — the voyage that first sighted the Antarctic continent — in six chapters from Kronstadt to the homecoming.

title: Ginza Rba — The Great Treasure of the Mandaeans (Mark Lidzbarski German translation, 1925)
creator: Anonymous Mandaean sages / Mark Lidzbarski (translator)
description: The complete Ginza Rba (Great Treasure), holy book of Mandaeism, in Lidzbarski's 1925 German translation — the standard scholarly version, public domain; includes the Mandaean creation story.

title: The Popol Vuh: The Mythic and Heroic Sagas of the Kiches (Lewis Spence, 1908)
creator: Anonymous K'iche' Maya / Lewis Spence (rendering)
description: The Maya book of creation and the Hero Twins in Lewis Spence's 1908 English rendering — the classic public-domain version; the single most important native text of the Americas.

title: The Ascension of Isaiah (R. H. Charles translation, 1900)
creator: Anonymous (early Christian pseudepigraphon) / R. H. Charles (translator)
description: The ancient martyrdom-and-vision text — Isaiah's ascent through the seven heavens — in R. H. Charles's 1900 standard English translation, public domain.

title: The Oxyrhynchus Sayings of Jesus — Greek Fragments of the Gospel of Thomas (Grenfell and Hunt, 1904)
creator: Anonymous (early Christian) / Grenfell and Hunt (editors)
description: The earliest-attested sayings of the Gospel of Thomas — the Greek Oxyrhynchus papyrus fragments with English translations (1904); the only public-domain edition of the Thomas material.

title: The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, Vol. II: Pseudepigrapha (R. H. Charles, ed., 1913)
creator: R. H. Charles (editor)
description: R. H. Charles's landmark 1913 English edition of the Old Testament Pseudepigrapha — Jubilees, 1–2 Enoch, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs, 2–3 Baruch, 4 Ezra, Psalms of Solomon, and more — the public-domain predecessor to Charlesworth's volume, staged as its substitute.

title: The Religion of the Samurai
creator: Kaiten Nukariya
description: Kaiten Nukariya's The Religion of the Samurai: A Study of Zen Philosophy and Discipline in China and Japan (1913) — the pioneering English exposition of Zen by a Japanese Soto scholar; substituted for the unlocatable 1899 Nukariya entry.

title: Ancient Times: A History of the Early World
creator: James Henry Breasted
description: James Henry Breasted's Ancient Times: A History of the Early World (1916) — the Oriental Institute founder's sweeping history of the ancient Near East, Egypt, Greece and Rome; substituted for the erroneous 'History of the Ancient World' entry.

title: La Russie et l'Église universelle
creator: Vladimir Solovyov (1853-1900)
description: Vladimir Solovyov's La Russie et l'Église universelle (1889) — the Russian philosopher's French masterwork on Russia's spiritual mission and church reunion, in the original French; PD substitute for the copyrighted 1948 Rees translation.

title: Masnavi I Ma'navi: The Spiritual Couplets
creator: Jalalu'ddin Rumi (1207-1273); E. H. Whinfield (translator)
description: E. H. Whinfield's 1898 complete abridged English verse translation of Rumi's Masnavi — the first complete English rendering; PD substitute for the copyrighted complete Nicholson edition.

title: The Gospel of Philip (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Valentinian sayings gospel; PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Apocalypse of Adam (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Adam’s revelation to Seth (NHC V,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Teachings of Silvanus (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Wisdom instruction (NHC VII,4); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: On the Origin of the World (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Sethian cosmology (NHC II,5); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Concept of Our Great Power (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Apocalyptic revelation (NHC VI,4); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: Trimorphic Protennoia (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Triple-formed Primal Thought (NHC XIII,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Acts of Peter and the Twelve Apostles (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Apostolic acts (NHC VI,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Gospel of Truth (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Valentinian meditation (NHC I,3); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Paraphrase of Shem (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Sethian apocalypse (NHC VII,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Heart Sutra (F. Max Müller translation, SBE Vol. 49, 1894)
creator: F. Max Müller
description: Müller’s 1894 PD translation substitutes the restricted Red Pine 2004 commentary edition.

title: Ragnarok: The Age of Fire and Gravel
creator: Ignatius Donnelly
description: Donnelly's 1883 comet-catastrophism sequel to Atlantis — the founding text of modern catastrophist geology, cited from Velikovsky to Hancock.

title: The Great Cryptogram: Francis Bacon's Cipher in the So-Called Shakespeare Plays
creator: Ignatius Donnelly
description: Donnelly's 1888 Bacon-cipher magnum opus — the landmark of the Bacon-Shakespeare authorship controversy and the founding text of cryptogram literature.

title: The History of Atlantis
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Spence's 1927 synthesis — the most complete early scholarly survey of Atlantis theories, the standard interwar reference.

title: Atlantis in America
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Spence's 1925 New World volume — the key statement of the American-evidence case for Atlantis, pairing Plato with Mesoamerican archaeology.

title: Sacred Mysteries Among the Mayas and the Quiches, 11,500 Years Ago
creator: Augustus Le Plongeon
description: Le Plongeon's 1886 Maya-Atlantis manifesto — source of the name 'Mu' and the Maya-Egypt diffusion theory behind Donnelly and Churchward.

title: Paradise Found: The Cradle of the Human Race at the North Pole
creator: William F. Warren
description: Warren's 1885 Arctic-origin thesis — the founding text of the polar-Atlantis tradition, cited by theosophists ever since.

title: Ancient America, in Notes on American Archaeology
creator: John D. Baldwin
description: Baldwin's 1871 diffusionist classic — the most widely read 19th-century case for a lost civilized race in ancient America.

title: Lettres sur l'Atlantide de Platon et sur l'ancienne histoire de l'Asie
creator: Jean-Sylvain Bailly
description: Bailly's 1779 letters — the first modern scholarly treatise on Plato's Atlantis, in French; Donnelly's chief 18th-century predecessor.

title: Quatre lettres sur le Mexique
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg
description: Brasseur's 1868 letters — the founding statement of the Maya-Atlantis connection by the great 19th-century Mayanist; in French.

title: Manuscrit Troano: Études sur le système graphique et la langue des Mayas, Vol. 1
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg
description: First publication of the Troano Codex (1869), vol. 1 — the Maya manuscript Le Plongeon misread to coin 'Mu'; in French.

title: Manuscrit Troano: Études sur le système graphique et la langue des Mayas, Vol. 2
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg
description: First publication of the Troano Codex, vol. 2 (1870), with Brasseur's conclusion and Maya phonetic table; in French.

title: Popol Vuh: Le livre sacré et les mythes de l'antiquité américaine
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg, trans.
description: Brasseur's 1861 first European edition of the Popol Vuh — the Maya sacred book at the heart of every Maya-Atlantis theory; in French.

title: The Myths of the New World
creator: Daniel G. Brinton
description: Brinton's 1868 landmark — the great sceptical counterweight to diffusionism that every Atlantis writer had to answer.

title: American Antiquities, and Discoveries in the West
creator: Josiah Priest
description: Priest's 1833 bestseller — the first popular American 'lost race' book and the founding text of the mound-builder craze.

title: Ancient Monuments of the Mississippi Valley
creator: E. G. Squier and E. H. Davis
description: The 1848 Smithsonian survey — the foundational scientific record of the American mounds, cited in every lost-race debate since.

title: New Atlantis
creator: Francis Bacon
description: Bacon's 1627 island utopia of Bensalem — the archetype of the lost-continent tale in English, cited by Atlantis writers for three centuries.

title: Mythical Monsters
creator: Charles Gould
description: Gould's 1886 survey of dragons and sea-serpents — the founding text of cryptozoology and the 19th century's great fortean natural history.

title: 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's qabalistic correspondence tables for the 32 paths — the standard Thelemic reference work cited by every later writer on magical qabalah.

title: Konx Om Pax: Essays in Light
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's early prose-poem essays on mysticism — the first book of his middle period, bridging his poetry and the later magical textbooks.

title: The Book of Lies, Which Is Also Falsely Called Breaks (Liber CCCXXXIII)
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's book of 93 paradoxical chapters — the central Thelemic scripture of wit and contradiction, endlessly cited in Thelemic commentary.

title: Book 4, Part I: Mysticism
creator: Aleister Crowley (with Mary D'Este Sturges)
description: Part I of Crowley's great magical textbook — the systematic A.'.A.'. manual of mysticism, from asana to samadhi.

title: Book 4, Part II: Magick (Elementary Theory)
creator: Aleister Crowley (with Mary D'Este Sturges)
description: Part II of Crowley's great magical textbook — the elementary theory of magick: the temple, the circle, the triangle, and the weapons of the magician.

title: Moonchild (Liber LXXXI, The Butterfly Net)
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's occult novel of a magical war over an unborn child — a roman-a-clef of the Golden Dawn and O.T.O. milieu, his major work of fiction.

title: The Diary of a Drug Fiend
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's notorious novel of cocaine and heroin addiction — the book that made him infamous in the British press and a landmark of drug literature.

title: Psychic Self-Defense: A Study in Occult Pathology and Criminality
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's classic manual of defense against psychic attack — the foundational text of modern occult self-protection, cited in every later work on the subject.

title: The Esoteric Orders and Their Work
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's early survey of the Western esoteric orders and their methods — the first systematic English account of how the mystery schools actually work.

title: The Training and Work of an Initiate
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's companion to Esoteric Orders — the practical curriculum of occult initiation, from meditation to ceremonial work.

title: Sane Occultism
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's defense of rational occultism against credulity and fraud — the manifesto of her no-nonsense approach to esoteric study.

title: The Secrets of Dr. Taverner
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's classic occult detective stories — the founding text of esoteric fiction's 'psychic doctor' genre, blending her nursing and occult experience.

title: The Legend of Aleister Crowley
creator: P. R. Stephensen and Israel Regardie
description: The contemporary defense of Crowley against the press vilification campaign — the primary document of the 1930s battle over his reputation, by his future secretary.

title: The Tree of Life: A Study in Magic
creator: Israel Regardie
description: Regardie's great theoretical exposition of magic through the qabalistic Tree of Life — the systematic textbook behind his later Golden Dawn work.

title: The Star in the West: A Critical Essay upon the Works of Aleister Crowley
creator: J. F. C. Fuller
description: Fuller's pioneering critical study of Crowley — the first serious literary assessment of the poet-occultist, by the future military theorist.

title: Q.B.L., or The Bride's Reception
creator: Frater Achad (Charles Stansfeld Jones)
description: Achad's first major qabalistic work — the radical Thelemic reassignment of the Tree of Life attributions that split him from Crowley.

title: The Egyptian Revival, or The Ever-Coming Son in the Light of the Tarot
creator: Frater Achad (Charles Stansfeld Jones)
description: Achad's qabalistic revisionism applied to Egyptian symbolism and the tarot — the second of his three major Thelemic qabalistic texts.

title: The Anatomy of the Body of God
creator: Frater Achad (Charles Stansfeld Jones)
description: Achad's geometric projection of the Tree of Life in three dimensions — the culmination of his qabalistic trilogy, with Will Ransom's diagrams.

title: A Vision
creator: W. B. Yeats
description: Yeats's occult system of history and personality channeled through automatic writing — the central esoteric text of the 1920s literary occult revival.

title: Tertium Organum: The Third Canon of Thought
creator: P. D. Ouspensky
description: Ouspensky's exposition of the fourth dimension as the key to cosmic consciousness — the book that carried hyperspace philosophy into the occult revival.

title: A New Model of the Universe
creator: P. D. Ouspensky
description: Ouspensky's synthesis of science, religion, and esotericism — the full statement of his psychological method, never renewed for copyright.

title: The Pictorial Key to the Tarot
creator: A. E. Waite
description: Waite's definitive exposition of the Rider-Waite tarot — the book that fixed the meanings of the modern tarot deck for the next century.

title: The Holy Kabbalah
creator: A. E. Waite
description: Waite's massive historical study of the secret tradition in Israel — the standard English survey of Christian kabbalah in the early 20th century.

title: The Brotherhood of the Rosy Cross
creator: A. E. Waite
description: Waite's documentary history of Rosicrucianism — the scholarly foundation for all later study of the Rosy Cross legend.

title: The Serpent Power: The Secrets of Tantric and Shaktic Yoga
creator: Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe)
description: Woodroffe's translation and commentary on the Sat-cakra-nirupana — the book that introduced kundalini yoga to the West.

title: The Rosicrucian Cosmo-Conception, or Mystic Christianity
creator: Max Heindel
description: Heindel's Rosicrucian cosmology — the founding text of the American Rosicrucian movement, first published 1909; this is the 1929 printing.

title: The Witch-Cult in Western Europe
creator: Margaret Alice Murray
description: Murray's anthropological argument for a surviving pagan witch-religion — the most influential (and contested) witchcraft thesis of the 20th century.

title: An Experiment with Time
creator: J. W. Dunne
description: Dunne's theory of serial time and precognitive dreams — the book that made 'precognition' a subject of serious psychical research.

title: The Masters and the Path
creator: C. W. Leadbeater
description: Leadbeater's account of the Theosophical Masters and the occult hierarchy — the definitive statement of 1920s Theosophical esotericism.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 2 (September 1909)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 2 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1909) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 3 (March 1910)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 3 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1910) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 4 (September 1910)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 4 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1910) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 5 (March 1911)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 5 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1911) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 6 (September 1911)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 6 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1911) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 7 (March 1912)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 7 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1912) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 8 (September 1912)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 8 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1912) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 9 (March 1913)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 9 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1913) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 10 (September 1913)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 10 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1913) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. III, No. 1: The Blue Equinox (March 1919)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: The Blue Equinox — Crowley's O.T.O. manifesto number, containing the Gnostic Mass, the O.T.O. constitutions, and the proclamation of the Law of Thelema.

title: The Case for the Sea-Serpent
creator: Rupert T. Gould
description: Rupert Gould's 1930 naval officer's brief for the sea-serpent — the 20th century's most methodical pro-sea-serpent monograph, answering Oudemans case by case.

title: The Great Sea-Serpent: An Historical and Critical Treatise
creator: Antoon Cornelis Oudemans
description: Oudemans' 1892 treatise — the founding scientific monograph of sea-serpent research, analyzing 162 sighting reports; the book every later sea-serpent writer answers.

title: Sea Monsters Unmasked
creator: Henry Lee
description: Henry Lee's 1883 skeptical natural history of sea-serpents — the Victorian debunking classic explaining sightings via giant squid and known animals.

title: Sea Fables Explained
creator: Henry Lee
description: Lee's 1883 companion volume dissecting mermaids, the kraken, and sea-fables — the great Victorian demystification of mermaid lore.

title: The Octopus; or, The Devil-Fish of Fiction and of Fact
creator: Henry Lee
description: Lee's 1875 monograph on the octopus and the kraken legend — the first scientific treatment separating the real devil-fish from the mythic kraken.

title: Monsters of the Sea, Legendary and Authentic
creator: John Gibson
description: Gibson's 1887 survey of sea monsters legendary and authentic — from the kraken and sea-serpent to the giant squid, a Victorian bestiary of the deep.

title: The Wilderness Hunter
creator: Theodore Roosevelt
description: Roosevelt's 1893 hunting memoir containing the famous 'Bauman' story — the trapper stalked by a mysterious bipedal beast, the classic proto-Bigfoot account.

title: Beasts and Men
creator: Carl Hagenbeck
description: Hagenbeck's 1910 memoir — the famous animal dealer who first published Western reports of a giant Congo dinosaur, the origin of the Mokele-mbembe story.

title: Mount Everest: The Reconnaissance, 1921
creator: Charles Howard-Bury and the Mount Everest Committee
description: The official 1922 account of the 1921 Everest reconnaissance — containing the first published report of the 'Metohkangmi' tracks that became the Abominable Snowman.

title: Through Tibet to Everest
creator: John B. L. Noel
description: Captain Noel's 1927 Everest book with a chapter on the 'Legendary Hairy Man of the Mountains' — an early mountaineer's treatment of yeti lore.

title: Three Voyages of a Naturalist
creator: Michael J. Nicoll
description: Nicoll's 1908 natural-history voyages, including his 1905 'Valhalla' sea-serpent sighting off Brazil — one of the most credible 20th-century reports, debated by Gould.

title: Explorations and Adventures in Equatorial Africa
creator: Paul Du Chaillu
description: Du Chaillu's 1861 bestseller — the book that introduced the gorilla to the popular imagination, the 'monster ape' narrative that made the gorilla famous.

title: Trailing the Giant Panda
creator: Theodore Roosevelt Jr. and Kermit Roosevelt
description: The Roosevelt brothers' 1929 account of the expedition that brought the first giant panda to the West — the 'mystery bear' of Tibet made real.

title: In Brightest Africa
creator: Carl E. Akeley
description: Akeley's 1923 classic of African natural history and gorilla study — the taxidermist-conservationist who made the mountain gorilla known to museums.

title: On the Gorilla Trail
creator: Mary Hastings Bradley
description: Bradley's 1922 account — among the first books on the mountain gorilla, by one of the first women to seek it in the Virungas.

title: Two Trips to Gorilla Land and the Cataracts of the Congo
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's 1876 narrative of seeking the gorilla in Gaboon — the great explorer's contribution to the 19th-century gorilla literature.

title: The Wonderland of the Eastern Congo
creator: T. Alexander Barns
description: Barns' 1922 account of the snow-crowned volcanoes region — early 20th-century gorilla country at the dawn of mountain-gorilla science.

title: Among the Himalayas
creator: Laurence Austine Waddell
description: Waddell's 1899 Himalayan travelogue recording legends of 'hairy wild men' — one of the earliest Western notices of yeti folklore.

title: The Kangchenjunga Adventure
creator: Frank S. Smythe
description: Smythe's 1930 account of the 1929 Kangchenjunga expedition, reporting 'footprints of a Snow Man' — a mountaineer's yeti encounter.

title: Account of a Photographic Expedition to the Southern Glaciers of Kangchenjunga in the Sikkim Himalaya
creator: N. A. Tombazi
description: Tombazi's 1926 expedition book containing the famous first-hand 1925 yeti sighting — the 'reported wild man' seen at 15,500 feet, with measured footprints.

title: The Romance of Natural History
creator: Philip Henry Gosse
description: Gosse's 1860 popular natural history treating sea-serpents and ocean marvels as 'romance' — the Victorian naturalist's take on sea monsters, cited by Oudemans.

title: The Lost World
creator: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Doyle's 1912 novel of living dinosaurs on a South American plateau — the fiction that created the 'lost world' trope driving real cryptozoological expeditions.

title: The Cruise of the 'Cachalot'
creator: Frank T. Bullen
description: Bullen's 1898 whaling classic with the famous giant-squid account — a whaleman's first-hand sea-monster narrative from the age of sail.

title: Denizens of the Deep
creator: Frank T. Bullen
description: Bullen's 1904 volume on deep-sea life, treating sea-serpents and ocean monsters from a sailor-naturalist's experience.

title: "What Is It? A Strange Creature Captured above Yale — A British Columbia Gorilla"
creator: Daily British Colonist (Victoria, B.C.)
description: The July 4, 1884 British Colonist report of 'Jacko,' the ape-like creature captured near Yale — the famous proto-Bigfoot capture story, likely a hoax, endlessly cited.

title: "Introducing B.C.'s Hairy Giants"
creator: J. W. Burns
description: Burns' April 1929 Maclean's article — the first publication to use the word 'Sasquatch' in English, launching the modern Bigfoot era.

title: Report of a Committee of the Linnaean Society of New England, Relative to a Large Marine Animal, Supposed to Be a Serpent, Seen near Cape Ann, Massachusetts, in August 1817
creator: Linnaean Society of New England
description: The 1817 Linnaean Society report on the Gloucester sea-serpent — the first organized scientific investigation of a sea-serpent, with sworn depositions.

title: The Stronsa Beast: Dr. Barclay's Account with Affidavits (1808–1809)
creator: Dr. John Barclay; Wernerian Natural History Society
description: Barclay's 1808–09 Wernerian Society papers on the Stronsa carcass with sworn affidavits — the 'sea-serpent' specimen later identified as a basking shark.

title: The Daedalus Sea-Serpent Reports (1848)
creator: Capt. Peter M'Quhae; Lieut. Edgar Drummond; The Zoologist
description: The complete 1848 Daedalus dossier from The Zoologist — M'Quhae's Admiralty report, Drummond's journal, Times reprints, and the Daphne account; the classic sea-serpent sighting.

title: "Notice of the External Characters and Habits of Troglodytes gorilla"
creator: Thomas S. Savage
description: Savage's 1847 paper naming the gorilla to science — the founding document that turned the 'wild man of the woods' from legend into zoology.

title: "The Quest for the Dragon of Komodo"
creator: W. Douglas Burden
description: Burden's 1927 Natural History account of the expedition that captured the Komodo dragon — the 'living dragon' brought to America, an inspiration for King Kong.

title: Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects (The Condon Report)
creator: University of Colorado / Dr. Edward U. Condon (USAF contract)
description: The complete 1968 USAF-commissioned scientific study of UFOs that ended Project Blue Book; its 'no further study warranted' conclusion is the pivotal document in government ufology, staged here with the full index.
source: National Center for Atmospheric Research mirror (ncas.org)

creator: Johann Sperling
description: Ten theses on magic defended at Wittenberg — a Latin academic disputation on magic and demons.

title: The History of the Devils of Loudun (1887)
creator: Des Niau (eyewitness)
description: Eyewitness account of the Ursuline possessions and Grandier's 1634 trial and execution; Goldsmid's translation.

title: Aboriginal Siberia: A Study in Social Anthropology
creator: Maria Czaplicka
description: The first great English synthesis of Siberian shamanism — Czaplicka's 1914 Oxford study fixed 'shaman' as an anthropological category and remains the most-cited early authority on the subject.

title: The Chukchee
creator: Waldemar Bogoras
description: The Jesup Expedition's monumental Chukchee ethnography (1904–1909) — the classic firsthand account of Chukchi shamanism, spirits, and ritual life.

title: Koryak Texts
creator: Waldemar Bogoras
description: Bogoras's 1917 Jesup collection of Koryak texts — primary shamanic narratives and ritual texts in the original, with translations.

title: The Central Eskimo
creator: Franz Boas
description: Boas's foundational Baffin Land ethnography — the first systematic account of Inuit angakok (shaman) practice, taboo, and cosmology.

title: The Eskimo of Baffin Land and Hudson Bay
creator: Franz Boas
description: Boas's AMNH bulletin (Parts I–II, 1901/1907) on Baffin Island and Hudson Bay Inuit — angakok ritual, taboo, and cosmology from his fieldwork.

title: The People of the Polar North
creator: Knud Rasmussen
description: Rasmussen's first great Arctic narrative — Inuit shamanism recorded from the inside by the Danish-Greenlandic explorer, with Moltke's illustrations.

title: Finno-Ugric, Siberian Mythology
creator: Uno Holmberg
description: The Mythology of All Races volume on Finno-Ugric and Siberian religion — the standard English survey of northern Eurasian shamanic cosmology.

title: Tales and Traditions of the Eskimo
creator: Hinrich Rink
description: Rink's classic collection of Greenlandic tales — the primary English source for Inuit shamanic folklore, drawn from native narrators.

title: The Eskimo about Bering Strait
creator: Edward William Nelson
description: The Bureau of American Ethnology's great Bering Strait monograph — the definitive 19th-century record of Yupik shamanism and ceremony.

title: Ethnological Results of the Point Barrow Expedition
creator: John Murdoch
description: The Point Barrow expedition's ethnology — Iñupiat shamanic practice and material culture documented at the edge of first contact.

title: Beschreibung von dem Lande Kamtschatka
creator: Georg Wilhelm Steller
description: Steller's 1774 Kamchatka description — the earliest European eyewitness account of Itelmen shamanism, from Bering's expedition naturalist. In German.

title: Shamanism in Siberia and European Russia
creator: V. M. Mikhailowski
description: The first English-language survey paper to define 'shamanism' for Western anthropology (Journal of the Anthropological Institute, 1895), translated by Oliver Wardrop.

title: Barddas
creator: Iolo Morganwg (ed. J. Williams ab Ithel)
description: Iolo Morganwg's 'Bardic-Druidic' theology, presented as ancient but largely his own invention — the forgery that shaped the entire modern druid revival. (Text of the 1862/1874 edition.)

title: The Mythology and Rites of the British Druids
creator: Edward Davies
description: Davies's 1809 druidic mythology — the Romantic era's grand system fusing Noah's Flood, the ark, and druid lore; the book that defined 'druidism' for a generation.

title: Celtic Researches
creator: Edward Davies
description: Davies's 1804 origin-treatise on the ancient Britons — the first Romantic attempt at a systematic Celtic-druidic prehistory.

title: A Critical History of the Celtic Religion and Learning
creator: John Toland
description: Toland's posthumous 1726 history (this text from the 1815 edition) — the Enlightenment's first critical, demystifying account of the druids.

title: The Druids: A Study in Keltic Prehistory
creator: T. D. Kendrick
description: Kendrick's 1927 synthesis (this text from the 1928 impression) — the first modern scholarly druid study, the baseline for all later work.

title: The Myvyrian Archaiology of Wales
creator: Owen Jones, Edward Williams, and William Owen Pughe (eds.)
description: The great Welsh manuscript collection (1801–1807; this text from the 1870 reprint) — the print vehicle through which Iolo Morganwg's druidic forgeries entered the tradition.

title: Mona Antiqua Restaurata
creator: Henry Rowlands
description: Rowlands's Anglesey antiquities (this text from the 1766 second edition) — the first druid-centered archaeology of Mona, founding the 'druidical temple' reading of megaliths.

title: Lectures on the Origin and Growth of Religion as Illustrated by Celtic Heathendom
creator: John Rhŷs
description: Rhŷs's 1888 Hibbert Lectures — the founding academic work on Celtic pagan religion, still cited on druidic belief.

title: Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx
creator: John Rhŷs
description: Rhŷs's two-volume folklore collection (1901) — druidic survivals traced through Welsh and Manx folk belief, fairies, and folk-heroes.

title: Les druides et les dieux celtiques à forme d'animaux
creator: Henri d'Arbois de Jubainville
description: D'Arbois de Jubainville's 1906 study — the French Celtic school's authority on druidic religion and animal-formed gods. In French.

title: The Mysteries of Britain
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Spence's 1928 survey of Britain's secret rites and traditions — druids, megaliths, and the native mystery tradition restored.

title: Runir seu Danica literatura antiquissima
creator: Ole Worm
description: Worm's runology (this text from the 1651 second edition) — the first scholarly treatment of the runes; the founding work of runic studies. In Latin.

title: Handbook of the Old-Northern Runic Monuments
creator: George Stephens
description: Stephens's 1884 handbook — the 19th century's standard English guide to the runic monuments of Scandinavia and England, by the great runologist.

title: Teutonic Mythology
creator: Jacob Grimm (trans. James Steven Stallybrass)
description: Grimm's Deutsche Mythologie in Stallybrass's English (4 vols., 1880–1888) — the foundation text of Germanic myth and rune-lore; every later work cites it.

title: Die Runenschrift
creator: Ludvig Wimmer
description: Wimmer's 1887 runology — the Danish school's definitive 19th-century study of the runic alphabet. In German.

title: Greeks and Goths: A Study on the Runes
creator: Isaac Taylor
description: Taylor's 1879 rune-origin theory — the Victorian debate on the runes' debt to the Greek alphabet, a turning point in runology.

title: Atalanta fugiens
creator: Michael Maier
description: Maier's 1618 alchemical emblem book — 50 emblems with epigrams, discourses, and musical fugues; the Rosicrucian era's most famous alchemical art-text. In Latin.

title: Amulets and Superstitions
creator: E. A. Wallis Budge
description: Budge's 1930 compendium (reprinted as 'Amulets and Talismans') — the classic English survey of Egyptian and Near Eastern amulets, with original texts and translations.

title: Amulets
creator: W. M. Flinders Petrie
description: Petrie's 1914 illustrated corpus — the great excavator's typology of Egyptian amulets, the archaeological foundation of the subject.

title: Les vrayes centuries et propheties
creator: Michel de Nostredame
description: Nostradamus's Centuries in the original French (1710 edition) — the prophecies as his readers first met them. In French.

title: The True Prophecies or Prognostications of Michael Nostradamus
creator: Michel de Nostredame (trans. Theophilus de Garencières)
description: Garencières's 1672 English translation — the first complete English Nostradamus, with the famous biographical preface; the version that made him an English prophet.

title: The Geomancie of Maister Christopher Cattan
creator: Christopher Cattan (trans. Francis Sparry)
description: Cattan's 1591 geomancy in Sparry's English — the first English manual of divination by earth-figures, the foundation of English geomantic literature.

title: Palmistry, the Secrets Thereof Disclosed
creator: Richard Saunders
description: Saunders's 1663 palmistry — the Restoration era's standard English chiromancy manual, reprinted for a century.

title: The Romance and Prophecies of Thomas of Erceldoune
creator: Thomas of Erceldoune (ed. James A. H. Murray)
description: Murray's 1875 Early English Text Society edition — Thomas the Rhymer's romance and the Scottish political-prophecy tradition in full.

title: The Strange and Wonderful Prophecies of Mother Shipton
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1700 Mother Shipton collection — England's great folk-prophetess in her classic chapbook form: birth, life, death, and prophecies.

title: The Essays and Hymns of Synesius of Cyrene
creator: Synesius of Cyrene (trans. Augustine Fitzgerald)
description: Fitzgerald's 1930 translation (2 vols.) — includes De insomniis, the Neoplatonic theory of divination by dreams, the late-antique classic on the subject.

title: A Dweller on Two Planets
creator: Frederick S. Oliver (as 'Phylos the Thibetan')
description: Oliver's 1905 theosophical novel, dictated by the discarnate 'Phylos' — Atlantis, Lemuria, and occult science; the pivotal American occult novel.

title: Perpetuum Mobile; or, Search for Self-Motive Power
creator: Henry Dircks
description: The great Victorian survey of three centuries of perpetual-motion schemes — the essential history of the obsession, cataloguing every known device and delusion.

title: Perpetuum Mobile; or, Search for Self-Motive Power, Second Series
creator: Henry Dircks
