The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 9: Books LXXI-LXXX (Epitome)
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), Books 71-80: Hadrian through Severus Alexander, in the Byzantine epitome, with indices, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dionysius of Halicarnassus: Roman Antiquities, Vol. 1 (Books I-II; Spelman, 1758)
creator: Dionysius of Halicarnassus (Edward Spelman, trans.)
description: Dionysius of Halicarnassus's Roman Antiquities (c. 7 BCE), Books 1-2: the origins of Rome, Aeneas, Romulus and the kings to Tullus Hostilius. The Greek historian's massive history of early Rome — our fullest source for the regal period and early Republic. Edward Spelman's 1758 English translation via Internet Archive.

title: Dionysius of Halicarnassus: Roman Antiquities, Vol. 2 (Books III-V; Spelman, 1758)
creator: Dionysius of Halicarnassus (Edward Spelman, trans.)
description: Dionysius of Halicarnassus's Roman Antiquities (c. 7 BCE), Books 3-5: the later kings, the expulsion of the Tarquins, and the early Republic. The Greek historian's massive history of early Rome — our fullest source for the regal period and early Republic. Edward Spelman's 1758 English translation via Internet Archive.

title: Dionysius of Halicarnassus: Roman Antiquities, Vol. 3 (Books VI-VIII; Spelman, 1758)
creator: Dionysius of Halicarnassus (Edward Spelman, trans.)
description: Dionysius of Halicarnassus's Roman Antiquities (c. 7 BCE), Books 6-8: the Conflict of the Orders and the wars with the Volscians, Coriolanus. The Greek historian's massive history of early Rome — our fullest source for the regal period and early Republic. Edward Spelman's 1758 English translation via Internet Archive.

title: Dionysius of Halicarnassus: Roman Antiquities, Vol. 4 (Books IX-XI; Spelman, 1758)
creator: Dionysius of Halicarnassus (Edward Spelman, trans.)
description: Dionysius of Halicarnassus's Roman Antiquities (c. 7 BCE), Books 9-11: the Decemvirate through the early 4th century BCE, with index and errata. The Greek historian's massive history of early Rome — our fullest source for the regal period and early Republic. Edward Spelman's 1758 English translation via Internet Archive.

title: Eutropius's Abridgment of Roman History
creator: Eutropius (Rev. John Selby Watson, trans.)
description: Eutropius's Breviarium (c. 369 CE) — the ten-book epitome of Roman history from Romulus to Jovian, written for the emperor Valens. The school-text of the Middle Ages and the most-copied Roman history for a thousand years. With Watson's biographical notice. Rev. John Selby Watson's 1853 translation via Internet Archive.

title: Epitome of Roman History
creator: Lucius Annaeus Florus (Rev. John Selby Watson, trans.)
description: Florus's Epitome (c. 120 CE) — Rome's history cast as the life-stages of a single man, from Romulus to Augustus. The most rhetorical of the Latin epitomators, widely read through the Middle Ages. With Watson's biographical notice. Rev. John Selby Watson's 1852 translation via Internet Archive.

title: 漢書 (Book of Han) — Chinese text
creator: Ban Gu (班固)
description: The complete 漢書 (Book of Han, c. 92 CE) in the original Classical Chinese: the dynastic history of the Western Han, annals, tables, treatises, and biographies. Text via Chinese Wikisource (public domain).

title: Herodian's History of His Own Times (J. Hart, trans., 1749)
creator: Herodian (J. Hart, trans.)
description: Herodian's History (c. 238 CE) — the eight-book narrative of the Roman Empire from the death of Marcus Aurelius (180) to Gordian III (238): Commodus, the Year of the Five Emperors, the Severans, and the crisis of the third century, by a contemporary. With Hart's appendix continuing the history to Constantine. J. Hart's 1749 English translation via Internet Archive. (Note: 18th-century orthography; the scan renders the long s as f.)

title: Historia Augusta, Vol. I (Magie, 1921)
creator: Unknown (David Magie, trans.)
description: The Historia Augusta (c. 400 CE), Vol. I: the lives of Hadrian, Aelius, Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius, Verus, Avidius Cassius, Commodus, Pertinax, Didius Julianus, Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Alexander Severus, with index — the imperial biographies from Hadrian to the mid-third century, our fullest (if gossipy and partly invented) source for the emperors of Rome's crisis age. David Magie's Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: Historia Augusta, Vol. II (Magie, 1924)
creator: Unknown (David Magie, trans.)
description: The Historia Augusta (c. 400 CE), Vol. II: the lives of the two Maximini, the three Gordians, and Maximus and Balbinus — the imperial biographies from Hadrian to the mid-third century, our fullest (if gossipy and partly invented) source for the emperors of Rome's crisis age. David Magie's Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: 後漢書 (Book of the Later Han) — Chinese text
creator: Fan Ye (范曄)
description: The complete 後漢書 (Book of the Later Han, c. 445 CE) in the original Classical Chinese: the dynastic history of the Eastern Han. Text via Chinese Wikisource (public domain).

title: Against Apion
creator: Flavius Josephus (William Whiston, trans.)
description: Josephus's two-book defense of Judaism against its Alexandrian critics (c. 93 CE) — our fullest ancient source for the Jewish counter-narrative to anti-Jewish polemic, and a key witness to Egyptian and Phoenician historiography. Whiston's 1737 translation via Project Gutenberg. Completes the library's Josephus set (Antiquities and Wars already present).

title: The Life of Flavius Josephus
creator: Flavius Josephus (William Whiston, trans.)
description: Josephus's autobiography (c. 94 CE) — his account of his command in Galilee during the Jewish War and his stormy relations with Justus of Tiberias. The only surviving first-person memoir of the war's Jewish leadership. Whiston's 1737 translation via Project Gutenberg.

title: Justin's Epitome of the History of Trogus Pompeius
creator: Marcus Junianus Justinus (Rev. John Selby Watson, trans.)
description: Justin's epitome (2nd-4th c. CE) of the lost 44-book universal history of Trogus Pompeius — the sole surviving witness to Trogus, preserving the Hellenistic kingdoms, Parthia, and early Rome. With Watson's biographical notice. Rev. John Selby Watson's 1853 translation via Internet Archive.

title: The History of Rome, Books 27 to 36
creator: Livy (D. Spillan and Cyrus Edmonds, trans.)
description: Livy's History of Rome, Books 27-36 (the close of the Second Punic War and the war with Philip V of Macedon) in the Spillan/Edmonds translation via Project Gutenberg. Continues the library's Livy set (Books 1-26 already present).

title: The History of Rome, Books 37 to 45
creator: Livy (D. Spillan and Cyrus Edmonds, trans.)
description: Livy's History of Rome, Books 37-45 (the Syrian war against Antiochus III and the conquest of Macedon) with the surviving Epitomes and Fragments, in the Spillan/Edmonds translation via Project Gutenberg. Completes the library's extant Livy set (Books 1-36 already present).

title: The Fragments of Manetho (Cory, 1832)
creator: Manetho (Isaac Preston Cory, trans.)
description: The surviving fragments of Manetho's Aegyptiaca (c. 280 BCE): the dynastic lists from the gods and demigods through the Thirty Dynasties — the Egyptian priest's chronology on which all Pharaonic dating still rests — with the allied Egyptian fragments. From Cory's Ancient Fragments (1832) via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: Res Gestae Divi Augusti (The Achievements of Augustus)
creator: Augustus (Frederick W. Shipley, trans.)
description: The Res Gestae Divi Augusti (14 CE) — Augustus's own political testament, the 'queen of inscriptions', recording his achievements for engraving at his mausoleum. The single most important documentary source for the Augustan age, in Shipley's 1924 Loeb translation with his introduction on the Monumentum Ancyranum. Via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: 三國志 (Records of the Three Kingdoms) — Chinese text
creator: Chen Shou (陳壽)
description: The complete 三國志 (Records of the Three Kingdoms, c. 289 CE) in the original Classical Chinese: the histories of Wei, Shu, and Wu. Text via Chinese Wikisource (public domain).

title: 史記 (Records of the Grand Historian) — Chinese text
creator: Sima Qian (司馬遷)
description: The complete 史記 (Records of the Grand Historian, c. 91 BCE) in the original Classical Chinese: 130 chapters — annals, tables, treatises, hereditary houses, and biographies. The founding work of Chinese historiography. Text via Chinese Wikisource (public domain).

title: Sima Qian: Mémoires historiques, Tome cinquième (Chavannes, 1905)
creator: Sima Qian (Édouard Chavannes, trans.)
description: Sima Qian's Shiji — Records of the Grand Historian (c. 91 BCE), Tome cinquième: Chapters 43-47: biographies, with index and errata. The founding work of Chinese historiography, covering legendary emperors through the Han dynasty. In Édouard Chavannes's monumental French translation (1895-1905), the standard public-domain Western version, via Internet Archive.

title: Sima Qian: Mémoires historiques, Tome premier (Chavannes, 1895)
creator: Sima Qian (Édouard Chavannes, trans.)
description: Sima Qian's Shiji — Records of the Grand Historian (c. 91 BCE), Tome premier: Chapters 1-4: the Five Emperors, the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties. The founding work of Chinese historiography, covering legendary emperors through the Han dynasty. In Édouard Chavannes's monumental French translation (1895-1905), the standard public-domain Western version, via Internet Archive.

title: Sima Qian: Mémoires historiques, Tome quatrième (Chavannes, 1901)
creator: Sima Qian (Édouard Chavannes, trans.)
description: Sima Qian's Shiji — Records of the Grand Historian (c. 91 BCE), Tome quatrième: Chapters 31-42: the hereditary houses continued and the biographies. The founding work of Chinese historiography, covering legendary emperors through the Han dynasty. In Édouard Chavannes's monumental French translation (1895-1905), the standard public-domain Western version, via Internet Archive.

title: Sima Qian: Mémoires historiques, Tome second (Chavannes, 1896)
creator: Sima Qian (Édouard Chavannes, trans.)
description: Sima Qian's Shiji — Records of the Grand Historian (c. 91 BCE), Tome second: Chapters 5-12: Qin, the First Emperor, Xiang Yu, and Emperor Gaozu of Han. The founding work of Chinese historiography, covering legendary emperors through the Han dynasty. In Édouard Chavannes's monumental French translation (1895-1905), the standard public-domain Western version, via Internet Archive.

title: Sima Qian: Mémoires historiques, Tome troisième (Chavannes, 1898)
creator: Sima Qian (Édouard Chavannes, trans.)
description: Sima Qian's Shiji — Records of the Grand Historian (c. 91 BCE), Tome troisième: Chapters 13-22: chronological tables and the hereditary houses. The founding work of Chinese historiography, covering legendary emperors through the Han dynasty. In Édouard Chavannes's monumental French translation (1895-1905), the standard public-domain Western version, via Internet Archive.

title: Compendium of Roman History
creator: Velleius Paterculus (Frederick W. Shipley, trans.)
description: Velleius Paterculus's Compendium (c. 30 CE) — the contemporary Tiberian epitome of Roman history from the Trojan War to Tiberius's reign, by a soldier who served under Tiberius in Germany. The only continuous narrative of the Augustan age by an insider. Frederick W. Shipley's 1924 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: 資治通鑑 (Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government) — Chinese text
creator: Sima Guang (司馬光)
description: The complete 資治通鑑 (Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, 1084 CE) in the original Classical Chinese: 294 chapters of chronological history from the Warring States to the Five Dynasties — the great universal history of imperial China. Text via Chinese Wikisource (public domain).

title: The New History of Count Zosimus (1684 English translation)
creator: Zosimus (Anonymous, trans.)
description: Zosimus's New History (c. 510 CE) — the six-book pagan history of Rome's decline from Augustus to Honorius (to 410), our fullest narrative of the late empire's fall and the last great pagan voice against Christian Rome. The 1684 anonymous English translation (the only public-domain English version) via Internet Archive. (Note: 17th-century orthography; the scan renders the long s as f.)

title: The Elegies of Tibullus
creator: Tibullus (Theodore Chickering Williams, trans.)
description: The complete Corpus Tibullianum (Books 1-4) in Williams's verse translation — Rome's elegist of the countryside and Delia; the essential third voice of Latin love-elegy.

title: The Elegies of Propertius
creator: Sextus Propertius (H. E. Butler, trans.)
description: The complete Cynthia elegies (Books 1-4) in the Loeb prose translation — elegy's master and the most allusive voice of Augustan poetry.

title: Epigrams of Martial, Vol. I (Books 1-7)
creator: Martial (Walter C. A. Ker, trans.)
description: Books 1-7 of the epigram canon in the Loeb translation — 1,500+ epigrams that defined the form for two millennia.

title: Epigrams of Martial, Vol. II (Books 8-14)
creator: Martial (Walter C. A. Ker, trans.)
description: Books 8-14 of the epigram canon in the Loeb translation — completes the 1,500+ epigrams.

title: Institutio Oratoria, Vol. I (Books 1-2)
creator: Quintilian (H. E. Butler, trans.)
description: Books 1-2 of rhetoric's bible in the Loeb translation — the complete Roman system of education and oratory.

title: Institutio Oratoria, Vol. II (Books 3-5)
creator: Quintilian (H. E. Butler, trans.)
description: Books 3-5 of the Institutio Oratoria in the Loeb translation.

title: Institutio Oratoria, Vol. III (Books 6-8)
creator: Quintilian (H. E. Butler, trans.)
description: Books 6-8 of the Institutio Oratoria in the Loeb translation.

title: Institutio Oratoria, Vol. IV (Books 9-12)
creator: Quintilian (H. E. Butler, trans.)
description: Books 9-12 of the Institutio Oratoria in the Loeb translation — completes the 12-book system.

title: Statius, Vol. I: Thebaid (Books 1-7)
creator: Statius (J. H. Mozley, trans.)
description: The Thebaid, Books 1-7, in the Loeb translation — the great Silver Latin epic of the Seven Against Thebes.

title: Statius, Vol. II: Thebaid (8-12), Achilleid, Silvae
creator: Statius (J. H. Mozley, trans.)
description: The Thebaid completed, plus the Achilleid fragment and the Silvae — the complete surviving Statius in the Loeb translation.

title: Ausonius, Vol. I
creator: Decimus Magnus Ausonius (Hugh G. Evelyn White, trans.)
description: Volume 1 of Ausonius's poems in the Loeb translation — the Mosella and late Latin poetry's most versatile voice.

title: Ausonius, Vol. II
creator: Decimus Magnus Ausonius (Hugh G. Evelyn White, trans.)
description: Volume 2 of Ausonius's poems in the Loeb translation — completes the late Latin corpus.

title: Lyra Graeca, Vol. I (Sappho, Alcaeus)
creator: J. M. Edmonds (ed./trans.)
description: The remains of Sappho and Alcaeus with English translation — the foundation fragments of Greek lyric.

title: Lyra Graeca, Vol. II (Anacreon, choral lyric)
creator: J. M. Edmonds (ed./trans.)
description: Anacreon, the Anacreontea, and choral lyric fragments with English translation.

title: Lyra Graeca, Vol. III (Simonides, Bacchylides, etc.)
creator: J. M. Edmonds (ed./trans.)
description: Stesichorus, Ibycus, Simonides, Bacchylides and further lyric fragments with English translation.

title: The Attic Nights of Aulus Gellius, Vol. I (Books 1-5)
creator: Aulus Gellius (John C. Rolfe, trans.)
description: Books 1-5 of the Attic Nights in the Loeb translation — the miscellany that preserved lost Latin literature.

title: The Attic Nights of Aulus Gellius, Vol. II (Books 6-13)
creator: Aulus Gellius (John C. Rolfe, trans.)
description: Books 6-13 of the Attic Nights in the Loeb translation.

title: The Attic Nights of Aulus Gellius, Vol. III (Books 14-20)
creator: Aulus Gellius (John C. Rolfe, trans.)
description: Books 14-20 of the Attic Nights in the Loeb translation — completes the 20-book miscellany.

title: Terence, Vol. II (Phormio, Hecyra, Adelphoe)
creator: Terence (John Sargeaunt, trans.)
description: The last three comedies of Terence in the Loeb translation — completes the 6-play corpus; complements the held Vol. I.

title: The Heroides, Amours, Art of Love, and Remedy of Love
creator: Ovid (Henry T. Riley, trans.)
description: Ovid's elegiac corpus — the Heroides, Amores, Ars Amatoria, and Remedia Amoris — in Riley's Bohn prose translation; fills the library's Ovid gaps.

title: The Fasti, Tristia, Pontic Epistles, Ibis, and Halieuticon
creator: Ovid (Henry T. Riley, trans.)
description: Ovid's exile poetry — Tristia and Ex Ponto — plus Fasti, Ibis, and Halieuticon in Riley's Bohn prose translation; the Tristia/Ex Ponto are new to the library.

title: The Loves of Hero and Leander
creator: Musaeus Grammaticus (trans. 1797)
description: The late-antique epyllion of Hero and Leander — the source for Marlowe, Chapman, Keats, and Byron.

title: Bacchylides: The Poems and Fragments
creator: Bacchylides (Sir Richard C. Jebb, ed./trans.)
description: The complete surviving odes and fragments of Bacchylides with Jebb's prose translation — the great rediscovered lyric poet (papyri, 1896).

title: Psychomachia; or, The War of the Soul
creator: Aurelius Prudentius Clemens (trans. 1743)
description: The first great Christian allegory — the battle of Virtues and Vices — in a 1743 English verse translation; the medieval cornerstone.

title: Theocritus, Bion and Moschus, Rendered into English Prose
creator: Theocritus, Bion, Moschus (Andrew Lang, trans.)
description: The complete Idylls of Theocritus plus Bion and Moschus in Lang's prose translation — the pastoral corpus; Bion and Moschus are new to the library.

title: The Works of Hesiod, Callimachus, and Theognis
creator: Hesiod, Callimachus, Theognis (Rev. J. Banks, trans.)
description: Banks's Bohn prose translation — the vehicle for the Elegies of Theognis (new to the library) alongside Hesiod and Callimachus.

title: The Second Punick War (Punica)
creator: Silius Italicus (Thomas Ross, trans.)
description: The complete Punica — the longest surviving Latin epic (17 books) — in Thomas Ross's 1661 English translation, the first ever.

title: Xenophon's Ephesian History; or, The Love-Adventures of Abrocomas and Anthia
creator: Xenophon of Ephesus (John Rooke, trans.)
description: The Ephesian Tale — one of the five complete ancient Greek novels — in John Rooke's 1727 English translation, the first ever.

title: Dictys Cretensis et Dares Phrygius: De Bello Trojano (Latin)
creator: Dictys of Crete; Dares the Phrygian
description: The Trojan War pseudo-chronicles in the 1825 Latin edition (documentary text — no public-domain English translation exists); the medieval West's authorities on Troy.

title: The Ante-Nicene Fathers, Vol. 1: The Apostolic Fathers, Justin Martyr, Irenaeus
creator: Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson (editors); A. Cleveland Coxe (American editor)
description: Volume 1 of the Ante-Nicene Fathers: the Apostolic Fathers (Clement of Rome, Mathetes, Polycarp, Ignatius, Barnabas, Papias), the works of Justin Martyr, and Irenaeus. Translated by Roberts, Donaldson, Dods, Reith, and Rambaut.

title: Irenaeus Against Heresies
creator: Irenaeus of Lyons
description: Irenaeus of Lyons' complete Against Heresies (Adversus Haereses), Books I-V, with fragments and elucidation. Translated by Rev. William H. Rambaut for the Ante-Nicene Fathers series.

title: Justin Martyr: The First and Second Apologies
creator: Justin Martyr
description: The First Apology and Second Apology of Justin Martyr, addressed to the Roman emperors. Translated by Rev. Marcus Dods for the Ante-Nicene Fathers series.

title: Justin Martyr: Dialogue with Trypho
creator: Justin Martyr
description: Justin Martyr's Dialogue with Trypho the Jew, the fullest 2nd-century Christian apologetic dialogue. Translated by Rev. George Reith for the Ante-Nicene Fathers series.

title: Ignatius of Antioch: The Epistles
creator: Ignatius of Antioch
description: The seven epistles of Ignatius of Antioch (shorter and longer versions), the Syriac versions, spurious epistles, and the Martyrdom of Ignatius. Translated by Roberts and Donaldson for the Ante-Nicene Fathers series.

title: Polycarp: Epistle to the Philippians and Martyrdom
creator: Polycarp of Smyrna
description: The Epistle of Polycarp to the Philippians and the Martyrdom of Polycarp. Translated by Roberts and Donaldson for the Ante-Nicene Fathers series.

title: Cyril of Alexandria: Five Tomes Against Nestorius
creator: Cyril of Alexandria
description: Cyril of Alexandria's Five Tomes Against Nestorius, with the Scholia on the Incarnation, That Christ is One, and fragments against Diodore of Tarsus, Theodore of Mopsuestia, and the Synousiasts. Translated by Edward Bouverie Pusey (Library of the Fathers, vol. 47).

title: Cyril of Alexandria: Commentary on the Gospel According to St. John
creator: Cyril of Alexandria
description: Cyril of Alexandria's Commentary on the Gospel of John, Books I-XII complete. Translated by P. E. Pusey (vol. 1, 1874) and Thomas Randell (vol. 2, 1885); Library of the Fathers vols. 43 and 48.

title: Cyril of Alexandria: Commentary on the Gospel According to St. Luke (156 Sermons)
creator: Cyril of Alexandria
description: Cyril of Alexandria's Commentary on the Gospel of Luke in 156 sermons, translated from a Syriac manuscript by R. Payne Smith (Oxford, 1859).

title: Charles Thomson's Translation of the Bible, Vol. 1 (Genesis-II Samuel)
creator: Charles Thomson
description: Volume 1 of Charles Thomson's 1808 translation of the Bible — the first English translation of the Septuagint published in America, translated directly from the Greek. Philadelphia: Jane Aitken.

title: Charles Thomson's Translation of the Bible, Vol. 2 (I Kings-Esther; Job-Song of Solomon)
creator: Charles Thomson
description: Volume 2 of Charles Thomson's 1808 translation of the Bible — the first English translation of the Septuagint published in America, translated directly from the Greek. Philadelphia: Jane Aitken.

title: Charles Thomson's Translation of the Bible, Vol. 3 (Prophets; Apocrypha)
creator: Charles Thomson
description: Volume 3 of Charles Thomson's 1808 translation of the Bible — the first English translation of the Septuagint published in America, translated directly from the Greek, including the Apocrypha. Philadelphia: Jane Aitken.

title: Charles Thomson's Translation of the Bible, Vol. 4 (New Testament)
creator: Charles Thomson
description: Volume 4 of Charles Thomson's 1808 translation of the Bible — the New Testament, translated directly from the Greek. The first American English Bible translation. Philadelphia: Jane Aitken.

title: The Syrian Churches, with a Literal Translation of the Four Gospels from the Peschito
creator: John Wesley Etheridge
description: John Wesley Etheridge's history of the Syrian churches, their liturgies and literature, with a literal English translation of the Four Gospels directly from the Syriac Peshitta. London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, 1846.

title: The New Testament of the Geneva Bible (1599 Edition, with the Geneva Notes)
creator: Geneva Bible translators (William Whittingham and others)
description: The complete New Testament of the Geneva Bible in the 1599 edition, with the famous Geneva study notes intact. The Bible of Shakespeare, Milton, Bunyan, and the Puritans.

title: The Coverdale Bible (1535), Bagster 1847 Reprint
creator: Miles Coverdale
description: The complete Coverdale Bible — the first complete printed English Bible (1535) — in Samuel Bagster's 1847 second modern edition, reprinting the original text in original spelling, with the Apocrypha. Translated by Miles Coverdale.

title: The Bishops' Bible (1572 Edition)
creator: Bishops' Bible translators (Matthew Parker and others)
description: The complete Bishops' Bible of 1572 — the officially authorized English Bible read in parish churches until the King James Version, and the KJV translators' base text. Transcribed from a facsimile scan; OCR is rough in places, especially the New Testament.

title: The Seven Books of Paulus Aegineta, Vol. 1
creator: Paulus Aegineta (Francis Adams, trans.)
description: Paulus Aegineta (c. 625-690), Adams 1844 — the Seven Books: the last great medical encyclopedia of antiquity and the standard surgical text for a thousand years; the bridge by which Greek medicine reached the Islamic world. Vol. 1 of 3.

title: The Seven Books of Paulus Aegineta, Vol. 2
creator: Paulus Aegineta (Francis Adams, trans.)
description: Paulus Aegineta (c. 625-690), Adams 1846 — the Seven Books: the last great medical encyclopedia of antiquity and the standard surgical text for a thousand years; the bridge by which Greek medicine reached the Islamic world. Vol. 2 of 3.

title: The Seven Books of Paulus Aegineta, Vol. 3
creator: Paulus Aegineta (Francis Adams, trans.)
description: Paulus Aegineta (c. 625-690), Adams 1847 — the Seven Books: the last great medical encyclopedia of antiquity and the standard surgical text for a thousand years; the bridge by which Greek medicine reached the Islamic world. Vol. 3 of 3, with weights-and-measures tables and general index.

title: Hipparchus: Commentary on the Phaenomena of Aratus and Eudoxus
creator: Hipparchus (Karl Manitius, ed.)
description: Hipparchus of Nicaea (c. 190-120 BC), Manitius 1894 Teubner edition — discoverer of the precession of the equinoxes, compiler of the first star catalogue, founder of trigonometry; this commentary on Aratus is his only surviving complete work. Greek text with German translation and Latin preface; no public-domain English translation exists (documentary text).

title: Pappus of Alexandria: The Mathematical Collection, Vol. 1
creator: Pappus of Alexandria (Friedrich Hultsch, ed.)
description: Pappus of Alexandria (c. 290-350), Hultsch 1876 — the Mathematical Collection: the single richest surviving source for lost works of Greek geometry, home of the Pappus centroid theorem. Vol. 1 (Books II-V). Greek text with Latin translation; no public-domain English translation exists (documentary text).

title: Pappus of Alexandria: The Mathematical Collection, Vol. 2
creator: Pappus of Alexandria (Friedrich Hultsch, ed.)
description: Pappus of Alexandria (c. 290-350), Hultsch 1877 — the Mathematical Collection: the single richest surviving source for lost works of Greek geometry. Vol. 2 (Books VI-VII, closing with the genuine TELOS of Book VII). Greek text with Latin translation; no public-domain English translation exists (documentary text).

title: Pappus of Alexandria: The Mathematical Collection, Vol. 3
creator: Pappus of Alexandria (Friedrich Hultsch, ed.)
description: Pappus of Alexandria (c. 290-350), Hultsch 1878 — the Mathematical Collection. Vol. 3 (Book VIII fragments, supplementa, and indices). Greek text with Latin translation; no public-domain English translation exists (documentary text).

title: Les œuvres de Zosime de Panopolis
creator: Zosimos of Panopolis
description: The complete surviving works of Zosimos of Panopolis (c. 300), the earliest named alchemical author — the Greek fountainhead of the art; French translation from Berthelot & Ruelle's critical edition.

title: Physica et mystica (Questions naturelles et mystérieuses)
creator: Pseudo-Democritus
description: Physica et mystica — the Graeco-Egyptian recipe-book attributed to Democritus (1st–2nd c.), the oldest stratum of Greek alchemy, with the Letter to Leucippe; French translation from Berthelot & Ruelle (1888).

title: Commentaire de Synésius sur le livre de Démocrite
creator: Synesius the alchemist
description: Synesius the alchemist's commentary on Pseudo-Democritus — the standard ancient teaching text of the art; French translation from Berthelot & Ruelle (1888).

title: Olympiodore — Sur l'art sacré
creator: Olympiodorus of Thebes (the alchemist)
description: Olympiodorus of Thebes' commentary on Zosimos (6th c.) — the Neoplatonic bridge carrying Alexandrian alchemy to Byzantium; French translation from Berthelot & Ruelle (1888).

title: De magna et sacra arte (On the Great and Sacred Art)
creator: Stephanos of Alexandria
description: Stephanos of Alexandria's lectures On the Great and Sacred Art (c. 620) — the Byzantine transmission of Alexandrian alchemy; Greek text from Ideler's critical edition (1842). No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Œuvres de Djâber (six traités)
creator: Jābir ibn Ḥayyān (Geber)
description: Six Arabic treatises of Jābir ibn Ḥayyān (c. 721–815), father of Arabic alchemy — the Jabirian corpus in French translation from Berthelot's L'alchimie arabe (1893). (Holmyard's 1928 edition could not be located in any digitized repository.)

title: De aluminibus et salibus (Of Alums and Salts)
creator: Muḥammad ibn Zakariyā al-Rāzī (attrib.)
description: The alchemical Book of Alums and Salts attributed to al-Rāzī (865–925) — Gerard of Cremona's Latin with Robert Steele's English translation, Isis vol. 12 (1929); the first Western work on preparing chemical substances for operations.

title: Introductorium in astronomiam
creator: Abū Maʿshar (Albumasar)
description: Abū Maʿshar's Introductorium maius (9th c.) — the Arabic systematization of astrology that taught the Latin West; Hermann of Dalmatia's Latin translation, printed 1489. No public-domain English translation exists (Lemay 1990s = copyright).

title: Isagoge ad magisterium iudiciorum astrorum
creator: Al-Qabīsī (Alcabitius)
description: Al-Qabīsī's Isagoge (10th c.) — the standard medieval beginners' introduction to astrology, with John of Saxony's commentary; Latin, Venice 1521. No public-domain English translation exists (Burnett/Yamamoto 2004 = copyright).

title: Pimander, sive De potestate et sapientia Dei
creator: Marsilio Ficino (translator); Hermes Trismegistus (attrib.)
description: Marsilio Ficino's 1463 Latin translation of the Corpus Hermeticum (printed 1481) — the translation that created Renaissance Hermeticism. No public-domain English translation of Ficino's Pimander exists (Copenhaver 1992 = copyright).

title: Asclepius (Latin)
creator: Hermes Trismegistus (attrib.)
description: The Latin Asclepius (2nd–4th c.) — the Hermetic dialogue on god, man, and the ensouled statues, in the Latin translation attributed to Apuleius of Madaura; Basel 1532.

title: Kore Kosmou (The Virgin of the World)
creator: Hermes Trismegistus (attrib.); translated by G. R. S. Mead
description: Kore Kosmou (The Virgin of the World) — Isis' revelation to Horus, the longest Hermetic excerpt preserved by Stobaeus; G. R. S. Mead's 1906 English translation, extracted as a standalone from Thrice-Greatest Hermes vol. 3.

title: Logic, in Three Books: Of Thought, of Investigation, and of Knowledge
creator: Hermann Lotze (Bernard Bosanquet, trans. and ed.)
description: Lotze’s System of Philosophy, Part I: his complete logic — of thought, of investigation, of knowledge — in Bosanquet’s 1884 Clarendon Press translation; the English form in which Lotze shaped British idealism and early analytic philosophy.

title: Metaphysic, in Three Books: Ontology, Cosmology, and Psychology
creator: Hermann Lotze (Bernard Bosanquet, trans. and ed.)
description: Lotze’s System of Philosophy, Part II: the complete Metaphysic — ontology, cosmology, psychology — in Bosanquet’s 1884 Clarendon Press translation; the metaphysical system that bridged German idealism and the new logic.

title: Microcosmus: An Essay Concerning Man and His Relation to the World
creator: Hermann Lotze (Elizabeth Hamilton and E. E. Constance Jones, trans.)
description: Lotze’s great synthesis of science, psychology, and philosophy — Books I–IX complete in 2 vols. (body, soul, life, man, mind, world, history, progress, the meaning of the world) — in the Hamilton/Jones English translation (1885; this scan 1888 reprint).

title: Psychologie vom empirischen Standpunkte
creator: Franz Brentano
description: DOCUMENTARY (German): Brentano’s 1874 founding work of descriptive psychology and intentionality — the book that launched phenomenology (Husserl), analytic philosophy of mind, and the Brentano school. First edition, complete as issued. No PD English translation exists.

title: Die Psychologie des Aristoteles, insbesondere seine Lehre vom nous poietikos
creator: Franz Brentano
description: DOCUMENTARY (German): Brentano’s 1867 doctoral dissertation on Aristotle’s psychology and the active intellect — the work Heidegger credited with setting him on the path to Being and Time. No PD English translation exists.

title: Quaestiones Quodlibetales
creator: John Duns Scotus (Luke Wadding, ed.; Franciscus Lychetus, comm.)
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Scotus’s Quodlibetal Questions — 21 disputed questions on God, the will, and metaphysics — from Wadding’s 1639 Opera Omnia, Tomus XII, with Lychetus’s commentary. No PD English translation exists.

title: Quaestiones in VIII libros Physicorum Aristotelis; Quaestiones in libros De Anima
creator: John Duns Scotus (Wadding ed.; Franciscus Pitigianus, annot.; Hugo Cavellus, suppl.)
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Scotus’s questions on Aristotle’s Physics (8 books) and De Anima, with the logical questions on the Isagoge and Categories, from the 1639 Wadding Opera Omnia. No PD English translation exists.

title: Disputationes quae De destructione destructionum Algazelis dicuntur; Tractatus de Animae beatitudine; Epistola de intellectu
creator: Averroes (Ibn Rushd); Calo Calonymos, trans.; Agostino Nifo, exp.
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Averroes’s Tahafut al-tahafut — the great refutation of al-Ghazali defending philosophy against theology — with his treatise on the beatitude of the soul and epistle on the intellect; Venice 1560 Giunta Tomus Decimus, Calonymos translation with Nifo’s exposition. No PD English translation exists.

title: Commentaria in libros Metaphysicorum Aristotelis
creator: Averroes (Ibn Rushd)
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Averroes’s great commentaries on Aristotle’s Metaphysics — Books I–XIII complete, with the epitome — the work that made him “the Commentator” for the Latin West; Venice 1560 Giunta Tomus Octavus. No PD English translation exists.

title: Colliget libri VII; Avicennae Cantica cum Averrois expositione; Collectaneorum sectiones tres
creator: Averroes (Ibn Rushd); Joannes Bruyerinus Campegius, trans.
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Averroes’s Colliget (Kulliyat) — his seven-book medical-philosophical compendium — with his exposition of Avicenna’s Cantica and the Collectanea; Venice 1560 Giunta Tomus Nonus. No PD English translation exists.

title: The Opus Majus of Roger Bacon
creator: Roger Bacon (Robert Belle Burke, trans.)
description: Bacon’s Opus Majus complete in 2 vols. — Parts One through Seven (the causes of error; theology and philosophy; language; mathematics; optics; experimental science; moral philosophy) — in Burke’s 1928 English translation, the first complete English rendering of the 13th-century program for experimental science.

title: The Book of the Lover and the Beloved
creator: Ramon Llull (E. Allison Peers, trans.)
description: Llull’s mystical classic — 366 prose poems of the Lover’s quest for the Beloved — in Peers’s 1923 English translation with his introductory essay on Llull’s life and the Lullian art.

title: Blanquerna: A Thirteenth Century Romance
creator: Ramon Llull (E. Allison Peers, trans.)
description: Llull’s Blanquerna — the great 13th-century philosophical romance tracing one soul’s ascent through the estates of the world to the papacy and hermit contemplation — in Peers’s 1926 English translation.

title: De divisione naturae libri quinque (Periphyseon); accedunt tredecim auctoris hymni
creator: Johannes Scottus Eriugena (C. B. Schlüter, ed.)
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Eriugena’s Periphyseon — all five books of the 9th-century division of nature, the first great speculative system of the Latin Middle Ages — with his thirteen hymns to Charles the Bald; Schlüter’s 1838 critical edition. No PD English translation exists.

title: Fons vitae ex arabico in latinum translatus ab Iohanne Hispano et Dominico Gundissalino
creator: Ibn Gabirol (Avicebron); John of Spain and Dominicus Gundissalinus, trans.; Clemens Baeumker, ed.
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): the Fons Vitae of Ibn Gabirol (Avicebron) — the 11th-century Jewish Neoplatonist’s metaphysics of universal matter and form, which shaped scholastic debates for centuries — in the medieval Latin translation, Baeumker’s 1892 critical edition. No PD English translation exists.

title: Libri IV Sententiarum
creator: Peter Lombard (Collegium S. Bonaventurae, ed.)
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Peter Lombard’s Sentences — Books I–IV complete in 2 vols. — the medieval theology textbook on which every scholastic master from Aquinas to Luther wrote a commentary; Quaracchi 1916 critical edition. No PD English translation exists.

title: Tria opuscula: Breviloquium; Itinerarium mentis in Deum; De reductione artium ad theologiam
creator: Bonaventure (Collegium S. Bonaventurae, ed.)
description: DOCUMENTARY (Latin): Bonaventure’s three great short works — the Breviloquium (the summa of Franciscan theology), the Itinerarium mentis in Deum (the soul’s six-stage ascent to God), and De reductione artium ad theologiam — Quaracchi 1911 edition. No complete PD English translation exists.

title: History of the Wars, Books I-II: The Persian War
creator: Procopius of Caesarea
description: Procopius's account of Justinian's wars against Sasanian Persia, in H. B. Dewing's Loeb translation (Vol. I, 1914). The essential primary source for 6th-century Byzantine-Persian warfare.

title: History of the Wars, Books III-IV: The Vandalic War
creator: Procopius of Caesarea
description: Procopius's account of Belisarius's reconquest of North Africa from the Vandals, in H. B. Dewing's Loeb translation (Vol. II, 1916).

title: History of the Wars, Books V-VI: The Gothic War (Part 1)
creator: Procopius of Caesarea
description: First half of Procopius's Gothic War narrative (Loeb Vol. III, 1916), covering Belisarius's Italian campaign through the siege of Rome.

title: History of the Wars, Books VI-VII: The Gothic War (Part 2)
creator: Procopius of Caesarea
description: Second half of the Gothic War (Loeb Vol. IV, 1924): the fall of Ravenna, Belisarius's recall, and the war's brutal latter phase.

title: History of the Wars, Books VII-VIII: The Gothic War (Part 3)
creator: Procopius of Caesarea
description: Conclusion of the Gothic War (Loeb Vol. V, 1928): Totila's resurgence, Narses's final victory, and the devastation of Italy.

title: Secret History
creator: Procopius of Caesarea
description: Procopius's scandalous unpublished invective against Justinian and Theodora, in Richard Atwater's 1927 translation. The most famous character assassination in ancient literature.

title: The Alexiad
creator: Anna Comnena
description: Anna Comnena's history of her father Alexius I's reign (1081-1118), in Elizabeth Dawes's 1928 translation. The first major historical work by a woman and the key Byzantine source for the First Crusade.

title: English History, Vol. I (1235-1249)
creator: Matthew Paris
description: Vol. I of J. A. Giles's translation of Matthew Paris's Chronica Majora (1235-1249). The fullest English medieval chronicle of the 13th century.

title: English History, Vol. II (1250-1259)
creator: Matthew Paris
description: Vol. II of Giles's Matthew Paris (1250-1259), covering the baronial reform movement and the road to the Barons' War.

title: English History, Vol. III (1259-1273)
creator: Matthew Paris
description: Vol. III of Giles's Matthew Paris (1259-1273) with the general index to Matthew Paris and Roger of Wendover.

title: On the Ruin of Britain
creator: Gildas
description: Gildas's 6th-century jeremiad on the fall of Roman Britain, in J. A. Giles's translation. The only narrative source for sub-Roman Britain.

title: Chronicle of the Kings of England
creator: William of Malmesbury
description: William of Malmesbury's Gesta Regum Anglorum (to 1127) in J. A. Giles's 1847 translation. The greatest English historian of the 12th century.

title: The Chronicle of Henry of Huntingdon
creator: Henry of Huntingdon
description: Henry of Huntingdon's Historia Anglorum (to 1154) in Thomas Forester's 1853 translation. A key 12th-century English chronicle.

title: Ecclesiastical History of England and Normandy, Vol. I
creator: Orderic Vitalis
description: Vol. I of Thomas Forester's translation of Orderic Vitalis's Historia Ecclesiastica. The fullest Norman chronicle of the 12th century.

title: Ecclesiastical History of England and Normandy, Vol. II
creator: Orderic Vitalis
description: Vol. II of Forester's Orderic Vitalis.

title: Ecclesiastical History of England and Normandy, Vol. III
creator: Orderic Vitalis
description: Vol. III of Forester's Orderic Vitalis.

title: Ecclesiastical History of England and Normandy, Vol. IV
creator: Orderic Vitalis
description: Vol. IV of Forester's Orderic Vitalis, completing the 4-volume set.

title: Flowers of History, Vol. I
creator: Roger of Wendover
description: Vol. I of J. A. Giles's translation of Roger of Wendover's Flores Historiarum. The St Albans chronicle tradition.

title: Flowers of History, Vol. II
creator: Roger of Wendover
description: Vol. II of Giles's Roger of Wendover, completing the set.

title: The Annals of Roger of Hoveden, Vol. I
creator: Roger of Hoveden
description: Vol. I of Henry Riley's translation of Roger of Hoveden's Chronica (to 1192). A key source for Henry II's reign.

title: The Annals of Roger of Hoveden, Vol. II
creator: Roger of Hoveden
description: Vol. II of Riley's Roger of Hoveden (1192-1201), covering Richard I and John.

title: The History of William of Newburgh
creator: William of Newburgh
description: William of Newburgh's Historia Rerum Anglicarum in Joseph Stevenson's 1853 translation. The most critical English historian of the 12th century.

title: Memoirs of Philip de Commines, Vol. I
creator: Philippe de Commynes
description: Vol. I (Books I-V) of Andrew Scoble's translation of Commynes's Mémoires. The first modern political memoir.

title: Memoirs of Philip de Commines, Vol. II
creator: Philippe de Commynes
description: Vol. II (Books VI-VIII plus Jean de Troyes's Scandalous Chronicle) of Scoble's Commynes.

title: The Works of Liudprand of Cremona
creator: Liutprand of Cremona
description: Liutprand's Antapodosis, Deeds of Otto, and Embassy to Constantinople in F. A. Wright's 1930 translation. The 10th-century Lombard diplomat's histories.

title: The Danish History
creator: Saxo Grammaticus
description: Saxo Grammaticus's Gesta Danorum (first nine books) in Oliver Elton's 1894 translation. The great Danish chronicle and source for Hamlet.

title: The Origins of the Islamic State, Part I
creator: al-Baladhuri
description: Part I of Philip Hitti's translation of al-Baladhuri's Futuh al-Buldan. The primary Arabic account of the early Islamic conquests.

title: The Origins of the Islamic State, Part II
creator: al-Baladhuri
description: Part II (Francis Murgotten, 1924) completing Hitti's translation of al-Baladhuri.

title: Meadows of Gold and Mines of Gems, Vol. I
creator: al-Masudi
description: Aloys Sprenger's 1841 partial English translation (Vol. I only) of al-Masudi's Muruj al-dhahab. The complete French translation is staged separately.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome I
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome I of Barbier de Meynard's complete French translation of al-Masudi's Muruj al-dhahab (1861-1877).

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome II
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome II of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome III
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome III of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome IV
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome IV of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome V
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome V of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome VI
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome VI of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome VII
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome VII of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome VIII
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome VIII of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi.

title: Les Prairies d'or, Tome IX
creator: al-Masudi
description: Tome IX of Barbier de Meynard's al-Masudi, completing the 9-volume set.

title: Memoirs of Usamah ibn-Munqidh
creator: Usama ibn Munqidh
description: Usama ibn Munqidh's Kitab al-I'tibar in Philip Hitti's 1929 translation. The great Crusader-era Syrian memoir.

title: The Babur-nama, Vol. I
creator: Babur
description: Vol. I of Annette Beveridge's translation of Babur's memoirs. The founder of the Mughal Empire's autobiography.

title: The Babur-nama, Vol. II
creator: Babur
description: Vol. II of Beveridge's Babur-nama, completing the set.

title: History of the Persians and Arabs in the Time of the Sasanians
creator: al-Tabari
description: Theodor Noldeke's 1879 German translation of the Sasanian portion of al-Tabari's History. The principal PD translation of Tabari.

title: A History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages, Vol. I
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. I of Lea's monumental History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages (1887-88) — the American scholarly foundation of modern Inquisition studies: origins, procedure, and the medieval tribunal in France and Italy.

title: A History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages, Vol. II
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. II of Lea's History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages — the Inquisition in the Iberian peninsula, Italy, and Germany; sorcery and witchcraft's medieval roots.

title: A History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages, Vol. III
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. III of Lea's History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages — special subjects: the Templars, Joan of Arc, Gilles de Rais, and the Inquisition's literature and organization.

title: A History of the Inquisition of Spain, Vol. 1
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. 1 of Lea's History of the Inquisition of Spain (1906-07) — the founding and organization of the Spanish Inquisition under Ferdinand and Isabella; the converso crisis.

title: A History of the Inquisition of Spain, Vol. 2
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. 2 of Lea's History of the Inquisition of Spain — jurisprudence, procedure, the auto de fe, and the tribunal's inner workings.

title: A History of the Inquisition of Spain, Vol. 3
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. 3 of Lea's History of the Inquisition of Spain — the spheres of action: blasphemy, sorcery, mysticism (alumbrados), and Protestantism under the Holy Office.

title: A History of the Inquisition of Spain, Vol. 4
creator: Henry Charles Lea
description: Vol. 4 of Lea's History of the Inquisition of Spain — decline and abolition; the Inquisition in the colonies, censorship, and the final suppression.

title: The History of the Inquisition, Vol. I
creator: Philipp van Limborch (Samuel Chandler, trans.)
description: Vol. I of Limborch's Historia Inquisitionis (1692) in Samuel Chandler's 1731 English translation — the classic Protestant history of the Inquisition, built on the Toulouse archives; the most-cited early modern account.

title: The History of the Inquisition, Vol. II
creator: Philipp van Limborch (Samuel Chandler, trans.)
description: Vol. II of Limborch's History of the Inquisition (Chandler trans., 1731) — the documentary appendix: sentences, edicts, and original instruments of the Holy Office.

title: Historia Inquisitionis (Latin)
creator: Philipp van Limborch
description: Limborch's Historia Inquisitionis (Amsterdam, 1692) in the original Latin — the classic Protestant history of the Inquisition and the edition Chandler translated in 1731. Staged alongside the English as the documentary original.

title: Liber Sententiarum Inquisitionis Tholosanae (Latin)
creator: Philipp van Limborch (ed.)
description: The Liber Sententiarum — the Book of Sentences of the Inquisition of Toulouse, 1307-1323, as published by Limborch in 1692: the primary documentary record of early-14th-century inquisitorial sentences against Cathars and Waldensians. Latin. First-order trial source.

title: The Life of St. Francis of Assisi
creator: Bonaventure (Miss Lockhart, trans.)
description: Bonaventure's Legenda Maior — the official Franciscan Life of St. Francis (c. 1260), in the 1915 English translation by Miss Lockhart. The Seraphic Doctor's mystical hagiography; the medieval biography par excellence.

title: Itinerarium Mentis ad Deum (Latin)
creator: Bonaventure (Karl Joseph von Hefele, ed.)
description: Bonaventure's Itinerarium Mentis in Deum (1259) — the Journey of the Mind to God, the central Franciscan mystical ascent text, in Hefele's 1861 Latin edition. No public-domain English translation exists; staged in Latin as a documentary text.

title: On Loving God
creator: Bernard of Clairvaux
description: Bernard of Clairvaux's De Diligendo Deo — On Loving God: the four degrees of love, the Cistercian classic of affective mysticism. 1910 London English edition (translator uncredited in scan).

title: Some Letters of Saint Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux
creator: Bernard of Clairvaux (Samuel J. Eales, trans. and ed.)
description: A selection from the letters of Bernard of Clairvaux in Samuel J. Eales's English translation (1904) — the Cistercian reformer's correspondence on theology, church politics, and the crusade.

title: Mysterium Baphometis Revelatum
creator: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall
description: Hammer-Purgstall's 1818 memoir in Fundgruben des Orients — the work that invented the modern Templar-idolatry/Baphomet thesis, arguing from trial records and artifacts that the Templars worshipped a Gnostic-Ophite idol. Latin with German notes. The single most consequential Templar-mythography text.

title: The Dialogue on Miracles, Vol. I
creator: Caesarius of Heisterbach (H. von E. Scott and C. C. Swinton Bland, trans.)
description: Vol. I of Caesarius of Heisterbach's Dialogus Miraculorum (c. 1219-23) in the 1929 Scott & Bland English translation — the Cistercian exempla collection, including firsthand Cathar episodes; the great medieval story-book of miracles, demons, and visions.

title: The Dialogue on Miracles, Vol. II
creator: Caesarius of Heisterbach (H. von E. Scott and C. C. Swinton Bland, trans.)
description: Vol. II of Caesarius's Dialogue on Miracles (Scott & Bland, 1929) — visions, temptations, and the moralized tales of the Cistercian novices; closes with the full index.

title: Practica Inquisitionis Heretice Pravitatis
creator: Bernard Gui (Célestin Douais, ed.)
description: Bernard Gui's Practica Inquisitionis Heretice Pravitatis — the inquisitor's manual of the Inquisitor of Toulouse (c. 1323-24), in Douais's 1886 Latin edition: interrogation formulae, sentences, and the descriptive catalogue of Cathar and Waldensian errors. The working handbook of the medieval Inquisition.

title: Summa de Catharis
creator: Rainier Sacconi (Martène and Durand, eds.)
description: Rainier Sacconi's Summa de Catharis et Leonistis — the ex-Cathar perfectus turned Dominican inquisitor's insider account of Cathar doctrine, hierarchy, and ritual (including the consolamentum), printed in Martène & Durand's Thesaurus Novus Anecdotorum, vol. V (1717). Latin. The closest-to-source Cathar doctrinal witness.

title: Adversus Catharos et Valdenses
creator: Moneta of Cremona (Tommaso Agostino Ricchini, ed.)
description: Moneta of Cremona's Adversus Catharos et Valdenses Libri Quinque (c. 1241) in Ricchini's 1743 Rome edition — the great Dominican scholastic summa against the Cathars and Waldensians, five books of systematic refutation. Latin. The high-medieval theological counter-offensive in full.

title: De Fide Catholica contra Haereticos (Latin)
creator: Alan of Lille
description: Alan of Lille's De Fide Catholica contra Haereticos, Libri Quatuor (c. 1200) — the 12th-century theological refutation of the Cathars, Waldensians, and other heretics, extracted from the 1855 Migne Patrologia Latina vol. 210 reprint. Latin. The first systematic anti-heretical summa of the schools.

title: Histoire générale des églises évangéliques des vallées de Piémont
creator: Jean-Paul Léger
description: Jean Léger's Histoire générale des églises évangéliques des vallées de Piémont, ou Vaudoises (1669) — the Waldensian pastor-historian's own record of his churches: doctrine and discipline (Livre I) and the persecutions culminating in the Piedmontese Easter of 1655 (Livre II). French. The Waldensian archive's founding history.

title: La Chanson de la croisade albigeoise, Tome I
creator: Anonymous (Paul Meyer, ed.)
description: Tome I of Paul Meyer's edition (1875-79) of La Chanson de la croisade albigeoise — the Provençal epic of the Albigensian Crusade, told from both the crusader and the Toulousain sides. Old French/Provençal with French apparatus. The crusade's great vernacular narrative.

title: La Chanson de la croisade albigeoise, Tome II
creator: Anonymous (Paul Meyer, ed.)
description: Tome II of Meyer's Chanson de la croisade albigeoise — continuation of the Provençal crusade epic with Meyer's notes, glossary, and the critical apparatus completing the edition.

title: Anecdotes historiques, légendes et apologues
creator: Etienne de Bourbon (A. Lecoy de la Marche, ed.)
description: Etienne de Bourbon's Anecdotes historiques, légendes et apologues (d. 1261), in Lecoy de la Marche's 1877 edition — the Dominican inquisitor's exempla treasury, rich in firsthand heresy episodes from the Languedoc inquisition. French (from the Latin Tractatus). The anecdotal archive of the Albigensian aftermath.

title: The History of the Inquisition, as it is Exercised at Goa
creator: Charles Dellon
description: Charles Dellon's Relation de l'Inquisition de Goa in the 1688 English translation — the French physician's firsthand account of arrest, interrogation, and the auto-da-fé at Goa (1676). The eyewitness narrative that carried the Inquisition's infamy across Protestant Europe.

title: The Life and Revelations of Saint Gertrude
creator: Gertrude the Great (Sister M. Frances Clare, trans.)
description: The Life and Revelations of Saint Gertrude the Great of Helfta (d. 1302) — the Herald of Divine Love (Legatus Divinae Pietatis) in the 1870 English translation by Sister M. Frances Clare of Kenmare. The great Helfta visionary's record of the Sacred Heart devotion at its source.

title: Gulshan-i Raz: The Mystic Rose Garden
creator: Mahmud Shabistari (E. H. Whinfield, trans.)
description: Shabistari's Gulshan-i Raz (1317), the great Persian Sufi didactic mathnawi — Whinfield's 1880 edition: English translation, introduction and Lahiji-commentary notes. Persian-text pages omitted (unscannable OCR mojibake); English matter complete.

title: Rabi'a the Mystic and Her Fellow-Saints in Islam
creator: Margaret Smith
description: Margaret Smith's 1928 Cambridge biography of Rabi'a al-Adawiyya (d. 801) — the first Western study of the first great woman mystic of Islam; with fellow-saints, women in early Islam, and Sufi doctrine.

title: The Divan, Vol. 1
creator: Hafez (H. Wilberforce Clarke, trans.)
description: Clarke's complete 1891 prose translation of Hafez's Divan, vol. 1 — the first complete English Divan, with critical and explanatory notes, preface on Sufism, and life of Hafez.

title: The Divan, Vol. 2
creator: Hafez (H. Wilberforce Clarke, trans.)
description: Clarke's complete 1891 prose translation of Hafez's Divan, vol. 2 — completing the first complete English Divan, with Clarke's copious commentary.

title: Lawa'ih: A Treatise on Sufism
creator: Jami (E. H. Whinfield & Mirza Muhammad Kazvini, trans.)
description: Jami's Lawa'ih (Flashes of Light) — Persian text with Whinfield and Kazvini's English translation (RAS, 1900), plus Whinfield's preface on Greek philosophy's influence on Sufism. Facsimile-page OCR omitted (mojibake); English matter complete.

title: Lalla-Vakyani
creator: Lalleshwari (Lal Ded) (George Grierson & Lionel Barnett, eds./trans.)
description: The vakhs (sayings) of Lal Ded, the 14th-century Kashmiri mystic — Grierson and Barnett's RAS edition (1920): text, translation, notes on yoga, language, metres, concordance and vocabulary.

title: The Word of Lalla the Prophetess
creator: Lalleshwari (Lal Ded) (Richard Carnac Temple, trans.)
description: Temple's 1924 Cambridge edition of Lal Ded's sayings — an independent English rendering of the Kashmiri mystic's vakhs, with introduction, notes and index.

title: Studies in Islamic Mysticism
creator: Reynold A. Nicholson
description: Nicholson's 1921 Cambridge collection — the foundational English studies in Sufi mysticism from the translator of Rumi's Mathnawi and Hujviri's Kashf al-Mahjub.

title: A Literary History of Persia, Vol. 1: From the Earliest Times until Firdawsi
creator: Edward G. Browne
description: Browne's Literary History of Persia, vol. 1 (1902) — the classic English survey; indispensable context for all Persian Sufi literature. Title page absent from scan; complete from preface.

title: A Literary History of Persia, Vol. 2: From Firdawsi to Sa'di
creator: Edward G. Browne
description: Browne's Literary History of Persia, vol. 2 (1928) — Firdawsi to Sa'di, covering the great age of Persian Sufi poetry.

title: A Literary History of Persia, Vol. 3: The Tartar Dominion (1265-1502)
creator: Edward G. Browne
description: Browne's Literary History of Persia, vol. 3 (1920) — the Tartar Dominion, closing with Jami; main text complete, index absent from scan.

title: A Literary History of Persia, Vol. 4: Modern Times (1500-1924)
creator: Edward G. Browne
description: Browne's Literary History of Persia, vol. 4 (1928) — modern times 1500-1924, completing the set.

title: The Life and Teaching of Tukaram
creator: J. Nelson Fraser & J. F. Edwards
description: Fraser and Edwards' Life and Teaching of Tukaram (1923) — the standard English life of the 17th-century Marathi poet-saint, with abhang translations; scanned from the 1932 reprint of the identical text.

title: Kitab al-Tawasin (French edition)
creator: Mansur al-Hallaj (Louis Massignon, ed.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French/Arabic): Massignon's 1913 Paris edition of Hallaj's Kitab al-Tawasin — Arabic text with French introduction, commentary and notes. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: The Kabbalah; or, The Religious Philosophy of the Hebrews
creator: Adolphe Franck (I. Sossnitz, trans.)
description: Franck's La Kabbale (1843) in Sossnitz's revised and enlarged 1926 English translation — the first modern critical history of Kabbalah.

title: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le livre de la splendeur), Tome 1
creator: attrib. Moses de Leon (Jean de Pauly, trans.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French): Jean de Pauly's complete French translation of the Zohar, tome 1 (1906) — the only complete public-domain translation; no complete PD English exists.

title: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le livre de la splendeur), Tome 2
creator: attrib. Moses de Leon (Jean de Pauly, trans.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French): de Pauly's Zohar, tome 2 (1907).

title: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le livre de la splendeur), Tome 3
creator: attrib. Moses de Leon (Jean de Pauly, trans.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French): de Pauly's Zohar, tome 3 (1908).

title: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le livre de la splendeur), Tome 4
creator: attrib. Moses de Leon (Jean de Pauly, trans.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French): de Pauly's Zohar, tome 4 (1909).

title: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le livre de la splendeur), Tome 5
creator: attrib. Moses de Leon (Jean de Pauly, trans.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French): de Pauly's Zohar, tome 5 (1909).

title: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le livre de la splendeur), Tome 6
creator: attrib. Moses de Leon (Jean de Pauly, trans.)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (French): de Pauly's Zohar, tome 6 (1911) — completing the only complete public-domain Zohar translation.

title: Die Kabbalah: Einführung in die jüdische Mystik und Geheimwissenschaft
creator: Erich Bischoff
description: Bischoff's 1923 illustrated introduction to Jewish mysticism (3rd ed.) — the standard German popular survey of Kabbalah.

title: De Verbo Mirifico (Latin)
creator: Johannes Reuchlin
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Latin): Reuchlin's De Verbo Mirifico (1514 Tübingen printing of the 1494 first edition) — the founding dialogue of Christian Kabbalah, on the wonder-working Word. Ends with the Tübingen colophon.

title: Sha'are Orah (Gates of Light) (Hebrew)
creator: Joseph Gikatilla
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Hebrew): Gikatilla's Sha'are Orah (c. 1300) — the classic exposition of the ten sefirot: introduction and all ten gates. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Sefer ha-Bahir (Hebrew)
creator: Anonymous
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Hebrew): Sefer ha-Bahir, the Book of Brightness (12th c.) — the first classic of medieval Kabbalah, all 200 sections. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Pardes Rimonim (Hebrew)
creator: Moses Cordovero
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Hebrew): Cordovero's Pardes Rimonim (1548) — the first comprehensive exposition of medieval Kabbalah, all 32 gates. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Etz Hayyim (Hebrew)
creator: Hayyim Vital (teachings of Isaac Luria)
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Hebrew): Hayyim Vital's Etz Hayyim — the authoritative recension of Isaac Luria's teachings, the foundation of Lurianic Kabbalah. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: De Harmonia Mundi Totius (Latin)
creator: Francesco Zorzi
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Latin): Zorzi's De harmonia mundi totius (Venice, 1525) — the great Franciscan synthesis of Neoplatonism and Christian Kabbalah; dedicated to Clement VII.

title: De Originibus (Latin)
creator: Guillaume Postel
description: DOCUMENTARY TEXT (Latin): Postel's De originibus (1553 Oporinus edition) — the wandering Christian kabbalist on Hebrew origins, Eastern traditions and the concord of peoples.

title: More Wonders of the Invisible World
creator: Robert Calef
description: Calef's 1700 Salem rebuttal — the great contemporary demolition of Cotton Mather's Wonders of the Invisible World, in five parts with the Margaret Rule narrative and the Parris dispute papers. The foundational skeptical document of the Salem episode.

title: Cases of Conscience Concerning Evil Spirits Personating Men
creator: Increase Mather
description: Increase Mather's 1693 Cases of Conscience — 'better ten suspected witches escape than one innocent be condemned': the prosecutorial brake that helped end the Salem trials, issued as the court's own ministerial guidance.

title: Dæmonolatreiæ Libri Tres
creator: Nicolas Rémy
description: Rémy's Daemonolatreiae (Lyon, 1595) in the original Latin — drawn from the capital trials of some 900 persons put to death in Lorraine. With the Malleus, the most important early work on demons and witches; the judge's casebook behind a generation of prosecutions. (English translation already held; this is the Latin original.)

title: Directorium Inquisitorum
creator: Nicholas Eymerich
description: Eymerich's Directorium Inquisitorum (1376) in the 1578 Rome edition with Francisco Peña's commentaries — the inquisitor's handbook for two centuries, with the witchcraft and sorcery sections that fed the Malleus tradition. The procedural root of the early-modern persecution.

title: Repetitio Disputationis de Lamiis seu Strigibus
creator: Thomas Erastus
description: Erastus's 1578 Basel disputation against Johann Weyer on witches — the Reformed physician-theologian's reply in the great 16th-century debate over the reality of witchcraft and the limits of skepticism.

title: Tractatus de Superstitionibus, contra Maleficia seu Sortilegia
creator: Martin of Arles
description: Martin of Arles's Tractatus de Superstitionibus (Rome, 1559; written 1517) — the Navarrese canon's systematic attack on maleficia and sortilegia then current, a bridge between medieval pastoral demonology and the 16th-century manuals.

title: Miscellaneous Reflections, Occasion'd by the Comet of December 1680, Vol. I
creator: Pierre Bayle
description: Bayle's Pensées diverses sur la comète (1682) in the 1708 English translation, vol. I — the great skeptical history of oracles and prodigies, demolishing comets-as-omens and popular superstition. A turning point of the early Enlightenment.

title: Miscellaneous Reflections, Occasion'd by the Comet of December 1680, Vol. II
creator: Pierre Bayle
description: Bayle's Pensées diverses sur la comète in the 1708 English translation, vol. II — continuation of the skeptical demolition of prodigies, oracles, and popular credulity.

title: De Erroribus circa Artem Magicam
creator: Jean Gerson
description: Gerson's De erroribus circa artem magicam (1402) — the Chancellor of Paris's early attack on magical errors and superstition, from the 1706 Dupin Opera omnia. The conciliar theologian's opening shot in the 15th-century demonological formation.

title: Histoire des Diables de Loudun
creator: Nicolas Aubin
description: Aubin's 1694 Histoire des diables de Loudun — the foundational French narrative of the Ursuline possessions and the trial and execution of Urbain Grandier (1634), drawn from the original documents. The closest-to-source PD account of the most famous possession case of the 17th century.

title: Histoire de Madeleine Bavent, Religieuse de Louviers
creator: Madeleine Bavent (attrib.)
description: The 1652 Histoire de Madeleine Bavent — the foundational first-person narrative of the Louviers possessions (1642-47), in the 1878 textual reprint with biographical notice and appendices (arrest, procès-verbal, récit véritable). The primary Louviers document.

title: Teatro Crítico Universal — Tomo Primero
creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Teatro Crítico Universal, tomo 1 (1773 Madrid edition) — the Spanish Enlightenment's great engine of desengaño: discourses exposing common errors, superstitions, false miracles and popular credulity across every field. The foundational skeptical work in Spanish.

title: Teatro Crítico Universal — Tomo Segundo
creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Teatro Crítico Universal, tomo 2 (1773 Madrid edition) — the Spanish Enlightenment's great engine of desengaño: discourses exposing common errors, superstitions, false miracles and popular credulity across every field. The foundational skeptical work in Spanish.

creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro

creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Teatro Crítico Universal, tomo 8 (1773 Madrid edition) — the Spanish Enlightenment's great engine of desengaño: discourses exposing common errors, superstitions, false miracles and popular credulity across every field. The foundational skeptical work in Spanish.

title: Cartas Eruditas, y Curiosas — Tomo Primero
creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Cartas Eruditas, y Curiosas, tomo 1 (1773) — the continuation of the Teatro Crítico's design: letters demolishing common errors and superstitions. Completes the author's great skeptical corpus.

creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Cartas Eruditas, y Curiosas, tomo 2 (1773) — the continuation of the Teatro Crítico's design: letters demolishing common errors and superstitions. Completes the author's great skeptical corpus.

creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Cartas Eruditas, y Curiosas, tomo 4 (1773) — the continuation of the Teatro Crítico's design: letters demolishing common errors and superstitions. Completes the author's great skeptical corpus.

creator: Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro
description: Feijóo's Cartas Eruditas, y Curiosas, tomo 5 (1773) — the continuation of the Teatro Crítico's design: letters demolishing common errors and superstitions. Completes the author's great skeptical corpus.

title: Sendbrieff, oder Bericht an alle, welche von der newen Brüderschafft dess Ordens vom Rosen-Creutz genandt
creator: Julianus de Campis
description: Julianus de Campis’ 1615 Sendbrieff — one of the earliest printed responses to the Rosicrucian Fama, addressing all who had read of the new Brotherhood of the Rose Cross. A primary document of the 1614–1616 manifesto controversy.

title: Ad responsum Florentini de Valentia — kurtze Duplic und Antwort (1618)
creator: F. G. Menapius
description: F. G. Menapius’s 1618 Duplic: his rejoinder to Florentinus de Valentia’s Rosa florescens, in the pamphlet war over the Rosicrucian manifestos. A first-hand voice from the 1617–1618 controversy.

title: Antikrisis ad responsum Florentini de Valentia (1618)
creator: F. G. Menapius
description: The 1618 Antikrisis: Menapius’s counter to Florentinus de Valentia’s defense of the Rosicrucian brotherhood — the critic’s side of the 1618 pamphlet exchange.

title: Cento Virgilianus de Fratribus Roseae Crucis (1618)
creator: F. G. Menapius
description: Menapius’s 1618 Cento Virgilianus: a Virgilian cento on the Brothers of the Rose Cross — the manifesto controversy carried into Latin verse, a unique literary artifact of the Rosicrucian furor.

title: Rosa florescens contra F. G. Menapii calumnias (1618)
creator: Florentinus de Valentia
description: Florentinus de Valentia’s 1618 Rosa florescens: the Benedictine’s point-by-point rebuttal of F. G. Menapius’s 1617 calumnies against the Rosicrucian society — the defense brief of the manifesto controversy.

title: Clypeum veritatis: kurtze jedoch gründliche Antwort (1618)
creator: Friedrich Grick
description: Friedrich Grick’s 1618 Clypeum veritatis (Shield of Truth): a thorough answer in the Rosicrucian pamphlet war, engaging Menapius’s charges — one of the fullest contemporary defenses of the manifestos’ claims.

title: Epitimia Fr. R.C.: endliche Offenbahrung oder Entdeckung (1619)
creator: Irenäus Agnostus
description: Irenäus Agnostus’s 1619 Epitimia: a “final revelation” on the Fraternity R.C., closing the 1617–1619 pamphlet cycle over the Rosicrucian manifestos.

title: Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer aus dem 16ten und 17ten Jahrhundert
creator: Anonymous (Gold- und Rosenkreuzer)
description: The Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785–88): the 18th-century Gold- und Rosenkreuzer order’s own emblem book — sixteen engraved symbolic plates with the order’s alchemical-theosophical doctrine, the order’s most famous publication.

title: Die Wolke über dem Heiligthum
creator: Karl von Eckartshausen
description: Eckartshausen’s Die Wolke über dem Heiligthum (1802): the classic of the “interior Church” — six letters on the hidden community of the elect, the work that carried Rosicrucian-theosophical ideas into the Golden Dawn, Theosophy, and Martinism.

title: The Cloud upon the Sanctuary
creator: Karl von Eckartshausen, trans. Isabel de Steiger
description: Isabel de Steiger’s English translation of Eckartshausen’s Cloud upon the Sanctuary, as serialized in A. E. Waite’s The Unknown World (1895) — the translation that put the “interior Church” before the Golden Dawn generation; Waite pressed it on the young Crowley.

title: Histoire de la magie, du monde surnaturel et de la fatalité à travers les temps et les peuples
creator: Paul Christian (Jean-Baptiste Pitois)
description: Paul Christian’s Histoire de la magie (1870): the great 19th-century French history of magic — from antiquity through the grimoire tradition — by the bibliophile-occultist of the Arsenal library, a founding text of the French occult revival’s historical imagination.

title: Le Musée des sorciers, mages et alchimistes
creator: Émile-Jules Grillot de Givry
description: Grillot de Givry’s Le Musée des sorciers (1929): the great illustrated museum of sorcerers, mages, and alchemists — a visual and documentary history of the grimoire tradition from the Middle Ages to the 18th century.

title: Das Kloster, weltlich und geistlich — Band 1 (Erste bis vierte Zelle)
creator: Johann Scheible (editor)
description: Johann Scheible’s Das Kloster, Band 1 (Erste bis vierte Zelle): the great 19th-century German anthology of folk magic, chapbooks, and popular literature — grimoires, Faust books, Höllenzwänge, and folk charms in complete reprints. The central source-anthology of the German grimoire tradition.
