description: Schweinfurth's travels in the Bahr-el-Ghazal and the lands of the Niam-niam (1868–71) — the great German naturalist's exploration of the unknown Sudan.

title: The Heart of Africa, Vol. II
creator: Georg Schweinfurth
description: Schweinfurth's travels in the unexplored Sudan — the Niam-niam, the Monbuttoo, and the pygmies of the Congo forest.

title: A Voyage of Discovery to the North Pacific Ocean, and Round the World, Vol. III
creator: George Vancouver
description: The official account of Vancouver's survey of the Pacific Northwest (1791–95) — vol. III of the 1798 first edition.

title: A Voyage to Terra Australis, Vol. I
creator: Matthew Flinders
description: Flinders' circumnavigation of Australia in HMS Investigator (1801–03) — the voyage that named Australia.

title: A Voyage to Terra Australis, Vol. II
creator: Matthew Flinders
description: Flinders' voyage continued — the Porpoise shipwreck and six and a half years' imprisonment at Mauritius.

title: Narrative of a Journey to the Shores of the Polar Sea, 1819–22
creator: John Franklin
description: Franklin's overland expedition to the Coppermine River and the Arctic coast (1819–22) — the journey of starvation and endurance that made his name.

title: Voyages from Montreal
creator: Alexander Mackenzie
description: Mackenzie's voyages to the Arctic Ocean (1789) and across the Rockies to the Pacific (1793) — the first transcontinental crossing of North America.

title: The Naturalist on the River Amazons
creator: Henry Walter Bates
description: Bates' eleven years on the Amazon (1848–59) — the naturalist's classic that founded the study of mimicry.

title: The Lake Regions of Central Africa
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's expedition with Speke to the great lakes (1857–59) — the search for the Nile's source and the discovery of Tanganyika.

title: First Footsteps in East Africa
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's disguised pilgrimage to Harar (1854–55) — the first European to enter the forbidden city and live.

title: How I Found Livingstone
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's 1871 expedition across Africa to Ujiji — 'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?' and the finding of the lost explorer.

title: The Congo and the Founding of Its Free State, Vol. I
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's founding of the Congo Free State (1879–84) — the Emin Pasha relief expedition's prelude and the scramble for the Congo.

title: The Congo and the Founding of Its Free State, Vol. II
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's Congo narrative continued — stations, treaties, and the making of the Free State.

title: Narrative of an Expedition to the Zambesi and Its Tributaries
creator: David Livingstone
description: Livingstone's Zambesi expedition (1858–64) — the Universities' Mission, the Shire highlands, and the discovery of Lake Nyasa.

title: A Voyage to the Pacific Ocean, Vol. I
creator: James Cook
description: The official account of Cook's third voyage (1776–79) — the search for the Northwest Passage and the discovery of Hawaii.

title: The Voyage of the Vega Round Asia and Europe, Vol. I
creator: Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld
description: Nordenskiöld's Vega expedition (1878–80) — the first transit of the Northeast Passage.

title: The Voyage of the Vega Round Asia and Europe, Vol. II
creator: Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld
description: The Vega expedition continued — wintering off Siberia and the triumphant return through Asia.

title: A Journey from Prince of Wales's Fort in Hudson's Bay to the Northern Ocean
creator: Samuel Hearne
description: Hearne's overland journey to the Coppermine River and the Arctic Ocean (1769–72) — the first European to reach the Arctic coast overland, with Matonabbee.

title: Report of the Exploring Expedition to the Rocky Mountains
creator: John C. Frémont
description: Frémont's report of the 1842 and 1843–44 expeditions — the 'Pathfinder's' survey that opened the Oregon Trail and California.

title: The Expeditions of Zebulon Montgomery Pike, Vol. I
creator: Zebulon Montgomery Pike (Elliott Coues, ed.)
description: Pike's journals of the 1805–06 Mississippi and 1806–07 southwestern expeditions, in Coues' definitive edition.

title: The Expeditions of Zebulon Montgomery Pike, Vol. II
creator: Zebulon Montgomery Pike (Elliott Coues, ed.)
description: Pike's southwestern expedition continued — across the plains, the Sangre de Cristos, and capture by the Spanish.

title: The Expeditions of Zebulon Montgomery Pike, Vol. III
creator: Zebulon Montgomery Pike (Elliott Coues, ed.)
description: Pike's expedition concluded — Santa Fe, Chihuahua, and the return through Texas; with the appendices.

title: The Oldest Code of Laws in the World
creator: Hammurabi (C. H. W. Johns, trans.)
description: C. H. W. Johns' landmark English translation of the Code of Hammurabi (c. 1754 BC) — 282 laws on commerce, family, labor and justice, the oldest substantially complete written legal code — with Johns' introduction on Babylonian law. Transcribed from the 1903 T. & T. Clark edition.

title: Ancient Laws and Institutes of England, Vol. I
creator: Benjamin Thorpe (ed.)
description: Vol. I of the Record Commission edition of the Anglo-Saxon dooms — the laws of AEthelberht, Alfred, Cnut and others — with facing-page English translation. The foundational source collection for early English law.

title: Ancient Laws and Institutes of England, Vol. II
creator: Benjamin Thorpe (ed.)
description: Vol. II of the Record Commission edition — the later Anglo-Saxon and Anglo-Norman legal texts, with Thorpe's glossary and indexes. Completes the great 1840 source collection of early English law.

title: The History of the Common Law of England
creator: Matthew Hale
description: Chief Justice Hale's posthumous history — the common law versus statute law, the Saxon and Norman roots of English law, the courts and their evolution. The first great historical account of the common-law tradition, staged from the 1713 first edition.

title: Bracton's Note Book, Vol. I: Introduction and Apparatus
creator: Henry de Bracton (F. W. Maitland, ed.)
description: Vol. I of Maitland's edition of Bracton's case notes — introduction and apparatus to the nearly 2,000 plea-roll cases (1217-1240) that underlie Bracton's De Legibus, the first great English law treatise.

title: Bracton's Note Book, Vol. II: Text
creator: Henry de Bracton (F. W. Maitland, ed.)
description: Vol. II of Maitland's Bracton's Note Book — the plea-roll cases themselves, the raw judicial material from which Bracton built his treatise on the laws of England.

title: Bracton's Note Book, Vol. III: Text
creator: Henry de Bracton (F. W. Maitland, ed.)
description: Vol. III of Maitland's Bracton's Note Book — the remaining plea-roll cases with indexes, completing the edition of the 13th-century case law behind De Legibus.

title: The Law of Nations; or, Principles of the Law of Nature
creator: Emer de Vattel (Joseph Chitty, ed.)
description: Vattel's 1758 classic of international law in Joseph Chitty's English edition with notes — the textbook of diplomacy and the law of nations, constantly cited by the American founders.

title: A Treatise on the Law of Obligations, or Contracts
creator: Robert Joseph Pothier (William David Evans, trans.)
description: Pothier's treatise on obligations — the French civilian foundation of modern contract law and the principal source of the Code civil's contract provisions — in Evans' 1806 English translation with introduction, appendix and notes on English law.

title: The Civil Law in its Natural Order, Vol. I
creator: Jean Domat (William Strahan, trans.; Luther S. Cushing, ed.)
description: Vol. I of Domat's rationalist restatement of Roman private law — 'the oracle of the civil law' — in Strahan's English translation as re-edited by Cushing: the bridge from Roman law to the Code Napoleon.

title: The Civil Law in its Natural Order, Vol. II
creator: Jean Domat (William Strahan, trans.; Luther S. Cushing, ed.)
description: Vol. II of Domat's Civil Law in its Natural Order — successions, obligations and the public law — completing Cushing's edition of Strahan's translation.

title: The Code Napoleon; or, The French Civil Code
creator: France (Commission of the Code Napoleon)
description: The 1804 Code civil in the 1827 English translation — the most influential civil code in history, the model for codes across Europe, Latin America and beyond.

title: Lectures on Jurisprudence; or, The Philosophy of Positive Law, Vol. I
creator: John Austin (Robert Campbell, ed.)
description: Vol. I of Austin's lectures — the command theory of law: sovereignty, commands, sanctions, the province of jurisprudence. The founding work of analytical jurisprudence, in Campbell's 5th edition.

title: Lectures on Jurisprudence; or, The Philosophy of Positive Law, Vol. II
creator: John Austin (Robert Campbell, ed.)
description: Vol. II of Austin's lectures — rights, persons, things, and the applications of the command theory across the divisions of law. Completes Campbell's 5th edition.

title: Lectures on Jurisprudence, Vol. III: Notes and Fragments
creator: John Austin
description: The posthumous third volume of Austin's Lectures — notes and fragments first published from his manuscripts in 1863, the sequel to The Province of Jurisprudence Determined.

title: Village-Communities in the East and West
creator: Henry Sumner Maine
description: Maine's six lectures on the village community as the primitive legal unit — India, Russia, England — extending Ancient Law's comparative method to property and the 'from status to contract' thesis.

title: Dissertations on Early Law and Custom
creator: Henry Sumner Maine
description: Maine's later essays — sovereignty, the king in early law, theories of primitive society, the natural state of mankind. The mature statement of his historical jurisprudence.

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. I
creator: Joseph Story
description: Vol. I of Justice Story's great commentary — the constitutional history of the colonies and states before 1787. The most cited American constitutional treatise of the 19th century, from the 1833 first edition.

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. II
creator: Joseph Story
description: Vol. II of Story's Commentaries — the legislature, the executive, and the powers of Congress under the Constitution.

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. III
creator: Joseph Story
description: Vol. III of Story's Commentaries — the judiciary, the states, amendments, and the forms of process. Completes the 1833 first edition.

title: Commentaries on American Law, Vol. I
creator: James Kent
description: Vol. I of Chancellor Kent's Commentaries — 'the American Blackstone': the law of nations, government, and constitutional law. The foundational American legal treatise, staged from the 1828 printing of vol. I.

title: Commentaries on American Law, Vol. III
creator: James Kent
description: Vol. III of Kent's Commentaries (2nd ed., 1832) — real property: feudal tenures, estates, and the American law of land.

title: A Treatise on the Constitutional Limitations which Rest upon the Legislative Power of the States of the American Union
creator: Thomas M. Cooley
description: Cooley's Constitutional Limitations (2nd ed., 1871) — the 19th century's leading treatise on due process, vested rights and the police power; the intellectual charter of American laissez-faire constitutionalism.

title: A First Book of Jurisprudence for Students of the Common Law
creator: Frederick Pollock
description: Pollock's introduction to legal theory for common-law students — the nature of law, the state, rights, duties and the sources of law. The standard English jurisprudence textbook of its generation.

title: The History of English Law before the Time of Edward I, Vol. I
creator: Frederick Pollock and Frederic William Maitland
description: Vol. I of Pollock and Maitland's History — the masterpiece of English legal historiography: the Anglo-Saxon age, the Norman conquest, and the making of the common law. 1895 first edition.

title: The History of English Law before the Time of Edward I, Vol. II
creator: Frederick Pollock and Frederic William Maitland
description: Vol. II of Pollock and Maitland's History — the doctrines of the common law to 1272: tenure, the courts, procedure, crime and tort. Completes the 1895 first edition.

title: English Law and the Renaissance
creator: Frederic William Maitland
description: Maitland's 1901 Rede Lecture — how the English common law survived the Renaissance reception of Roman law that transformed the Continent. The classic essay on England's legal exceptionalism.

title: A History of English Law, Vol. I
creator: William Searle Holdsworth
description: Vol. I of Holdsworth's monumental History (3rd ed., 1922) — the judicial system: the courts and their development. The standard reference history of English law.

title: A History of English Law, Vol. II
creator: William Searle Holdsworth
description: Vol. II of Holdsworth's History (3rd ed., 1922) — Anglo-Saxon and Norman law, the sources of English law.

title: A History of English Law, Vol. III
creator: William Searle Holdsworth
description: Vol. III of Holdsworth's History (3rd ed., 1922) — the medieval common law: the development of the courts and the legal profession.

title: The Geneva Bible (1560)
creator: William Whittingham and others
description: The Geneva Bible of 1560 — the first full edition of the Bible of the English exiles at Geneva (Whittingham, Coverdale, Goodman, Gilby, Sampson, Cole); the first English Bible with verse divisions, the Bible of Shakespeare and the Pilgrims. Complete Old and New Testaments with Apocrypha, from a 1560 printing.

title: The Great Bible (1539)
creator: Myles Coverdale
description: The Great Bible of 1539 — 'the Byble in Englyshe', the first authorized English Bible, prepared by Myles Coverdale under Thomas Cromwell and set up in every English parish; the revision of Matthew's Bible that the Geneva translators then revised in turn. Complete Old and New Testaments.

title: Matthew's Bible (1537)
creator: John Rogers (as Thomas Matthew)
description: Matthew's Bible of 1537 — John Rogers' compilation under the pseudonym Thomas Matthew, combining Tyndale's New Testament and Pentateuch with Coverdale's rendering of the rest; the pivotal bridge edition between Tyndale and the Great Bible, the first Bible printed in England under royal licence. Complete Old and New Testaments.

title: Biblia: Die gantze Heilige Schrifft Deudsch (Luther, 1545)
creator: Martin Luther
description: The Luther Bible of 1545 — 'Biblia: das ist: Die gantze Heilige Schrifft Deudsch, auffs new zugerichtet', printed by Hans Lufft at Wittenberg; the last edition overseen by Luther himself ('Ausgabe letzter Hand'), the translation that shaped the German language. Complete Bible in the original Early New High German.

title: Forerunners and Rivals of Christianity, Vol. 1: From 330 B.C. to 330 A.D.
creator: Francis Legge
description: Francis Legge's history of Christianity's forerunners and rivals — Vol. 1 (1915), covering the pre-Christian religious world: Alexander's conquests, the Alexandrian divinities, the origin of Gnosticism, and the pre-Christian Gnostics. Companion to the already-hosted Vol. 2 on the post-Christian Gnostic systems.

title: The Apostolic Tradition of Hippolytus (Easton translation)
creator: Hippolytus of Rome; translated by Burton Scott Easton
description: Burton Scott Easton's 1934 English translation — with introduction and notes — of Hippolytus of Rome's Apostolic Tradition (c. 215 AD), the earliest surviving church order, describing early Christian ordination, baptism, and eucharistic practice in detail. Public domain (Project Gutenberg).

title: Treaty of Westphalia (1648) — Treaty of Münster
creator: Holy Roman Emperor and King of France (plenipotentiaries)
description: The 1648 Treaty of Münster — the principal instrument of the Peace of Westphalia, ending the Thirty Years’ War. English translation.

title: Instrument of Government (1653)
creator: England (Council of Officers; drafted by John Lambert)
description: The 1653 Instrument of Government — England’s first codified constitution, establishing the Protectorate.

title: Edit de Nantes (1598) — Edict of Nantes
creator: Henri IV of France
description: The 1598 Edict of Nantes — Henri IV’s edict of religious toleration for French Protestants (French original).

title: Locke
creator: Samuel Alexander
description: Samuel Alexander's 1908 study of John Locke in the Philosophical Classics series.

title: Of God and His Creatures: An Annotated Translation (with some Abridgement) of the Summa Contra Gentiles
creator: Thomas Aquinas (Joseph Rickaby, trans.)
description: Rickaby's 1905 annotated English rendering of Aquinas's Summa Contra Gentiles, covering all four books (abridged): the obtainable complete public-domain English SCG.

title: Compendium Maleficarum
creator: Francesco Maria Guazzo (Montague Summers, trans./ed.)
description: Guazzo's 1608 witch-hunter's manual in Montague Summers's 1929 English translation: the classic early-modern demonology of witchcraft prosecution and its remedies.

title: Philosophie als strenge Wissenschaft
creator: Edmund Husserl
description: Husserl's 1911 programmatic essay 'Philosophy as Rigorous Science' (Logos, vol. I): the founding manifesto of the phenomenological movement. Extracted from the complete Logos I volume; German.

title: The Jesuit Relations and Allied Documents, Vol. 26
creator: Reuben Gold Thwaites (ed.)
description: Vol. 26 (Lower Canada) of Reuben Gold Thwaites's 73-volume edition of the Jesuit Relations (1896-1901): the foundational documentary corpus of the North American indigenous missions. Completes vols. 1-30.

title: The Institutes of Justinian
creator: Justinian I (J. B. Moyle, trans.)
description: Moyle's translation of Justinian's Institutes (1906 ed.): alternate English rendering to the Sandars 1874 translation already in the library.

title: Second Characters; or, The Language of Forms
creator: Anthony Ashley Cooper, Earl of Shaftesbury (Benjamin Rand, ed.)
description: Shaftesbury's Second Characters (ed. Benjamin Rand, 1914): the posthumous second series of the Characteristics, on art, aesthetics and the language of forms.

title: The Damnable Life and Death of One Stubbe Peeter, a Most Wicked Sorcerer
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1590 English pamphlet on Peter Stumpp (Stubbe Peeter), executed 1589 for murders, lycanthropy and witchcraft: the founding werewolf pamphlet of early modern England.

title: Textes philosophiques
creator: Léon Wieger
description: Wieger's 1906 French collection of Chinese philosophical and religious texts. French.

title: A Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy, Vol. 1
creator: Thomas Young
description: Vol. 1 of Thomas Young's 1807 Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy and the Mechanical Arts: the polymath's great physics lectures. Completes the set with Vol. 2 (already in the library).

The Complexity of Defining and Separating Fixpoint Formulae in Modal Logic
creator: Jean Christoph Jung ORCID:0000-0002-4159-2255, Jędrzej Kołodziejski ORCID:0000-0001-5008-9224
description: Abstract . Modal separability for modal fixpoint formulae is the problem to decide for two given modal fixpoint formulae φ , φ ′ \varphi,\varphi^{\prime} whether there is a modal formula ψ \psi that separates them, in the sense that φ ⊧ ψ \varphi\models\psi and ψ ⊧ ¬ φ ′ \psi\models\neg\varphi^{\prime} .

title: T-duality and bosonization as examples of continuum gauging and disentangling
creator: Gertian Roose, Erez Zohar
description: Abstract Dualities and duality transformations form a well established methodology in various aspects of quantum many body physics and quantum field theories, allowing one to exploit equivalence between models which may naively seem completely different in order to gain access to further physical regimes, either analytically, numerically or experimentally.

title: Hype or not? Formalizing Automatic Promotional Language Detection in Biomedical Research
creator: Bojan Batalo, Erica K. Shimomoto, Neil Millar
description: Abstract In science, promotional language (’hype’) is increasing and can undermine objective evaluation of evidence, impede research development, and erode trust in science. In this paper, we introduce the task of automatic detection of hype, which we define as hyperbolic or subjective language that authors use to glamorize, promote, embellish, or exaggerate aspects of their research.

title: UniDex: Rethinking Search Inverted Indexing with Unified Semantic Modeling Conference: Proceedings of the xxx; Beijing; China the Preprint Version of UniDex, Beijing, China DOI: 10.1145/xxxxx ISBN: xxxxx/2025/09 CCS: Information systems Novelty in information retrieval
creator: Zan Li † , Jiahui Chen † , Yuan Chai ∗† , Xiaoze Jiang ∗† , Xiaohua Qi † , Zhiheng Qin, Runbin Zhou, Shun Zuo, Guangchao Hao, Kefeng Wang, Jingshan Lv, Yupeng Huang, Xiao Liang, Han Li
description: Abstract . Inverted indexing has traditionally been a cornerstone of modern search systems, leveraging exact term matches to determine relevance between queries and documents. However, this term-based approach often emphasizes surface-level token overlap, limiting the system’s generalization capabilities and retrieval effectiveness.

title: Capture and escape from the 2:1 resonance between Ariel and Umbriel in a fast-migration scenario of the Uranian system
creator: M. Rossi, G. Lari, M. Falletta, C. Grassi, S.R.A. Gomes, M. Saillenfest
description: Abstract Recent measurements and theoretical developments suggest that Uranus may exhibit a higher tidal dissipation than previously assumed. This enhanced dissipation leads to a faster orbital migration of its five major moons: Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, and Oberon. Consequently, when studying their orbital evolution, resonant encounters that have always been discarded in previous works need to be included.

title: Hill-Type Stability Analysis of Periodic Solutions of Fractional-Order Differential Equations
creator: Paul-Erik Haacker 1, Remco I. Leine 1, Renu Chaudhary 2, Kai Diethelm 2, André Schmidt 1, Safoura Hashemishahraki 2
description: Abstract This paper explores stability properties of periodic solutions of (nonlinear) fractional-order differential equations (FODEs). As classical Caputo-type FODEs do not admit exactly periodic solutions, we propose a framework of Liouville-Weyl-type FODEs, which do admit exactly periodic solutions and are an extension of Caputo-type FODEs.

title: Reconstructing Quantum States and Expectations via Dynamical Tomography
creator: Marco Peruzzo, Tommaso Grigoletto, Francesco Ticozzi
description: Abstract When the dynamics of a quantum system of interest is known, an informationally-complete set of observables is not needed for state reconstruction via tomographic techniques: letting the system evolve before performing the measurement allows one to effectively extend the available ways to probe the system.

title: Symplectic Singularities, Color Confinement, and the Quantum Dirac Sheaf
description: Abstract A singularity ℂ 2 ​ r / G {\mathbb{C}}^{2r}/G , with G G a split symplectic reflection group, may or may not be crepant. Then the total space 𝒳 \mathscr{X} of the Donagi-Witten integrable system is crepant for some 4d 𝒩 = 2 {\cal N}=2 SCFT and non-crepant for others. Which physical mechanism controls the (dis)crepancy?

title: Can you SPLICE it together? A Human Curated Benchmark for Probing Visual Reasoning in VLMs
creator: Mohamad Ballout, Okajevo Wilfred, Seyedalireza YaghoubiNohayr Muhammad Abdelmoneim , Julius Mayer , Elia Bruni Institute of Cognitive Science, Osnabrück University, Osnabrück, Germany mohamad.ballout@uos.de
description: Abstract In this work, we introduce SPLICE, a human-curated benchmark derived from the COIN instructional video dataset, designed to probe event-based reasoning across multiple dimensions: temporal, causal, spatial, contextual, and general knowledge. SPLICE includes 3,381 human-filtered videos spanning 12 categories and 180 sub-categories, such as sports, engineering, and housework. These videos are segmented into a total of 11,423 event clips.

title: Investigating the Task Load of Investigating the Task Load in Visualization Studies
creator: Daniel Pahr and Sara Di Bartolomeo
description: Abstract The NASA task load index (short: NASA-TLX) is a common metric to evaluate the workload of a user in a visualization study. Yet, it is rarely performed as initially intended, as the sources-of-workload evaluation is often omitted for various reasons.

title: Strong BSD for abelian surfaces and the Bloch-Beilinson conjecture
creator: Kalyan Banerjee
description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove the Bloch-Beilinson conjecture for certain abelian surfaces over ℚ {\mathbb{Q}} , provided that the BSD is known for these abelian surfaces. 1. Introduction One of the most important problems in algebraic geometry is to compute the Chow groups for higher codimensional cycles on a smooth projective variety.

title: Observability estimates for the Schrödinger equation on the equilateral triangle
creator: Paul Alphonse, David Lafontaine
description: Abstract . We prove observability estimates for the Schrödinger equation posed on the equilateral triangle in the plane, under both Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions. No geometric control condition is required on the rough localization functions that we consider. This is the first result of this kind on a non-toric domain in the compact setting.

title: VoxCPM: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Context-Aware Speech Generation and True-to-Life Voice Cloning
description: Abstract Generative models for speech synthesis face a fundamental trade-off: discrete tokens ensure stability but sacrifice expressivity, while continuous signals retain acoustic richness but suffer from error accumulation due to task entanglement. This challenge has driven the field towards multi-stage pipelines that rely on pre-trained speech tokenizers, but these create a semantic-acoustic divide, limiting holistic and expressive speech generation.

title: “Stop replacing salt with sugar!”: Towards Intuitive Human-Agent Teaching
creator: Nikolaos Kondylidis, Andrea Rafanelli *, Ilaria Tiddi, Annette ten Teije, Frank van Harmelen
description: Abstract Humans quickly learn new concepts from a small number of examples. Replicating this capacity with Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems has proven to be challenging. When it comes to learning subjective tasks–where there is an evident scarcity of data–this capacity needs to be recreated.

title: HyperHELM: Hyperbolic Hierarchy Encoding for mRNA Language Modeling
creator: Max van Spengler, Artem Moskalev, Tommaso Mansi, Mangal Prakash, Rui Liao
description: Abstract Language models are increasingly applied to biological sequences like proteins and mRNA, yet their default Euclidean geometry may mismatch the hierarchical structures inherent to biological data. While hyperbolic geometry provides a better alternative for accommodating hierarchical data, it has yet to find a way into language modeling for mRNA sequences.

title: VNODE: A Piecewise Continuous Volterra Neural Network
creator: Siddharth Roheda, Aniruddha Bala, Rohit Chowdhury, Rohan Jaiswal
description: Abstract This paper introduces Volterra Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (VNODE), a piecewise continuous Volterra Neural Network that integrates nonlinear Volterra filtering with continuous‑time neural ordinary differential equations for image classification. Drawing inspiration from the visual cortex, where discrete event processing is interleaved with continuous integration, VNODE alternates between discrete Volterra feature extraction and ODE‑driven state evolution.

title: Tree-based formulation for the multi-commodity flow problem
creator: Simon Spoorendonk, Bjørn Petersen
description: Abstract We introduce a tree-based formulation for the minimum-cost multi-commodity flow problem that addresses large-scale instances. The method decomposes the source-based model by representing flows as convex combinations of trees rooted at source nodes, and solves the resulting formulation with column generation.

title: Automated Discovery of Gadgets in Quantum Circuits for Efficient Reinforcement Learning
creator: Oleg M. Yevtushenko, Florian Marquardt
description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven itself as a powerful tool for the discovery of quantum circuits and quantum protocols. We have recently shown that including composite quantum gates – referred to as “gadgets” – in the action space of RL agents substantially enhances the RL performance Olle et al. 2025 in the context of quantum error correction.

title: Limiting behaviour of pattern counts in biased binary strings
creator: Jon V. Kogan and Nicolò Paviato
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jon V. Kogan and Nicolò Paviato. For p ∈ ( 0 , 1 ) p\in(0,1) , sample a binary sequence from the infinite product measure of Bernoulli ( p ) (p) distributions. It is known that for p = 1 / 2 p=1/2 , almost every binary sequence is Poisson generic in the sense of Peres and Weiss, a property that reflects a specific statistical pattern in the frequency of finite substrings.

title: Successful Misunderstandings: Learning to Coordinate Without Being Understood
creator: Nikolaos Kondylidis, Anil Yaman, Frank van Harmelen, Erman Acar, Annette ten Teije
description: Abstract The main approach to evaluating communication is by assessing how well it facilitates coordination. If two or more individuals can coordinate through communication, it is generally assumed that they understand one another. We investigate this assumption in a signaling game where individuals develop a new vocabulary of signals to coordinate successfully.

title: Magnetoelectric Switching of Competing Magnetic Orders in Rhombohedral Graphene
creator: Kilian Krötzsch, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Arnaud Magrez, Mitali Banerjee
description: Abstract A finite Hall conductance under zero magnetic field implies time reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking due to magnetic ordering. In rhombohedral (RH) stacked graphene, the angular momentum breaking TRS can result from the orbital degree of freedom at the K K and K ′ K^{\prime} valleys.

title: Community detection robustness of graph neural networks
creator: Jaidev Goel, Pablo Moriano, Ramakrishnan Kannan, Yulia R. Gel
description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly widely used for community detection in attributed networks. They combine structural topology with node attributes through message passing and pooling. However, their robustness or lack of thereof with respect to different perturbations and targeted attacks in conjunction with community detection tasks is not well understood.

title: Study of nuclear magnetic resonance spectra with the multi-model multi-level quantum complex exponential least squares algorithm
creator: Antonio Márquez Romero, Josh J.M. Kirsopp, Giuseppe Buonaiuto, Michal Krompiec
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antonio Márquez Romero, Josh J.M. Kirsopp, Giuseppe Buonaiuto, Michal Krompiec. We present a novel application of the multi-modal, multi-level quantum complex exponential least squares (MM-QCELS) algorithm, a state-of-the-art, early fault-tolerant quantum phase estimation (QPE) technique, to the simulation and analysis of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) of spin systems. By leveraging the robustness and precision of MM-QCELS, we demonstrate enhanced phase resolution in quantum simulations of spin dynamics, also in systems with complex coupling topologies.

title: Strong Correlations and Superconductivity in the Supermoiré Lattice
creator: Zekang Zhou 1, Cheng Shen 1, Kryštof Kolář 2, Kenji Watanabe 3, Takashi Taniguchi 4, Cyprian Lewandowski 5,6, Mitali Banerjee 1,7,†
description: Abstract The supermoiré lattice, arising from the interference of multiple moiré patterns, dramatically reshapes the electronic band structure by introducing new minibands and modifying band dispersion. Concurrently, strong electronic interactions within moiré flat bands lead to the emergence of various correlated states. However, the impact of the supermoiré lattice on the flat band systems with strong interactions remains largely unexplored.

title: Hierarchical Analysis and Control of Epidemic Spreading over Networks using Dissipativity and Mesh Stability
creator: Shirantha Welikala, Hai Lin, Panos J. Antsaklis
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shirantha Welikala, Hai Lin, Panos J. Antsaklis. Analyzing and controlling spreading processes are challenging problems due to the involved non-linear node (subsystem) dynamics, unknown disturbances, complex interconnections, and the large-scale and multi-level nature of the problems. The dissipativity concept provides a practical framework for addressing such concerns, thanks to the energy-based representation it offers for subsystems and the compositional properties it provides for the analysis and control of interconnected (networked) systems comprised of such subsystems.

title: Continuation strategies to mitigate convergence to low-performing local optima in dynamic topology optimization
creator: Tom De Weer, Vanessa Cool, Elke Deckers
description: Abstract Solving dynamic topology optimization problems often yields low-performing local optima. Instead of converging towards a design that exploits dynamic mechanisms, a less interesting, mass-driven solution is often generated. This necessitates repeated and computationally expensive optimization reruns before a suitable optimum is found.

title: The influence of solute induced memory on interface migration
creator: C. W. Sinclair, J. Rottler
description: Abstract Interface migration governs microstructural evolution during phase transformations and grain growth thereby dictating those material properties that depend on microstructure. Recent work continues to highlight the rich range of behaviors exhibited by migrating interfaces and the complex connection between these behaviors and the underlying atomistic processes that determine coarse-grained interfacial mobility.

title: Advancing Zero-Shot Open-Set Speech Deepfake Source Tracing
creator: Manasi Chhibber, Jagabandhu Mishra, Tomi H. Kinnunen
description: Abstract We propose a novel zero-shot source tracing framework inspired by advances in speaker verification. Specifically, we adapt the SSL-AASIST system for attack classification, ensuring that the attacks used for training are disjoint from those used to form fingerprint–trial pairs.

title: Impedance Modeling of Magnetometers: A Path Toward Low-Noise Readout Circuits
creator: *, Eric Elzenheimer, Elizaveta Spetzler, Pablo Mendoza, Daniel Fernández, Jordi Madrenas, Jeffrey McCord, Michael Höft, Robert Rieger, Andreas Bahr
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by *, Eric Elzenheimer, Elizaveta Spetzler, Pablo Mendoza, Daniel Fernández, Jordi Madrenas, Jeffrey McCord, Michael Höft, Robert Rieger, Andreas Bahr. Optimizing sensor readout schemes and integrated circuit designs for both open-loop and closed-loop implementations requires precise modeling and simulation strategies. This study introduces a novel two-port impedance model to estimate the behavior of a converse Magnetoelectric (cME) sensor.

title: Traumatic Brain Injury Segmentation using an Ensemble of Encoder-decoder Models
creator: Ghanshyam Dhamat, Vaanathi Sundaresan
description: Abstract The identification and segmentation of moderate-severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) lesions pose a significant challenge in neuroimaging. This difficulty arises from the extreme heterogeneity of these lesions, which vary in size, number, and laterality, thereby complicating downstream image processing tasks such as image registration and brain parcellation, reducing the analytical accuracy.

title: YITP-25-149
creator: KEK-TH-2759
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by KEK-TH-2759. The parity solution to the strong CP problem necessarily extends the Standard Model to include the SU ( 2 ) R (2)_{\rm R} gauge sector and imposes restrictions on the structure of the Yukawa interactions. In this framework, one can consider an appealing structure of the neutrino sector in which the smallness of the neutrino masses is naturally explained, while lepton number symmetry is substantially violated at the TeV scale.

title: The polarization problem for the honeycomb structure Thanks: This research was funded in whole or in part by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) [ 10.55776/PAT5102224 ].
creator: Markus Faulhuber
description: Abstract . We study the polarization problem in dimension 2 for the honeycomb structure and compare it to the maximal polarization lattice, the hexagonal lattice. As expected, the hexagonal lattice has higher polarization than the honeycomb at all densities. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 52C25, 74G65 1.

title: From order to chaos: the blurred out metallicity gradient of the Gaia-Enceladus/Sausage progenitor 2015 From order to chaos: the blurred out metallicity gradient of the Gaia-Enceladus/Sausage progenitor – A
creator: Andreia Carrillo, Alis J. Deason, Azadeh Fattahi, Robert J. J. Grand, Francesca Fragkoudi
description: Abstract The powerful combination of Gaia with other Milky Way large survey data has ushered in a deeper understanding of the assembly history of our Galaxy, which is marked by the accretion of Gaia-Enceladus/Sausage (GES). As a step towards reconstructing this significant merger, we examine the existence and destruction of its stellar metallicity gradient.

title: 𝒦 ​ ℒ \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} and Lyapunov Approaches for Discrete-time Peak Computation Problems
creator: Assalé Adjé
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a method to solve discrete-time peak computation problems (DPCPs for short). DPCPs are optimization problems that consist of maximizing a function over the reachable values set of a discrete-time dynamical system. The optimal value of a DPCP can be rewritten as the supremum of the sequence of optimal values.

title: Circuit-Aware Reward Training: A Mechanistic Framework for Longtail Robustness in RLHF
creator: Jing Liu
description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) reward models exhibit systematic failures on longtail distributions, leading to reward hacking and misalignment. We propose a mechanistic interpretability framework that identifies specialized neural circuits responsible for rare-event processing in reward models. Drawing from recent advances showing distributed specialization for rare tokens in language models [ Liu 2025 , Liu et al.

title: MemGen: Weaving Generative Latent Memory for Self-Evolving Agents
creator: Guibin Zhang, Muxin Fu, Shuicheng Yan
description: Abstract Agent memory shapes how Large Language Model (LLM)-powered agents, akin to the human brain, progressively refine themselves through environment interactions. Existing paradigms remain constrained: parametric memory forcibly adjusts model parameters, and retrieval-based memory externalizes experience into structured databases, yet neither captures the fluid interweaving of reasoning and memory that underlies human cognition.

title: CoTune: Co-evolutionary Configuration Tuning ∗ Tao Chen is the corresponding author. Gangda Xiong is also supervised in the IDEAS Lab.
creator: Gangda Xiong 1 and Tao Chen 2∗
description: Abstract To automatically tune configurations for the best possible system performance (e.g., runtime or throughput), much work has been focused on designing intelligent heuristics in a tuner. However, existing tuner designs have mostly ignored the presence of complex performance requirements (e.g., “ the latency shall ideally be 2 seconds ”), but simply assume that better performance is always more preferred.

title: SenSE: Semantic-Aware High-Fidelity Universal Speech Enhancement
creator: Xingchen Li, Hanke Xie, Ziqian Wang, Zihan Zhang, Longshuai Xiao, Lei Xie
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xingchen Li, Hanke Xie, Ziqian Wang, Zihan Zhang, Longshuai Xiao, Lei Xie. Generative universal speech enhancement (USE) methods aim to leverage generative models to improve speech quality under various types of distortions. Diffusion- or flow-based generative models are capable of producing enhanced speech with high quality and fidelity. However, they typically achieve speech enhancement by learning an acoustic feature mapping from degraded speech to clean speech, while lacking awareness of high-level semantic information.

title: Evaluation of Polarimetric Fusion for Semantic Segmentation in Aquatic Environments Thanks: This research was partially supported by the French Agence Nationale de la Recherche, under grant ANR-23-CE23-0030 (project R3AMA) * These authors contributed equally to this work.
creator: Luis F. W. Batista * , Tom Bourbon * , Cédric Pradalier
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luis F. W. Batista * , Tom Bourbon * , Cédric Pradalier. Accurate segmentation of floating debris on water is often compromised by surface glare and changing outdoor illumination. Polarimetric imaging offers a single-sensor route to mitigate water-surface glare that disrupts semantic segmentation of floating objects. We benchmark state-of-the-art fusion networks on PoTATO, a public dataset of polarimetric images of plastic bottles in inland waterways, and compare their performance with single-image baselines using traditional models.

title: Diamonds in the rough: Transforming SPARCs of imagination into a game concept by leveraging medium sized LLMs
creator: Julian Geheeb, Farhan Abid Ivan, Daniel Dyrda, Miriam Anschütz, Georg Groh
description: Abstract Recent research has demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can support experts across various domains, including game design. In this study, we examine the utility of medium-sized LLMs—models that operate on consumer-grade hardware typically available in small studios or home environments.

title: Quasi-Ergodic Control of Multi-Periodic Autoregressive Processes: Formulation and Examples
creator: Vyacheslav Kungurtsev
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vyacheslav Kungurtsev. This work considers state dynamics driven by Periodic Autoregressive Moving Average noise, and control of the system over time. Such processes appear frequently in applications involving the environment, such as energy and agriculture. Managing these systems applying forecasts to make decisions that exhibit foresight and risk aversion while maximizing profits is a challenging control problem that can be computationally difficult for standard scenario-based methods.

title: MAD: Manifold Attracted Diffusion
creator: Dennis Elbrächter, Giovanni S. Alberti, Matteo Santacesaria
description: Abstract Score-based diffusion models are a highly effective method for generating samples from a distribution of images. We consider scenarios where the training data comes from a noisy version of the target distribution, and present an efficiently implementable modification of the inference procedure to generate noiseless samples.

title: An asymptotic field approach for the control of dipole emission in integrated structures
creator: Vincenzo Macrì ID, Alice Viola ID, Marco Liscidini
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vincenzo Macrì ID, Alice Viola ID, Marco Liscidini. We present a general framework to model spontaneous emission in integrated photonic structures by exploiting quantization of the electromagnetic field in terms of asymptotic in/out modes. This approach allows for an efficient and physically meaningful calculation of the emission rate into each radiative channel of an arbitrary structure, without relying on approximations such as Lorentzian lineshapes or point-like system-bath coupling.

title: Socratic-Zero: Bootstrapping Reasoning via Data-Free Agent Co-evolution
creator: Shaobo Wang Zhengbo Jiao Zifan Zhang Yilang Peng, Xu Ze Boyu Yang Wei Wang Hu Wei Linfeng Zhang, * Equal contribution Corresponding authors
description: Abstract Recent breakthroughs in large language models (LLMs) on reasoning tasks rely heavily on massive, high-quality datasets—typically human-annotated and thus difficult to scale. While data synthesis or distillation offers a promising alternative, existing methods struggle with inconsistent data quality and an inability to dynamically adapt to the evolving capabilities of the model, leading to suboptimal training signals.

title: Beyond Softmax: A Natural Parameterization for Categorical Random Variables
creator: Alessandro Manenti, Cesare Alippi
description: Abstract Latent categorical variables are frequently found in deep learning architectures. They can model actions in discrete reinforcement-learning environments, represent categories in latent-variable models, or express relations in graph neural networks. Despite their widespread use, their discrete nature poses significant challenges to gradient-descent learning algorithms.

title: Direct numerical simulation of two-phase flows with surfactant-induced surface viscous effects Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
creator: Debashis Panda, Seungwon Shin ∗, Abdullah M. Abdal, Lyes Kahouadji, Jalel Chergui, Damir Juric ∗∗, Omar K. Matar
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Debashis Panda, Seungwon Shin ∗, Abdullah M. Abdal, Lyes Kahouadji, Jalel Chergui, Damir Juric ∗∗, Omar K. Matar. Direct numerical simulations of interfacial flows with surfactant-induced complexities involving surface viscous stresses are performed within the framework of the Level Contour Reconstruction Method (LCRM); this hybrid front-tracking/level-set approach leverages the advantages of both methods.

title: Discrete Variational Autoencoding via Policy Search
creator: Michael Drolet, Firas Al-Hafez, Aditya Bhatt, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Michael Drolet, Firas Al-Hafez, Aditya Bhatt, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz. Discrete latent bottlenecks in variational autoencoders (VAEs) offer high bit efficiency and can be modeled with autoregressive discrete distributions, enabling parameter-efficient multimodal search with transformers. However, discrete random variables do not allow for exact differentiable parameterization; therefore, discrete VAEs typically rely on approximations, such as Gumbel-Softmax reparameterization or straight-through gradient estimates, or employ high-variance gradient-free methods such as REINFORCE that have had limited success on high-dimensional tasks such as image reconstruction.

title: Dynamic Pricing of an Expiring Item under Strategic Buyers with Stochastic Arrival
creator: Suyeon Choi, Changhyun Kwon, Seungki Min
description: Abstract Problem definition: We study the optimal dynamic pricing for an expiring ticket or voucher, sold by a time-sensitive seller to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically with random private values. The item’s expiring nature creates a fundamental conflict: the seller’s pressure to sell before expiration leads to price reductions, which in turn incentivizes buyers to wait for a better deal.

title: A TRIANGLE Enables Multimodal Alignment Beyond Cosine Similarity
creator: Giordano Cicchetti, Eleonora Grassucci, Danilo Comminiello
description: Abstract Multimodal learning plays a pivotal role in advancing artificial intelligence systems by incorporating information from multiple modalities to build a more comprehensive representation. Despite its importance, current state-of-the-art models still suffer from severe limitations that prevent the successful development of a fully multimodal model. Such methods may not provide indicators that all the involved modalities are effectively aligned.

title: Bundle Network: a Machine Learning-Based Bundle Method
creator: Francesca Demelas, Antonio Frangioni, Mathieu Lacroix, Joseph Le Roux, Emiliano Traversi, Roberto Wolfler Calvo
description: Abstract This paper presents Bundle Network , a learning-based algorithm inspired by the Bundle Method for convex non-smooth minimization problems. Unlike classical approaches that rely on heuristic tuning of a regularization parameter, our method automatically learns to adjust it from data.

title: SymBoltz.jl: a symbolic-numeric, approximation-free and differentiable linear Einstein-Boltzmann solver
creator: Herman Sletmoen
description: Abstract SymBoltz is a new Julia package that solves the linear Einstein-Boltzmann equations. It features a symbolic-numeric interface for specifying equations, is free of approximation switching schemes and is compatible with automatic differentiation. Cosmological models are built from replaceable physical components in a way that scales well in model space.

title: Cofinal families of finite VC-dimension Thanks: The first author would like to thank the Israel Science Foundation for partial support of this research (Grant 1302/23). The second author would like to thank the Israel Science Foundation for partial support of this research (Grant no. 804/22).
creator: Omer Ben-Neria, Itay Kaplan, George Peterzil
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Omer Ben-Neria, Itay Kaplan, George Peterzil. Given infinite cardinals θ ≤ κ \theta\leq\kappa , we ask for the minimal VC-dimension of a cofinal family ℱ ⊆ [ κ ] < θ \mathcal{F}\subseteq[\kappa]^{<\theta} . We show that for θ = ω \theta=\omega and κ = ℵ n \kappa=\aleph_{n} it is consistent with ZFC that there exists such a family of VC-dimension n + 1 n+1 , which is known to be the lower bound.

title: Resolution of the Borel–Kolmogorov Paradox via the Maximum Entropy Principle
creator: Raphaël Trésor Mykola Lukashchuk
description: Abstract This paper presents a rigorous resolution of the Borel–Kolmogorov paradox using the Maximum Entropy Principle. We construct a metric-based framework for Bayesian inference that uniquely extends conditional probability to events of null measure. The results unify classical Bayes’ rules and provide a robust foundation for Bayesian inference in metric spaces.

title: Laboratory and Synchrotron Validation of µ-XRF for Sulfur Mapping in CTMP Paper Samples
creator: and B. Norlin
description: Abstract The transition toward renewable, fiber-based packaging requires an improved understanding of chemical modifications in high-yield pulps such as chemithermomechanical pulp (CTMP). Sulfonation uniformity is essential for the energy-efficient production of high-strength CTMP pulp. However, laboratory methods only measure total sulfur and cannot illustrate its distribution at the fiber level, which can be visualized using µ-XRF.

title: ProxyAttn: Guided Sparse Attention via Representative Heads
creator: Yixuan Wang, Huang He, Siqi Bao, Haifeng Wang, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che
description: Abstract The quadratic complexity of attention mechanisms limits the efficiency of Large Language Models (LLMs) on long-text tasks. Recently, methods that dynamically estimate block importance have enabled efficient block sparse attention, leading to significant acceleration in long-text pre-filling of LLMs. However, their coarse-grained estimation inevitably leads to performance degradation at high sparsity rates.

title: Is Turbulence able to Generate Magnetic Islands in Tokamaks? Gyrokinetic Simulations of Turbulence-Driven Magnetic Islands in Toroidal Geometry
creator: F. Widmer, E. Poli, A. Mishchenko, A. Ishizawa, T. Hayward-Schneider, A. Bottino
description: Abstract We report a universal mechanism for turbulence-driven magnetic islands in fusion plasmas. Using gyrokinetic simulations of a linearly stable tearing mode in a large-aspect-ratio toroidal geometry under collisionless conditions, we demonstrate that micro-instabilities generate an 𝑬 × 𝑩 {\boldsymbol{E}}\times{\boldsymbol{B}} flow that drives magnetic field line reconnection.

title: A Quantum Computer Based on Donor-Cluster Arrays in Silicon
creator: Shihang Zhang, Chunhui Zhang, Guanyong Wang, Tao Xin, Guangchong Hu, Yu He, Peihao Huang
description: Abstract Significant advances in silicon spin qubits highlight the potential of silicon quantum dots for scalable quantum computing, given their compatibility with industrial fabrication and long coherence times. In particular, phosphorus (P)-doped spin qubits possess excellent coherence and have demonstrated high-fidelity two-qubit gates exceeding 99.9%.

title: One-sided Hom shifts
creator: Marie-Pierre Béal ID, Alexi Block Gorman
description: Abstract We prove that it is decidable whether a one-sided shift of finite type is conjugate to a one-sided Hom-shift, and whether a tree-shift of finite type is conjugate to a Hom tree-shift. The proof uses Williams’s theory for one-sided shifts. 1 Introduction We consider two types of shift spaces, shifts of sequences and tree-shifts.

title: Geometric structure of stationary problem for spatial 1D self-diffusion equation with logistic growth
creator: Yu Ichida
description: Abstract This paper considers the solution structure of non-trivial, non-constant stationary states of 1D spatial parabolic equations with nonlinear self-diffusion and logistic growth terms. A two-dimensional ordinary differential equation satisfying the stationary problem is derived and all its dynamics, including to infinity, is revealed by the Poincaré-Lyapunov compactification, one of the compactifications of phase space.

title: The real-time QCD static potential at high temperature
creator: Margaret E. Carrington, Cristina Manuel, Joan Soto
description: Abstract We develop a procedure to analytically calculate higher-order contributions to the high-temperature real-time static potential in QCD. It is based on the introduction of a semi-hard external scale, which lies between the hard scale (the temperature) and the soft scale (the screening mass), and the method of integration by regions.

title: When risk defies order: On the limits of fractional stochastic dominance
creator: Christian Laudagé, Felix-Benedikt Liebrich
description: Abstract . Motivated by recent work on monotone additive statistics and questions regarding optimal risk sharing for return-based risk measures, we investigate the existence, structure, and applications of Meyer risk measures . Those are monetary risk measures consistent with fractional stochastic orders suggested by Meyer 1977a , Meyer 1977b as refinement of second-order stochastic dominance (SSD).

title: Autoregressive Processes on Stiefel and Grassmann Manifolds Journal: JOURNALTOFIND
creator: Jordi-Lluís Figueras, Aron Persson
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jordi-Lluís Figueras, Aron Persson. System identification of autoregressive processes on Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds are presented and studied. We define the system parameters as elements in the orthogonal group and we show that the system can be estimated by averaging over observations. Then we propose an algorithm on how to compute these system parameters using conjugate gradient descent on Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds, respectively.

title: FESTIM v2.0: Upgraded framework for multi-species hydrogen transport and enhanced performance
creator: James Dark, Rémi Delaporte-Mathurin, Jørgen S. Dokken, Huihua Yang, Chirag Khurana, Kaelyn Dunnell, Gabriele Ferrero, Vladimir Kulagin, Samuele Meschini
description: Abstract FESTIM is an open-source finite element framework for modelling the transport of hydrogen isotopes in materials. It provides a flexible and extensible tool for simulating diffusion, trapping, surface interactions, and other processes that govern hydrogen behaviour. This paper presents FESTIM v2.0, a major release that broadens both the physical scope and the software infrastructure of the framework.

title: Demonstration of quantum error detection in a silicon quantum processor
creator: Chunhui Zhang, Chunhui Li, Zhen Tian, Yan Jiang, Feng Xu, Shihang Zhang, Hao Wang, Yu-Ning Zhang, Xuesong Bai, Baolong Zhao, Yi-Fei Zhang, Huan Shu, Jiaze Liu, Kunrong Wu, Chao Huang, Keji Shi, Mingchao Duan, Tao Xin, Peihao Huang, Tianluo Pan, Song Liu, Guanyong Wang, Guangchong Hu, Yu He, Dapeng Y
description: Abstract Quantum error detection is essential in realizing large-scale universal quantum computation, especially for quantum error correction (QEC). However, key elements for FTQC have yet to be realized in silicon qubits. Here, we demonstrate quantum error detection on a donor-based silicon quantum processor comprising four-nuclear spin qubits and one electron spin as an auxiliary qubit.

title: Spatial-Functional awareness Transformer-based graph archetype contrastive learning for Decoding Visual Neural Representations from EEG Thanks: Citation : Authors. Title. Pages…. DOI:000000/11111.
creator: Yueming Sun, Long Yang
description: Abstract Decoding visual neural representations from Electroencephalography (EEG) signals remains a formidable challenge due to their high-dimensional, noisy, and non-Euclidean nature. In this work, we propose a Spatial-Functional Awareness Transformer-based Graph Archetype Contrastive Learning (SFTG) framework to enhance EEG-based visual decoding.

title: LatentEvolve: Self-Evolving Test-Time Scaling in Latent Space
creator: Guibin Zhang, Fanci Meng, Guancheng Wan, Zherui Li, Kun Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Lei Bai, Shuicheng Yan
description: Abstract Test-time Scaling (TTS) has been demonstrated to significantly enhance the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) during the inference phase without altering model parameters. However, existing TTS methods are largely independent, implying that LLMs have not yet evolved to progressively learn how to scale more effectively.

title: Surjective Independence of Causal Influences for Local Bayesian Network Structures
creator: Kieran Drury, Martine J. Barons, Jim Q. Smith
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kieran Drury, Martine J. Barons, Jim Q. Smith. The very expressiveness of Bayesian networks can introduce fresh challenges due to the large number of relationships they often model. In many domains, it is thus often essential to supplement any available data with elicited expert judgements. This in turn leads to two key challenges: the cognitive burden of these judgements is often very high, and there are a very large number of judgements required to obtain a full probability model.

title: In-Context Learning of Temporal Point Processes with Foundation Inference Models
creator: David Berghaus, Patrick Seifner, Kostadin Cvejoski, César Ojeda & Ramsés J. Sánchez, Lamarr Institute, Fraunhofer IAIS, University of Bonn, JetBrains Research, & University of Potsdam david.berghaus@iais.fraunhofer.de
description: Abstract Modeling event sequences of multiple event types with marked temporal point processes (MTPPs) provides a principled way to uncover governing dynamical rules and predict future events. Current neural network approaches to MTPP inference rely on training separate, specialized models for each target system.

title: Understanding the Nature of Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves
creator: A.J. Iovino, G.Perna, D. Perrone, D.Racco, A. Riotto
description: Abstract We offer a physical interpretation of the origin of the scalar-induced gravitational wave background, showing that it is mainly produced around the peaks of the scalar perturbations. We also provide a compact expression to estimate the amount of scalar-induced gravitational waves generated by peaks.

title: Attosecond electron bunch generation by an intense high-order harmonic pulse interacting with a thin target
creator: Yang He, Mamat Ali Bake, Cheng-Qi Zhang, Bai-Song Xie
description: Abstract Laser-accelerated electron bunches and the secondary radiation sources they produce exhibit unique temporal resolution for probing ultrafast physical processes due to their ultrashort pulse duration. The inherently short temporal profile of these pulses leads to extremely high peak bunch currents, thereby enabling a wide range of practical applications.

title: Accelerating Regression Tasks with Quantum Algorithms
creator: Chenghua Liu, Zhengfeng Ji
description: Abstract Regression is a cornerstone of statistics and machine learning, with applications spanning science, engineering, and economics. While quantum algorithms for regression have attracted considerable attention, most existing work has focused on linear regression, leaving many more complex yet practically important variants unexplored.

title: Relativistic Flux-Tube Model Predictions from Charmed Mesons to Double-Charmed Baryons
creator: Pooja Jakhad 1∗, Ajay Kumar Rai 1
description: Abstract Utilizing comprehensive experimental data on charmed mesons, we systematically investigate masses of the higher radial and orbital excitations of the D D and D s D_{s} meson families using the relativistic flux tube model. Our study employs mass splitting induced by spin-dependent interactions within the j–j coupling scheme.

title: VTPerception-R1: Enhancing Multimodal Reasoning via Explicit Visual and Textual Perceptual Grounding
creator: Yizhuo Ding, Mingkang Chen, Zhibang Feng, Tong Xiao, Wanying Qu, Wenqi Shao, Yanwei Fu
description: Abstract Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often struggle to ground reasoning in perceptual evidence. We present a systematic study of perception strategies—explicit, implicit, visual, and textual—across four multimodal benchmarks and two MLLMs. Our findings show that explicit perception, especially when paired with textual cues, consistently yields the best improvements, particularly for smaller models.

title: Comment on “Strong lensing and shadow of Ayon-Beato-Garcia (ABG) nonsingular black hole”
creator: M. Fahmi Fauzi
description: Abstract It was suggested by Ramadhan et al. (Eur Phys J C 83:465, 2023) that the Sagittarius A* black hole cannot be modeled by an Ayón-Beato-Garcìa regular black hole due to the incompatible shadow radius. However, they overlooked the distant-observer limit of the correction term in the effective geometry, which renders their calculation invalid.

title: SkyLink: Unifying Street-Satellite Geo-Localization via UAV-Mediated 3D Scene Alignment Conference: Proceedings of the 3rd International Workshop on UAVs in Multimedia: Capturing the World from a New Perspective; October 27–31, 2025; Dublin, Ireland. Proceedings of the 3rd International Workshop on
creator: Hongyang Zhang, Yinhao Liu, Zhenyu Kuang
description: Abstract . Cross-view geo-localization aims at establishing location correspondences between different viewpoints. Existing approaches typically learn cross-view correlations through direct feature similarity matching, often overlooking semantic degradation caused by extreme viewpoint disparities. To address this unique problem, we focus on robust feature retrieval under viewpoint variation and propose the novel SkyLink method.

title: A tree bijection for rigid quadrangulations
creator: Bart Zonneveld
description: Abstract We study the counting problem of rigid quadrangulations, recently introduced by Budd [ 8 ] and proven to be in bijection with colorful quadrangulations. The generating function for the latter has been derived in an algebraic manner by Bousquet-Mélou and Elvey Price [ 3 ] , which therefore also counts rigid quadrangulations.

title: Nowcasting and aggregation: Why small Euro area countries matter
creator: Andrii Babii
description: Abstract The paper studies the nowcasting of Euro area Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth using mixed data sampling machine learning panel data regressions with both standard macro releases and daily news data. Using a panel of 19 Euro area countries, we investigate whether directly nowcasting the Euro area aggregate is better than weighted individual country nowcasts.

title: Assessing the risk of future Dunkelflaute events for Germany using generative deep learning
creator: Felix M. Strnad, Jonathan Schmidt, Fabian Mockert, Philipp Hennig, Nicole Ludwig
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Felix M. Strnad, Jonathan Schmidt, Fabian Mockert, Philipp Hennig, Nicole Ludwig. The European electricity power grid is transitioning towards renewable energy sources, characterized by an increasing share of off- and onshore wind and solar power. However, the weather dependency of these energy sources poses a challenge to grid stability, with so-called Dunkelflaute events— periods of low wind and solar power generation—being of particular concern due to their potential to cause electricity supply shortages.

title: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Consistency in Automatically Generated Sewing Instructions
creator: Luisa Geiger, Mareike Hartmann, Michael Sullivan, Alexander Koller
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luisa Geiger, Mareike Hartmann, Michael Sullivan, Alexander Koller. In this paper, we propose a novel, automatic tree-based evaluation metric for LLM-generated step-by-step assembly instructions, that more accurately reflects spatiotemporal aspects of construction than traditional metrics such as BLEU and BERT similarity scores. We apply our proposed metric to the domain of sewing instructions, and show that our metric better correlates with manually-annotated error counts as well as human quality ratings, demonstrating our metric’s superiority for evaluating the spatiotemporal soundness of sewing instructions.

title: Quantifying Generalisation in Imitation Learning
creator: Nathan Gavenski, Odinaldo Rodrigues
description: Abstract Imitation learning benchmarks often lack sufficient variation between training and evaluation, limiting meaningful generalisation assessment. We introduce Labyrinth, a benchmarking environment designed to test generalisation with precise control over structure, start and goal positions, and task complexity. It enables verifiably distinct training, evaluation, and test settings.

title: RDD: Pareto Analysis of the Rate-Distortion-Distinguishability Trade-off
creator: Andriy Enttsel, Alex Marchioni, Andrea Zanellini, Mauro Mangia, Gianluca Setti, and Riccardo Rovatti
description: Abstract Extensive monitoring systems generate data that is usually compressed for network transmission. This compressed data might then be processed in the cloud for tasks such as anomaly detection. However, compression can potentially impair the detector’s ability to distinguish between regular and irregular patterns due to information loss.

title: Causal-Adapter: Taming Text-to-Image Diffusion for Faithful Counterfactual Generation
creator: Lei Tong, Zhihua Liu, Chaochao Lu, Dino Oglic, Tom Diethe, Philip Teare, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris, Chen Jin
description: Abstract We present Causal-Adapter, a modular framework that adapts frozen text-to-image diffusion backbones for counterfactual image generation. Our method enables causal interventions on target attributes, consistently propagating their effects to causal dependents without altering the core identity of the image.

title: TACO-Net: Topological Signatures Triumph in 3D Object Classification
creator: Anirban Ghosh, Ayan Dutta
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anirban Ghosh, Ayan Dutta. 3D object classification is a crucial problem due to its significant practical relevance in many fields, including computer vision, robotics, and autonomous driving. Although deep learning methods applied to point clouds sampled on CAD models of the objects and/or captured by LiDAR or RGBD cameras have achieved remarkable success in recent years, achieving high classification accuracy remains a challenging problem due to the unordered point clouds and their irregularity and noise.

title: Vision Function Layer in Multimodal LLMs
creator: Cheng Shi, Yizhou Yu, Sibei Yang
description: Abstract This study identifies that visual-related functional decoding is distributed across different decoder layers in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Typically, each function, such as counting, grounding, or OCR recognition, narrows down to two or three layers, which we define as Vision Function Layers (VFL).

title: Discrete flat disks: rigid quadrangulations
creator: Timothy Budd
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Timothy Budd. Inspired by a question of Ferrari in the physics context of JT gravity, we introduce and enumerate a combinatorial family of quadrangulations of the disk, called rigid quadrangulations . These form a subclass of the flat quadrangulations in the sense that every inner vertex has degree 4 4 , and therefore it can be viewed as a discrete model of flat metrics on the disk.

title: Fidel-TS: A High-Fidelity Benchmark for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
creator: Zhijian Xu, Wanxu Cai, Xilin Dai, Zhaorong Deng, Qiang Xu
description: Abstract The evaluation of time series forecasting models is hindered by a critical lack of high-quality benchmarks, leading to a potential illusion of progress. Existing datasets suffer from issues ranging from pre-training data contamination in the age of LLMs to the causal and description leakage prevalent in early multimodal designs.

title: Collision types and times in interacting particle systems
creator: Sergio Andraus, Nicole Hufnagel, Jacek Małecki
description: Abstract We consider a system of stochastic interacting particles with general diffusion coefficient and drift functions and we study the types of collisions that arise in them. In particular, interactions between particles are inversely proportional to their separation, and the coupling function of interaction is also considered in great generality.

title: Query Circuits: Explaining How Language Models Answer User Prompts
creator: Tung-Yu Wu, Fazl Barez
description: Abstract Explaining why a language model produces a particular output requires local, input-level explanations. Existing methods uncover global capability circuits (e.g., indirect object identification), but not why the model answers a specific input query in a particular way. We introduce query circuits , which directly trace the information flow inside a model that maps a specific input to the output.

title: A Bilevel Approach to Integrated Surgeon Scheduling and Surgery Planning solved via Branch-and-Price
creator: Broos Maenhout, Přemysl Šůcha, Viktorie Valdmanová, Ondřej Tkadlec, Jana Thao Rozlivková
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Broos Maenhout, Přemysl Šůcha, Viktorie Valdmanová, Ondřej Tkadlec, Jana Thao Rozlivková. In this paper, we study a multi-agent scheduling problem for organising the operations within the operating room department. The head of the surgeon group and individual surgeons are together responsible for the surgeon schedule and surgical case planning. The surgeon head allocates time blocks to individual surgeons, whereas individual surgeons determine the planning of surgical cases independently, which might degrade the schedule quality envisaged by the surgeon head.

title: A Greedy PDE Router for Blending Neural Operators and Classical Methods
creator: Sahana Rayan, Yash Patel, Ambuj Tewari
description: Abstract When solving PDEs, classical numerical solvers are often computationally expensive, while machine learning methods can suffer from spectral bias, failing to capture high-frequency components. Designing an optimal hybrid iterative solver–where, at each iteration, a solver is selected from an ensemble of solvers to leverage their complementary strengths–poses a challenging combinatorial problem.

title: OF-SemWat: High-Payload Text Embedding for Semantic Watermarking of AI-Generated Images with Arbitrary Size
creator: Benedetta Tondi, Andrea Costanzo, Mauro Barni
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Benedetta Tondi, Andrea Costanzo, Mauro Barni. We propose a high-payload image watermarking method for textual embedding, where a semantic description of the image - which may also correspond to the input text prompt-, is embedded inside the image.

title: The Quantum Decoding Problem : Tight Achievability Bounds and Application to Regev’s Reduction
creator: Agathe Blanvillain, André Chailloux, Jean-Pierre TillichInria de Paris, { \{ agathe.blanvillain,andre.chailloux,jean-pierre.tillich } \} @inria.fr
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Agathe Blanvillain, André Chailloux, Jean-Pierre TillichInria de Paris, { \{ agathe.blanvillain,andre.chailloux,jean-pierre.tillich } \} @inria.fr. We consider the quantum decoding problem. It consists in recovering a codeword given a superposition of noisy versions of this codeword. By measuring the superposition, we get back to the classical decoding problem. It appears for the first time in Chen, Liu and Zhandry’s work showing a quantum advantage for the Short Integer Solution (SIS) problem for the l ∞ l_{\infty} norm.

title: An Efficient Finite Element Method for Multi-dimensional Nonlocal Laplacian on Uniform Grids Thanks: † School of Mathematics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai, 200433, China. Email: ctsheng@sufe.edu.cn (C. Sheng). The work of this author is partially supported by the National N
creator: Changtao Sheng † , Huiyuan Li ‡ , Huifang Yuan ⋆ and Li-Lian Wang ¶
description: Abstract . Computing the stiffness matrix for the finite element discretization of the nonlocal Laplacian on unstructured meshes is difficult, because the operator is nonlocal and can even be singular. In this paper, we focus on the C 0 C^{0} -piecewise linear finite element method (FEM) for the nonlocal Laplacian on uniform grids within a d d -dimensional rectangular domain.

title: DiaCDM: Cognitive Diagnosis in Teacher-Student Dialogues using the Initiation-Response-Evaluation Framework
creator: Rui Jia 1,2 \sthanks Equal contribution, Yuang Wei 1,2∗ , Ruijia Li 1,2 , Yuang-Hao Jiang 1,2 , Xinyu Xie 1,2 , Yaomin Shen 3 , Min Zhang 1,2 \sthanks Corresponding authors \sthanks Project leader, Bo Jiang 1,2†
description: Abstract While cognitive diagnosis (CD) effectively assesses students’ knowledge mastery from structured test data, applying it to real-world teacher-student dialogues presents two fundamental challenges. Traditional CD models lack a suitable framework for handling dynamic, unstructured dialogues , and it’s difficult to accurately extract diagnostic semantics from lengthy dialogues . To overcome these hurdles, we propose DiaCDM, an innovative model.

title: Putnam-like dataset summary: LLMs as mathematical competition contestants
creator: Bartosz Bieganowski, Robert Skiba, Daniel Strzelecki, Mateusz Topolewski
description: Abstract . In this paper we summarize the results of the Putnam-like benchmark published by Google DeepMind. This dataset consists of 96 original problems in the spirit of the Putnam Competition and 576 solutions of LLMs. We analyse the performance of models on this set of problems to verify their ability to solve problems from mathematical contests. 1.

title: Rescue Operators’ Perspectives on KIRETT Wearable Technology: A Qualitative Study Thanks: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics (SMC) | 978-1-6654-1020-5/24/$31.00 ©2024 IEEE | DOI: 10.1109/SMC54092.2024.10831087
creator: Mubaris Nadeem, Johannes Zenkert, Lisa Bender, Christian Weber, Madjid Fathi
description: Abstract In emergencies, treatment needs to be fast, accurate and patient-specific. For instance, in emergency scenarios, obstacles like treatment environments and medical difficulties can lead to bad outcomes for patients. Additionally, a drastic change of health vitals can force paramedics to shift to a different treatment in the ongoing treatment of the patient in order to save a patient’s life.

title: Snakelike trajectories of electrons released from quantum dots driven by the spin Hall effect
creator: B. Szafran, P. Wójcik
description: Abstract Using time-dependent simulations, we analyze the trajectories of electrons released from a quantum dot in a waveguide made of a spin-orbit-coupled material (InSb). An electron released from the quantum dot, when driven by an electric field follows a trajectory that is deflected by spin-orbit interaction and undergoes spin precession that results in a spin-dependent, snake-like trajectory.

title: Turbulence and dust fragility in protoplanetary discs 2025 Turbulence and dust fragility in protoplanetary discs – 15
creator: Simin Tong, Richard Alexander, Giovanni Rosotti
description: Abstract Dust growth from micron- to planet-size in protoplanetary discs involves multiple physical processes, including dust growth and fragmentation, the streaming instability, and pebble accretion. Disc turbulence and dust fragility matter at almost every stage. Previous studies typically vary one of them while fixing the other, failing to provide a complete picture.

title: The development of a high granular crystal calorimeter prototype of VLAST
creator: Yan-shuo Zhang, Qian Chen, Deng-yi Chen, Jian-guo Liu, Yi-ming Hu, Yun-long Zhang, Yi-feng Wei, Zhong-tao Shen, Chang-qing Feng, Jian-hua Guo, Shu-bin Liu, Guang-shun Huang, Xiao-lian Wang, Zi-zong Xu
description: Abstract Very Large Area gamma-ray Space Telescope (VLAST) is the next-generation flagship space observatory for high-energy gamma-ray detection proposed by China. The observation energy range covers from MeV to TeV and beyond, with acceptance of 10 m 2 sr. The calorimeter serves as a crucial subdetector of VLAST, responsible for high-precision energy measurement and electron/proton discrimination.

title: Cell2Text: Multimodal LLM for Generating Single-Cell Descriptions from RNA-Seq Data
creator: Oussama Kharouiche, Aris Markogiannakis, Xiao Fei, Michail Chatzianastasis, Michalis Vazirgiannis
description: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed biology by enabling the measurement of gene expression at cellular resolution, providing information for cell types, states, and disease contexts. Recently, single-cell foundation models have emerged as powerful tools for learning transferable representations directly from expression profiles, improving performance on classification and clustering tasks.

title: Adaptive Pseudo-Marginal Algorithm
creator: Sarra Abaoubida, Mylène Bédard, Florian Maire
description: Abstract The Pseudo-Marginal (PM) algorithm is a popular Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method used to sample from a target distribution when its density is inaccessible, but can be estimated with a non-negative unbiased estimator. Its performance depends on a key parameter, N , the number of iterations (or particles) used to approximate the target density.

title: Continuous differentiability of the signum function and Newton’s method for bang-bang control
creator: Daniel Wachsmuth, Gerd Wachsmuth
description: Abstract We investigate bang-bang control problems and the possibility to apply Newton’s method to solve such kind of problems numerically. To this end, we show that the signum function is Fréchet differentiable between appropriate function spaces. Numerical experiments show the applicability of the resulting method.

title: The Free Option Problem of ePBS
creator: Bruno Mazorra, Burak Öz, Christoph Schlegel, Fei Wu
description: Abstract Ethereum’s upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade introduces EIP-7732 enshrined Proposer–Builder Separation (ePBS) which improves the block production pipeline by addressing trust and scalability challenges. Yet it also creates a new liveness risk: builders gain a short-dated “free” option to prevent the execution payload they committed to from becoming canonical, without incurring an additional penalty.
